Shared across components via Context<T> — see AppContexts.QueryCache. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Remarks Threading. All public methods are safe to call from any thread. Slots are protected by a per-key lock; QueryCache.EntryChanged fires either inline or on the configured QueryCache.DispatcherPost callback (set by ReactorHost at bootstrap). Tests can leave it null to observe events inline. Eviction. A single shared timer (started lazily on first subscription) polls all slots every QueryCache.EvictionPollInterval. Slots whose SubscriberCount == 0 for longer than their CacheTime are evicted. Using one timer keeps the entry count's impact on system timers O(1). Constructors QueryCache Properties Count Snapshot the current cache size. Diagnostic only — do not use for correctness. DispatcherPost Injected marshaller for QueryCache.EntryChanged. Null → fires inline. EvictionPollInterval How often the eviction timer checks every slot for expiry. Default 1s. UtcNow Clock override for deterministic tests. Methods Clear Removes every entry. Subscribers are retained. Fires QueryCache.EntryChanged once per key that actually held a value. Dispose Releases the resources that this object holds. EvictNow Test / diagnostic hook: drive the eviction sweep explicitly rather than waiting for the background QueryCache.EvictionPollInterval timer. Returns the set of keys that were evicted on this pass. Safe to call from any thread. Remarks Production code should not need this — subscribers keep entries alive and the shared timer evicts zero-subscriber entries past their CacheTime. It's exposed publicly so framerate / stress tests can make eviction deterministic. Invalidate Removes the entry (if any) for key. Subscribers are retained — the next QueryCache.Set will see their count. Fires QueryCache.EntryChanged if there was an entry to remove. O(n) in the number of cached keys — document the pattern prefix carefully if you store a lot of unrelated keys under one cache. content: Why a runtime flag at all. Interceptors are baked in at compile time, so without a runtime gate every Debug build would pay the stamping cost whether or not anyone is inspecting. This flag is what the emitted interceptor checks before writing a location, so an un-inspected Debug session allocates nothing extra. It does not change control tagging for leaves. The reconciler attaches a ReactorState (the control → element back-pointer) only to controls that something will read back — callbacks, a key, extras, or reference modifiers (see Reconciler.NeedsTag), which is the allocation win PR #468 landed. NeedsTag has no arm for this flag on ordinary elements: a stamped element carries its CallSite in the Extensions bucket and so already satisfies the existing Extensions is not null test. Adding one would only tag unstamped elements, which have no location to return, while re-introducing the per-leaf allocation. Elements the generator does not reach (wrapper factories, bare-string children) therefore stay untagged and report no location rather than a wrong one. The one exception is component boundaries: while this flag is on, every component's Border wrapper is tagged so an inspector can find where each component starts — one allocation per component, never per leaf. Who turns it on. The devtools session switch. ReactorApp sets ReactorSourceMap.Enabled when the process was launched with --devtools app / --devtools run, so a retail session never pays. It is public-settable so a host that embeds its own inspector (or a test) can opt in without going through the CLI. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Diagnostics. Learn more: Diagnostics Properties Enabled True when source mapping is active for this process. Read by every generated factory interceptor before it stamps, so it is an int + Volatile rather than a lock. Methods GetSource Resolves the DSL call site that produced control. This is the whole read chain, and it deliberately reuses the back-pointer that already exists rather than adding a second attached property: UIElement → ReactorAttached.StateProperty → ReactorState.Element → Element.CallSite. Returns null when the control was not produced by Reactor, or when the element behind it carries no Element.CallSite — because it was built while ReactorSourceMap.Enabled was false, or because no provider reaches that factory (see the known limitations in the source-mapping guide). Note this is a property of the ELEMENT, not of tagging: a control can be tagged for unrelated reasons (callbacks, a key, other extras) and still report no location, and an element hand-stamped with a CallSite reports one even with the flag off. Target-wrapping decorators are resolved through. Flyout, MenuFlyout and CommandBarFlyout mount their Target's control and then deliberately replace that control's tag with themselves, because their Opened/Closed handlers read it back. The realized control is still the target's — a Button inside a Flyout(...) was created by the Button( line — so reporting the decorator's line would name the wrong creator, the same misattribution the generator avoids for pass-through factories. The walk is a loop so nested decorators resolve to the innermost target. Native AOT in diagnostics mode does not tag a control whose element's only extra is its call site (no managed inspector can load to read the tag); there the location is resolved from the control's published ReactorSource value and is the same SourceLocation the tag would give. Menu and command-bar items a flyout, menu bar or command bar builds from item records (MenuItem(…), AppBarButton(…)) carry no element tag; in diagnostics mode their location is resolved the same way, from their published value. Parameters Name Type Description control UIElement

content: Without this, a thin forwarding helper collapses every one of its call sites onto a single line, because an interceptor replaces the call site and the call site of TextBlock(...) in static Element MyHeader() => TextBlock("header"); is inside MyHeader. Annotating MyHeader flips the attribution outward: the source-map generator emits no interceptor for the factory calls in its body, and instead intercepts calls to MyHeader and stamps the caller's line. Deliberately opt-in. It is not a blanket rule for helpers, because for most element-returning methods the body line is the RIGHT answer — a Component.Render() body is where the author actually wrote the UI, and deferring it to the reconciler's call site would be a regression. Only a thin forwarder, whose own line carries no information a reader wants, benefits. This attribute is how that intent is expressed. Nesting. Annotated methods compose: a transparent helper calling another transparent helper keeps deferring outward until it reaches a caller that is not annotated, and that caller's line is what gets stamped. [ReactorSourceTransparent] internal static Element Field(string label, string value) => HStack(TextBlock(label), TextBlock(value)); // Both rows report THEIR OWN line, instead of both reporting the // `HStack(` line inside Field. var form = VStack( Field("Name", name), Field("Email", email)); Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Diagnostics. Inherits from Attribute. Learn more: Diagnostics Remarks Requirements. The generator has to be able to emit an interceptor that forwards to the annotated method, so it must be static, return an Element, and be reachable by name from a generated file in the same compilation — i.e. public or internal (never private), not declared in a file-local or generic type, and not a local function (C# interceptors cannot intercept those). An annotation the generator cannot honour is reported as REACTOR_SOURCEMAP_001 rather than silently doing nothing, and attribution falls back to today's behaviour — the helper's own line — so a bad annotation never makes attribution worse than no annotation. Where it takes effect. Rule 1 (suppressing stamps inside the body) applies in the compilation that declares the method; rule 2 (stamping at the call site) applies in the compilation that calls it. Both need the source-map generator loaded, so annotating a method in a library whose consumer has not enabled ReactorSourceMap simply leaves those elements unstamped. A plain marker attribute with no members and no reflection surface, so it is trim- and AOT-safe. It is read by the generator from metadata, which is why it must be public. Constructors ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute
description: Spec 010 — marks a helper method as source-transparent: elements it returns are attributed to the line that CALLED it, not to the line inside it that ran the DSL factory.
title: ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute

content: In-process subscription helper for the Microsoft-UI-Reactor EventSource. Lets an app developer (or an internal devtools surface — reactor.logs MCP, an ILogger bridge) observe framework events without writing an EventListener subclass. This is deliberately not a file-capture API. The .NET runtime already provides three: DOTNET_EnableEventPipe + DOTNET_EventPipeOutputPath environment variables (zero app code). dotnet-trace collect --providers Microsoft-UI-Reactor. Visual Studio Performance Profiler → Events Viewer. See docs/guide/diagnostics.md for end-to-end examples. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Diagnostics. Learn more: Diagnostics Methods GetComponentControl Resolves the componentId carried by a ComponentRendered event (Microsoft-UI-Reactor EventId 40) to the realized control whose bounds are that component's — the component's wrapper, or for a host's root component the host's current root content control. Use it to flash the region that just re-rendered ("highlight updates"). Returns null for 0, for an id this process never issued, once the component has unmounted or its control was collected, and while the control does not exist yet: a component's mount event is raised before its subtree mounts (the id is mapped once that finishes), and a root's first event before its reconcile pass has produced the content. An id from a render whose subtree was then discarded — caught by an ErrorBoundary, or a failure that propagated — may never resolve. So resolve after the pass completes (e.g. on the next dispatcher tick) rather than inside the event callback, and treat null as "nothing on screen for this id". Ids are only issued, and controls only recorded, while the event is enabled, so subscribe first. Call on the UI thread; the returned control is a live WinUI object. Parameters Name Type Description componentId long The event's componentId payload field. Subscribe Subscribes to Microsoft-UI-Reactor events in-process. Returns an IDisposable token; dispose it to detach. The callback fires on the emission thread — typically the UI dispatcher when an event originates from reconcile / render, or a thread-pool thread otherwise. Keep the callback work minimal and never let it throw across the framework boundary — a throwing subscriber propagates into EventSource's emit path and surfaces as an ETW failure. Multiple concurrent subscribers are supported. Each subscriber's level and keywords are independently active until the returned token is disposed; the runtime unions them when computing whether IsEnabled on the event source returns true. Be aware that a broad subscriber (EventLevel.Verbose + all keywords) raises the cost of every hot-path call site on the framework for as long as it lives. For writing a trace file, use one of: DOTNET_EnableEventPipe / DOTNET_EventPipeOutputPath env vars. dotnet-trace collect --providers Microsoft-UI-Reactor. Visual Studio Performance Profiler → Events Viewer. Parameters Name Type Default Description onEvent Action<ReactorEvent> Callback invoked once per matching event. Must be non-null. level EventLevel (EventLevel)5 Minimum severity to forward. Defaults to EventLevel.Verbose so subscribers see everything (state changes, per-trampoline dispatches) unless they explicitly pass a stricter level. keywords EventKeywords (EventKeywords)-1 Keyword mask to forward. Defaults to all keywords ((EventKeywords)(-1)). Returns: Disposable token. Disposing detaches the underlying EventListener; subsequent events do not reach onEvent. Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentNullException If onEvent is null. TryGetComponentId The reverse of ReactorTrace.GetComponentControl: the componentId that ComponentRendered events use for the component rendering into control (a component's wrapper control). Lets an inspector filter the event stream down to the component a user selected. Returns false when control is not a component wrapper, or when that component has not rendered since ComponentRendered was enabled. A host's root id is never returned here — the root content control is often also a child component's wrapper, and that child keeps the mapping. Call on the UI thread: the id is read from the control's Reactor state. Parameters Name Type Description control UIElement componentId long Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentNullException If control is null.
title: ReactorTrace

ReactorDiagnostics Process-wide diagnostic collector for structural problems the reconciler can detect at runtime (today: keyed-list bailouts). Read-only surface for agents, tests, and the in-app dev overlay; the producer side is internal. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.Diagnostics. Remarks The collector deduplicates by (control instance, kind, hashed sample keys). The first occurrence is logged in full; subsequent occurrences of the same triple bump a counter rather than appending a fresh entry. This matches the spec 042 §9 Q1 resolution ("warn-and-bailout via a one-shot diagnostic") and avoids drowning the dev overlay during a run-away render loop. The buffer is bounded to ReactorDiagnostics.MaxRecentEntries; once full, the oldest entry is dropped. This is intentionally generous — keyed-list bailouts are a per-app rarity, not a per-frame event. Reads are lock-free against a snapshot; writes take a short lock. Properties IsSourcePublishingEnabled True when Reactor is publishing ReactorDiagnostics.SourceProperty in this process: the Reactor.DevtoolsSupport build switch is on and the process was started with REACTOR_DIAGNOSTICS=1. RecentKeyedListWarnings Recent keyed-list key diagnostics (see KeyedListDiagnostic), newest first. Returns an independent snapshot — safe to enumerate while producers continue running. Empty when no key problem has ever been found (the common case). SourceProperty Attached string property, registered as "ReactorSource", that Reactor sets on every control it realizes while diagnostics publishing is on. Its value describes where the control came from — call site, owning component, element kind, key, declared name, and for component boundaries the component's hooks — in the v1 grammar: with % escaped as %25 and | as %7C in values. at is never an absolute developer path: it is relative to the project directory, or to the solution/repo root (rel=root), or just the file name (rel=0) — the same posture as XAML's runtime source info, which reports ms-appx:/// paths. Why a string on the control. An out-of-process inspector reads it through XamlDiagnostics like any other property (it is reported as .ReactorSource), with no managed code in the app — so it works for Native AOT apps, where no managed inspector agent can be loaded. When it is set. Only when the app was built with the Reactor.DevtoolsSupport switch on AND launched with REACTOR_DIAGNOSTICS=1; see ReactorDiagnostics.IsSourcePublishingEnabled. Otherwise no control carries it and the publishing code is trimmed from AOT/trimmed builds. Reading this property registers the attached property (once) but publishes nothing. Methods ClearRecentKeyedListWarnings Drop every captured entry and contextual dedup state, retaining per-control counts. Tests use this between scenarios; production code never needs to call it. DescribeComponent Describes the component hosted at element: a component's wrapper Border (every class, function and memo component is mounted into one), or a host's root content (its rendered root control, the window content or ContentTarget it was installed into, or a ReactorHostControl itself). Returns null for any other element. Works with or without source mapping. Parameters Name Type Description element UIElement Remarks Must be called on the UI thread. One element can anchor two components: when a root renders a component directly (Render() => Component<Shell>()), the root's rendered control is Shell's wrapper. The wrapper wins — the element describes Shell, the innermost component it hosts — and ReactorDiagnostics.TrySetState / ReactorDiagnostics.Rerender address the same component. The root stays reachable through its other anchors: a ContentTarget, a ReactorHostControl, or the dev-overlay wrapper. A host that installs straight into Window.Content has none of those, so in that one shape its root is not reachable. GetAppliedProperties The WinUI properties Reactor writes on control from the common modifiers of the element that produced it, so an inspector can mark a property as set in C# (and overwritten when the element's value changes). Empty when the control is not tagged with its element — Reactor tags only controls something reads back (callbacks, a key, or a stamped source location), so turn on ReactorSourceMap.Enabled for full coverage. Parameters Name Type Description control UIElement Remarks Covers ElementModifiers and AccessibilityModifiers, plus the AutomationProperties.Name Reactor derives from a captioned control (Button("Save"), CheckBox("Agree"), …) when the author sets none. That one is reported as "DefaultAutomationName", and only while the live name still equals it; a different live name was written by the app. Properties a control's own element record sets (TextBlock("hi") → Text) are not listed. Must be called on the UI thread. GetHosts Snapshot of every live Reactor host in the process, in creation order: windows opened through ReactorApp (including ones not yet mounted), hosts created with new ReactorHost(window), and ReactorHostControl islands. Disposed hosts are excluded. Safe to call from any thread; see ReactorHostInfo for consistency rules. Remarks Provisional diagnostics API for external inspectors. A ReactorHostControl that was removed from the tree but never disposed stays listed until it is collected — Reactor cannot tell a transient reparent from a removal (issue #344); check its XamlRoot to skip detached islands. GetReferenceEdges The references control declares to other controls — including pending ones whose target has not mounted yet, for which the WinUI property itself (e.g. XYFocusRight, AutomationProperties.LabeledBy) still reads null. Grouped by property in a fixed order (control-descriptor references, then bindings, then the modifier references), then list position; both LabeledBy forms are adjacent, the ElementRef one first. Parameters Name Type Description control UIElement Remarks ElementRef references (modifiers such as .LabeledBy(ref) or .XYFocusRight(ref), control descriptors and bindings) are always reported. An AutomationId .LabeledBy("id") is reported while pending; once resolved it is reported only while the control is loaded and tagged with its element (turn source mapping on). Reads existing reconciler state on demand. Must be called on the UI thread. GetSource Reads ReactorDiagnostics.SourceProperty from element; null when unset. Parameters Name Type Description element DependencyObject Rerender Schedules a re-render of the component hosted at element, bypassing its memoization (the path a state setter takes). Parameters Name Type Description element UIElement Returns: False when no component is hosted at element or it has never rendered. Remarks A re-render diffs the new element tree against the previous one, so it re-applies a property only when the element's value for it changed: it does not restore a property that was edited directly on the control while the element's value stayed the same. Must be called on the UI thread that renders the component. TrySetState Development-time state edit: parses text to the value type of hook hookIndex of the component hosted at element, writes it, and — when the value changed — schedules a re-render exactly as the hook's own setter would. Parameters Name Type Description element UIElement A component wrapper or host root, as for ReactorDiagnostics.DescribeComponent. hookIndex int The hook's DiagnosticValue.Index. text string Invariant-culture text: a number, a single character, true/false, an enum member name, a date, time span or GUID, or the string itself (unquoted). null sets a string or nullable to null. error string? Why the edit was refused, when this returns false. Returns: True when the value was written (including when it was already equal). Remarks Only state, reducer and persisted hooks of a text-typed value can be set. Must be called on the UI thread that renders the component. Fields MaxRecentEntries Maximum number of distinct (control, kind, sample-set) entries retained. New entries beyond this drop the oldest. MaxSampleKeys Maximum number of representative keys captured per entry. Larger duplicate sets are truncated and an ellipsis is appended. ReactorHostInfo Point-in-time description of one live Reactor host: where it renders, what its root is, and where that root was mounted. Returned by ReactorDiagnostics.GetHosts. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.Diagnostics. Remarks Provisional diagnostics API for external inspectors (for example winapp devtools); shape may change while Reactor is in preview. Deliberately exposes no reconciler internals: the root is described by name and call site, and reached on screen through ReactorHostInfo.RootControl — the same WinUI control an inspector already walks. Everything else is an existing public WinUI or Reactor hosting type. A snapshot, not a live view: re-query after a render, window open, or close. The snapshot itself can be taken from any thread, and every value in it is read atomically (never half of one mount and half of another). A snapshot taken while the UI thread is remounting may still pair the outgoing root's name with the incoming root's site; take it on the UI thread when the values must agree with each other or with the visual tree you are about to walk. Touching the returned WinUI objects is subject to their usual UI-thread rules. Holding a snapshot keeps its host, window and root control alive; the registry behind ReactorDiagnostics.GetHosts does not. Properties Host The window host, when ReactorHostInfo.Kind is ReactorHostKind.WindowHost. HostControl The embedded host control, when ReactorHostInfo.Kind is ReactorHostKind.HostControl. HostElement The element whose content is the Reactor root: the ReactorHostControl itself, a window host's ReactorHost.ContentTarget, or null when a window host renders straight into Window.Content. Kind Which host shape this is. MountSite Where the root was mounted — the ReactorApp.Run, ReactorApp.OpenWindow, ReactorWindow.Mount, ReactorHost.Mount or ReactorHostControl.Mount call in app code. Null unless the calling project was built with source mapping (ReactorSourceMap=true, the Debug default) and ReactorSourceMap.Enabled was true at mount time; also null for a root created from ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory or ReactorHostControl.ComponentType, or mounted by framework code, none of which has a call site in app code. ReactorWindow The ReactorApp window that owns the host (its Id, Key and NativeWindow identify it), or null for a host constructed directly on a window and for every ReactorHostKind.HostControl. RootComponentName The root component's type name, namespace-qualified, with nested types joined by . and generic arguments spelled out (MyApp.Pages.Dashboard, MyApp.ListPage<MyApp.Order>). Null for a render-function root and before the first mount. RootControl The control the root currently renders as, or null before the first render. This is the control the host places in Window.Content / its content slot; when a dev overlay is on, that slot holds an overlay wrapper and this control is its child. After a render error it is the error fallback panel. RootRenderFunctionName A readable name for a render-function root: the method that declares it, with compiler-generated names undone — MyApp.Program.Main (lambda), MyApp.Program.Main.Render for a local function, MyApp.Shell.Render for a method group. Null for a component root, before the first mount, and when the runtime cannot describe the delegate (for example NativeAOT with stack-trace data disabled). For a lambda, ReactorHostInfo.MountSite is usually the better identity. Window The WinUI window a ReactorHostKind.WindowHost renders into. Null for ReactorHostKind.HostControl, which does not own a window; use ReactorHostInfo.HostElement's XamlRoot to place it. ReactorHostKind Which kind of Reactor host a ReactorHostInfo describes. content: Every control in Reactor is described by an element record. Factory methods create them and modifiers return changed copies. The reconciler turns them into real WinUI controls. Buttons Buttons, toggle buttons, split buttons and hyperlink buttons. Input Text boxes, check boxes, combo boxes, sliders, pickers and other input controls. Menus and commands Menus, menu bars, command bars and keyboard accelerators. Dialogs and flyouts Content dialogs, flyouts, popups and teaching tips. Media and icons Images, icons, animated visuals, media playback and person pictures. Shapes Rectangles, ellipses, lines, paths and brushes. Status and info Info bars, badges and progress indicators. content: Element records are immutable descriptions of a control. You usually create them with a factory method and change them with modifiers. Learn more: Controls, Commanding ButtonElement The element record that describes a WinUI Button control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: Button Modifiers: AccentButton, Click, Command, DisabledFocusable, IsDisabledFocusable, Set, SubtleButton, TextLink Property Type Default Description Command Command? The ButtonElement.Command bound to this button via the Button(Command) factory, the .Command() modifier, or a direct new ButtonElement(cmd.Label) { Command = cmd } / with { Command = cmd } record-init (issue #153, made fully uniform in issue #637). Carries the command so the reconciler can compare it field-aware in Element.ShallowEquals and apply its metadata + enabled state through a descriptor entry — no per-render ButtonElement.Setters lambda. Every binding path is now equivalent: dispatch (Execute/ExecuteAsync) is invoked by the click trampoline when ButtonElement.OnClick is null, Command.IsEnabled is folded into the IsEnabled descriptor entry (see ButtonElement.EffectiveIsEnabled), and the command counts as a callback source for ButtonElement.HasCallbacks. The init accessor is public: a bare record-init invokes the command on click exactly like the factory/modifier. ContentElement Element? IsDisabledFocusable bool When true, the button is visually dimmed and its OnClick handler is suppressed, but it stays keyboard-focusable and reachable via Tab. Use for submit buttons gated on validation so users can discover them and the disable state doesn't trap keyboard navigation through commit- on-blur inputs. Conceptually equivalent to Fluent UI React's disabledFocusable / ARIA's aria-disabled. Like React's ErrorBoundary — catches errors during rendering, not event handlers. When the ErrorBoundary re-renders, it retries the child (error recovery). Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Created by: RenderEachTime Property Type Description RenderFunc Func<RenderContext, Element> GroupElement A transparent grouping element (like React's Fragment). Does not introduce any layout container — its children are flattened into the parent. Produced by ForEach and Group() in the DSL. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Property Type Description Children Element[] KeyedMemoElement Issue #327 — an opt-in, typed keyed memo wrapper produced by the Memo(key, factory) factory (see Factories). The author asserts KeyedMemoElement.Factory is a pure function of KeyedMemoElement.MemoKey: when a virtualized ElementFactory<T> recycles a container and asks for the same key again, the factory-scoped LRU returns the previously-built inner Element instance unchanged instead of rebuilding+diffing the subtree. Returning the same instance lets Element.ShallowEquals hit its ReferenceEquals fast-path so the per-row reconcile descent is skipped entirely. Purity contract. The key must capture every input the factory reads. Closing over unkeyed mutable state (a UseState cell, an external counter, the theme) without folding it into the key will serve stale content — that is the author's responsibility. Widen the key to a tuple (e.g. Memo((item.Id, isSelected), …)) to capture extra inputs. KeyedMemoElement.MemoKey is compared with Object.Equals / Object.GetHashCode, so value keys (ints, strings, records, value tuples) dedupe by value — this is what makes the int-index VirtualList path hit the cache where the reference-identity _viewBuilderCache cannot. Used outside a virtualized factory (e.g. a plain VStack child), the reconciler treats it as a transparent, keyed wrapper: a re-render with the same KeyedMemoElement.MemoKey is a no-op (by the purity contract the factory output is identical to the mounted inner, so there is nothing to diff), and a CHANGED key replaces the inner (unmount + fresh mount of the new KeyedMemoElement.Factory output). The old factory is never re-invoked at update time, so it is always safe to drop a Memo(key, …) anywhere a normal element is expected. The one exception to the no-op: when a component inside the mounted subtree updates its own state, the reconciler runs the current KeyedMemoElement.Factory again and walks that output against itself to reach the component, so the update renders. The cross-recycle cache benefit only applies on the ElementFactory<T> recycle path. The positional parameter is named MemoKey (not Key) so it does not clash with the inherited Element.Key string used for keyed reconciliation. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. content: Element records are immutable descriptions of a control. You usually create them with a factory method and change them with modifiers. Learn more: Dialogs and Flyouts ContentDialogElement Declarative content dialog. Set IsOpen to true to show, false to close; content is reconciled live while the dialog is open. OnClosed reports how the dialog was dismissed — the button the user chose, or ContentDialogResult.None for a declared IsOpen = false. It does not fire when the dialog is torn down because its owner unmounted or its host/reconciler was disposed. Disposal also cancels deferred opens without OnOpened. State reset needed during teardown belongs in effect cleanup, not OnClosed. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Content Element DefaultButton ContentDialogButton IsOpen bool IsPrimaryButtonEnabled bool Enables/disables the primary button while the dialog is open. Defaults to true. IsSecondaryButtonEnabled bool Enables/disables the secondary button while the dialog is open. Defaults to true. OnClosed Action<ContentDialogResult>? OnOpened Action? Raised after the dialog finishes opening. PrimaryButtonText string "OK" SecondaryButtonText string? Title string ContentFlyoutElement Describes a content flyout (used as a slot value on buttons or as a modifier attachment). NOT independently mountable — the reconciler recognizes it in flyout slots. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: ContentFlyout Property Type Description Content Element Placement FlyoutPlacementMode Preferred position of the flyout relative to its target. Defaults to FlyoutPlacementMode.Auto, which means "no opinion — let WinUI decide": Reactor clears FlyoutBase.Placement so it falls back to the control's own default (FlyoutPlacementMode.Top) instead of writing Auto, because WinUI's show-time validator rejects Auto and terminates the process. Changing an already-mounted flyout from an explicit placement back to FlyoutPlacementMode.Auto therefore returns it to that default, rather than leaving a stale local value that would outrank a Style setter. FlyoutElement A flyout attached to another element. Wrap the target element. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: Flyout Modifiers: AreOpenCloseAnimationsEnabled, Closed, Opened, OverlayInputPassThroughElement, Set, ShowMode Property Type Description AreOpenCloseAnimationsEnabled bool Whether the flyout animates on open/close. Defaults to true. FlyoutContent Element IsOpen bool Opens the flyout declaratively. A one-shot trigger: the flyout is shown on mount when already true, and on the false → true edge of an update, against any target (a Button/SplitButton target holds the flyout in its own Flyout slot, any other target as FlyoutBase.AttachedFlyout). Setting it back to false does not close the flyout — the user dismisses it. Reset your state from FlyoutElement.OnClosed so the next true is a fresh edge. OnClosed Action? OnOpened Action? OverlayInputPassThroughElement Element? Element whose input is passed through the light-dismiss overlay (lets the user interact with one element behind the flyout). Placement FlyoutPlacementMode Preferred position of the flyout relative to its target. Defaults to FlyoutPlacementMode.Auto, which means "no opinion — let WinUI decide": Reactor clears FlyoutBase.Placement so it falls back to the control's own default (FlyoutPlacementMode.Top) instead of writing Auto, because WinUI's show-time validator rejects Auto and terminates the process. Changing an already-mounted flyout from an explicit placement back to FlyoutPlacementMode.Auto therefore returns it to that default, rather than leaving a stale local value that would outrank a Style setter. Created by: Popup Modifiers: Closed, IsLightDismissEnabled, LightDismiss, Offset, Opened, Set Property Type Description Child Element HorizontalOffset double IsLightDismissEnabled bool IsOpen bool OnClosed Action? OnOpened Action? VerticalOffset double TeachingTipElement The element record that describes a WinUI TeachingTip control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: TeachingTip Modifiers: ActionButtonClick, Closed, HeroContent, IconSource, PlacementMargin, PreferredPlacement, Set, Target Property Type Default Description ActionButtonContent string? CloseButtonContent string? Content Element? HeroContent Element? Optional "hero" Element (image / banner) rendered above the title. IconSource IconData? Custom icon source rendered in the tip's leading slot. IsOpen bool Whether the tip is shown. Defaults to false — drive it from state. Edge-triggered. This declares a transition, not a mirror: after the initial render Reactor writes the control only when the declared value changes. A light dismiss or the tip's own close button sets IsOpen to false on the control without touching the declared value, so re-rendering the same declared true will not re-open it. Wire TeachingTipElement.OnClosed back into the state that drives this property; a later false → true transition then re-opens the tip. Mount is the one exception (issue #949): a first render that declares true does open the tip. WinUI drops a pending open if the tip is written again while it is still unparented, and Reactor configures controls before parenting them, so the mount-time open is deferred until the control is loaded. One consequence worth knowing: because that write lands after the setter pass, a .Set(t => t.IsOpen = false) cannot override a declared mount-time true the way setters normally win. Declare the value instead of reaching for .Set — this property is the supported channel for it. OnActionButtonClick Action? OnClosed Action? content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Learn more: Reconciliation Constructors Element Properties AnimationConfig Compositor property animation configuration (.Animate() modifier). When set, the reconciler creates ImplicitAnimationCollection entries on the element's Visual for Opacity/Scale/Rotation/Offset/CenterPoint. Attached Attached properties from parent containers (Grid.Row, Canvas.Left, etc.). Set via fluent extension methods: TextBlock("hi").Grid(row: 1, column: 2) Stored as a type-keyed dictionary so each provider defines its own data record. CallSite Spec 010 — the C# source location that created this element, or null when nothing stamped it. This is a property of the ELEMENT, not of the current flag state. An element stamped while mapping was on keeps its location after the flag is turned off, and a hand-assigned value is honoured regardless of the flag; conversely an element built while mapping was off, or produced by a factory the provider does not reach, stays null forever. Elements are immutable, so this is fixed at construction. NOTE ON THE NAME: spec 010 proposes Element.Source. That name is unusable — five existing element records already declare a positional Source member of an incompatible type (ImageElement(string Source), WebView2Element(Uri? Source), MediaPlayerElementElement(string? Source), plus AnimatedIconElement and ParallaxViewElement), and a base property of a different type makes their positional parameters fail to bind (CS8866). CallSite is the collision-free equivalent. The slot is present in every build configuration (the library ships as a Release-built NuGet package, so a #if DEBUG gate would make the property invisible to consumers). The cost is what is gated: nothing writes this slot unless a source-map provider is wired into the consuming compilation, and the generated interceptors check ReactorSourceMap.Enabled before stamping. Tagging is NOT keyed on that runtime flag. A stamped element carries this value in its Element.Extensions bucket, and Reconciler.NeedsTag already tags anything with a non-null bucket — so the back-pointer follows the stamp, not the flag. A hand-assigned CallSite is therefore tagged and readable even with the flag off (see the HandStampedLeafIsTaggedWithFlagOff selftest), and an element the provider never reached stays untagged and reports no location rather than a wrong one. Populated per call site, so it is a compile-time constant for a given DSL invocation and survives fluent modifier chains automatically (record with copies it). It is deliberately NOT consulted by Element.ShallowEquals — see the reconciler's allow-list. STORAGE: this is a shim over the spec 047 §4.4 Element.Extensions bucket, exactly like Element.Attached and Element.ThemeBindings. Declaring it inline on the record instead costs +24 bytes on every element ever allocated, measured, in every build — a permanent retail tax for a debug-only feature. The public shape is identical either way, so this is a storage decision, not an API one. ConnectedAnimationKey Connected animation key for cross-container transitions. When set, the reconciler automatically captures a visual snapshot on unmount (via ConnectedAnimationService.PrepareToAnimate) and starts the animation on mount if a prepared animation with the same key exists. Set via fluent extension method: Border(child).ConnectedAnimation("hero") ContextValues Context values provided to this element's subtree via .Provide(). The reconciler pushes these onto the context scope when entering this element's subtree and pops them when leaving. ElementTransition Element enter/exit transition configuration (.Transition() modifier). When set, the reconciler animates mount (enter) and unmount (exit) with compositor animations, deferring removal until exit animation completes. Extensions Cross-cutting extras (attached properties, transitions, theme bindings, animation configs, resource overrides, context values) bucketed into a lazy sub-record (spec 047 §4.4). The common case — a leaf with none of these — leaves this slot null, so the 14 fields below cost one reference instead of 14 inline slots on every Element. The setter is internal (PR #455 CR item #6): ordinary code uses the field shim properties (Attached, ThemeBindings, AnimationConfig, …) below and never observes this slot. Keeping the setter off the public surface removes an initializer-ordering footgun — a public with { Extensions = X } after a shim write would have silently discarded the shim. The engine and perf-critical internal paths may still set it directly. Remarks Spec 047 §4.4. ImplicitTransitions Implicit transitions (opacity, scale, rotation, translation, background). Set via fluent extension methods: Rectangle().OpacityTransition() Applied by the reconciler after mount/update, so they are always present when property values are set via .Set() callbacks. InteractionStates Interaction states configuration (.InteractionStates() modifier). When set, the reconciler registers pointer event handlers that drive zero-reconcile visual state transitions (hover, pressed, focused). Key Optional key for stable identity across re-renders (like React's key prop). When set, the reconciler uses it to match elements across list reorderings. KeyframeAnimations Keyframe animation definitions (.Keyframes() modifier). Trigger-based: plays when the trigger value changes between renders. LayoutAnimation Composition-layer layout animation configuration. When set, the reconciler attaches implicit animations to the element's Visual so that layout-driven position (and optionally size) changes animate smoothly. Set via fluent extension methods: Border(child).LayoutAnimation() Margin Outer margin shim that routes to Element.Modifiers. Lets el with { Margin = new Thickness(8) } work directly on a record initializer (where extension methods are not visible). Identical semantics to .Margin(...). Modifiers Layout modifiers (margin, padding, size, alignment, etc.) applied to this element. Set via fluent extension methods: TextBlock("hi").Margin(10).Width(200) Modifiers are stored inline so the concrete element type is preserved through chaining. Padding Inner padding shim that routes to Element.Modifiers. Lets el with { Padding = new Thickness(8) } work directly on a record initializer (where extension methods are not visible). Identical semantics to .Padding(...). ResourceOverrides Per-control resource overrides (lightweight styling). When set, the reconciler injects these into FrameworkElement.Resources so that the control's VisualStateManager picks them up for hover/pressed/disabled states. Set via fluent extension: Button("Go").Resources(r => r.Set("ButtonBackground", "#0078D4")) ScrollAnimation Scroll-linked expression animation configuration (.ScrollLinked() modifier). Expression animations run on the compositor, driven by ScrollViewer position. StaggerConfig Stagger configuration for container children (.Stagger() modifier). When set, child animations (enter, layout, property) have incrementing DelayTime = childIndex * staggerDelay. ThemeBindings Theme-resource bindings for brush properties (Background, Foreground, BorderBrush). When set, the reconciler resolves from WinUI theme resources instead of using local values. Set via fluent extension methods: TextBlock("hi").Background(Theme.Accent) ThemeTransitions Theme transitions (children, item container). Set via fluent extension methods: VStack(children).WithTransitions(...) Operators op_Implicit Convenience: implicitly convert a string to a TextBlockElement. Allows writing: VStack("Hello", "World") instead of VStack(TextBlock("Hello"), TextBlock("World")) Parameters Name Type Description text string

Learn more: Commanding CommandBarElement Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: CommandBar Modifiers: Set Property Type Default Description Content Element? DefaultLabelPosition CommandBarDefaultLabelPosition IsOpen bool PrimaryCommands AppBarItemBase[]? null SecondaryCommands AppBarItemBase[]? null CommandBarFlyoutElement Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: CommandBarFlyout Modifiers: Set Property Type Default Description IsOpen bool Opens the flyout declaratively. Like FlyoutElement.IsOpen this is a one-shot trigger: the flyout is shown on mount when already true, and on the false → true edge of an update. Setting it back to false does not close the flyout — the user dismisses it (outside click, Esc, or invoking a command). The target normally opens the flyout on click without this. Placement FlyoutPlacementMode Preferred position of the flyout relative to its target. Defaults to FlyoutPlacementMode.Auto, which means "no opinion — let WinUI decide": Reactor clears FlyoutBase.Placement so it falls back to the control's own default (FlyoutPlacementMode.Top) instead of writing Auto, because WinUI's show-time validator rejects Auto and terminates the process. Changing an already-mounted flyout from an explicit placement back to FlyoutPlacementMode.Auto therefore returns it to that default, rather than leaving a stale local value that would outrank a Style setter. PrimaryCommands AppBarItemBase[]? null SecondaryCommands AppBarItemBase[]? null Target Element CommandHostElement Scopes keyboard accelerators from a set of commands to a subtree. Accelerators are only active when the host or its descendants have focus. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: BreadcrumbBar Modifiers: ItemClicked, Set Property Type Default Description Items BreadcrumbBarItemData[] OnItemClicked Action<BreadcrumbBarItemData>? null FrameElement The element record that describes a WinUI Frame control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: Frame Modifiers: Navigated, Navigating, NavigationFailed, Set Property Type Description NavigationParameter object? OnNavigated Action<Type>? Raised after a successful navigation. Receives the new SourcePageType. OnNavigating Action<Type>? Raised before navigation begins. Receives the target SourcePageType. Cancellation is not supported via this fluent — use .Set(...) to wire the raw Navigating event for that. OnNavigationFailed Action<Type, Exception>? Raised when a navigation fails. Receives the target SourcePageType and the failure exception. Wiring this also marks the failure handled, so a page whose constructor throws degrades into this callback instead of tearing down the application. SourcePageType Type? The Page-derived type to navigate to on mount. NavigationHostElement Renders the content for the current route of a NavigationHandle<TRoute>. Created via NavigationHost<TRoute>(nav, routeMap) in the DSL. The reconciler uses a Grid container so outgoing/incoming pages can overlap during transitions (Phase 4). Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: NavigationHost Property Type Description CacheMode NavigationCacheMode CacheSize int NavigationHandle object RouteMap Func<object, Element> Transition NavigationTransition NavigationViewElement The element record that describes a WinUI NavigationView control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: NavigationView Modifiers: AlwaysShowHeader, AutoSuggestBox, BackButtonVisible, BackRequested, CompactModeThresholdWidth, CompactPaneLength, ContentOverlay, DisplayModeChanged, ExpandedModeThresholdWidth, FooterMenuItems, IsPaneOpen, ItemCollapsed, ItemExpanding, ItemInvoked, OpenPaneLength, OverflowLabelMode, PaneCustomContent, PaneDisplayMode, PaneFooter, PaneHeader, PaneOpenChanged, PaneTitle, PaneToggleButtonVisible, PaneVisible, SelectedTagChanged, SelectionFollowsFocus, Set, SettingsSelected, ShoulderNavigation, TitleBarAutoPadding, WithNavigation Property Type Default Description AlwaysShowHeader bool Whether NavigationViewElement.Header stays visible in Minimal/Compact display modes. AutoSuggestBox AutoSuggestBoxElement? AutoSuggestBox rendered at the top of the pane. Mirrors NavigationView.AutoSuggestBox. CompactModeThresholdWidth double Window width below which the pane collapses to compact mode. NaN (the default) means Reactor never writes this property, leaving the WinUI default of 640. Sticky: changing an explicit value back to NaN skips the write rather than restoring 640. CompactPaneLength double Width of the pane when compact. NaN (the default) means Reactor never writes this property, leaving the WinUI default of 48. Sticky: changing an explicit value back to NaN skips the write rather than restoring 48. Content Element? null ContentOverlay Element? Element overlaid on top of NavigationViewElement.Content, e.g. a persistent player or status bar. ExpandedModeThresholdWidth double Window width at which the pane auto-expands. NaN (the default) means Reactor never writes this property, leaving the WinUI default of 1008. Sticky: changing an explicit value back to NaN skips the write rather than restoring 1008. FooterMenuItems NavigationViewItemData[] Menu items pinned to the bottom of the pane, below NavigationViewElement.PaneFooter's divider. Share the NavigationViewElement.SelectedTag namespace with NavigationViewElement.MenuItems. Header Element? IsBackButtonVisible NavigationViewBackButtonVisible Visibility of NavigationView's built-in back button. Mirrors NavigationView.IsBackButtonVisible. Set to NavigationViewBackButtonVisible.Collapsed when a TitleBarElement owns the back button instead. IsBackEnabled bool IsPaneOpen bool Whether the pane is open. Defaults to true. Edge-triggered. This declares a transition, not a mirror: Reactor writes the control only when the declared value changes. The control opens and closes its own pane (light dismiss, adaptive display-mode changes on resize) without touching the declared value, so re-rendering the same declared value will not force the pane back. Feed NavigationViewElement.OnPaneOpenChanged into the state that drives this property (issue #916). IsPaneToggleButtonVisible bool Whether NavigationView's built-in pane-toggle ("hamburger") button is shown. Mirrors NavigationView.IsPaneToggleButtonVisible. Set to false when a TitleBarElement owns the pane-toggle button instead. IsPaneVisible bool Whether the pane is shown at all. false hides the whole pane, leaving only the content area. IsSettingsVisible bool IsTitleBarAutoPaddingEnabled bool Whether NavigationView reserves top padding for the window's title bar. MenuItems NavigationViewItemData[] OnBackRequested Action? OnDisplayModeChanged Action<NavigationViewDisplayMode>? Raised when NavigationView switches between Minimal/Compact/Expanded in response to its width. OnItemCollapsed Action<string?>? Raised when a hierarchical menu item is collapsed. Carries the item's tag. OnItemExpanding Action<string?>? Raised when a hierarchical menu item is expanded. Carries the item's tag. OnItemInvoked Action<string?>? Raised when a menu item is invoked (clicked / activated), including re-invoking the already-selected item, which NavigationViewElement.OnSelectedTagChanged does not report. Carries the item's tag, or NavigationViewElement.SettingsTag for the settings item. OnPaneOpenChanged Action<bool>? Fires whenever the realized control's IsPaneOpen changes — including changes the app never requested (light dismiss, adaptive display-mode changes on resize) and the echo of a programmatic NavigationViewElement.IsPaneOpen write. Feed the value back into the state that drives NavigationViewElement.IsPaneOpen to keep controlled pane state in sync (issue #916). Same shape as SplitViewElement.OnPaneOpenChanged. OnSelectedTagChanged Action<string?>? OnSettingsSelected Action? Raised when NavigationView's built-in settings item becomes selected — by the user, or by setting NavigationViewElement.SelectedTag to NavigationViewElement.SettingsTag. Distinguishes the settings item from "nothing selected" — NavigationViewElement.OnSelectedTagChanged reports null for both. OpenPaneLength double Width of the pane when expanded. NaN (the default) means Reactor never writes this property, leaving the WinUI default of 320. Sticky: changing an explicit value back to NaN skips the write rather than restoring 320. OverflowLabelMode NavigationViewOverflowLabelMode Whether the Top pane's overflow button shows a "More" label or only the chevron. PaneCustomContent Element? Custom element rendered between the AutoSuggestBox and the menu items. PaneDisplayMode NavigationViewPaneDisplayMode PaneFooter Element? Element rendered at the bottom of the pane, below all menu items. PaneHeader Element? Element rendered at the top of the pane, above the menu items and below the pane title. PaneTitle string? SelectedTag string? SelectionFollowsFocus NavigationViewSelectionFollowsFocus Whether moving keyboard focus between menu items also changes the selection. ShoulderNavigationEnabled NavigationViewShoulderNavigationEnabled Whether gamepad shoulder buttons cycle the selection. Member Description SettingsTag Well-known NavigationViewElement.SelectedTag value that selects NavigationView's built-in settings item — the only menu entry NavigationView creates itself, so it has no NavigationViewItemData and cannot be addressed by an author-chosen tag. Also the tag reported to NavigationViewElement.OnItemInvoked when settings is invoked. An author item carrying this tag still wins: selection searches NavigationViewElement.MenuItems and NavigationViewElement.FooterMenuItems before falling back to the settings item, so the sentinel can never shadow real content. Reserved, so do not use it as an ordinary item tag. Selection would work, but WithNavigation skips it when mapping a tag back to a route — it routes the sentinel through its own settingsRoute parameter instead — so such an item would select without navigating. Created by: PipsPager Modifiers: MaxVisiblePips, NextButtonVisibility, PreviousButtonVisibility, SelectedPageIndexChanged, Set, WrapMode Property Type Description MaxVisiblePips int Maximum number of visible pips. Defaults to 5 (matches WinUI). NextButtonVisibility PipsPagerButtonVisibility When the next button shows. Defaults to Collapsed. NumberOfPages int OnSelectedPageIndexChanged Action<int>? PreviousButtonVisibility PipsPagerButtonVisibility When the previous button shows. Defaults to Collapsed. SelectedPageIndex Optional<int> Selected page index. Defaults to Optional.Unset; use Optional<int>.Of(-1) to force no page selection. WrapMode PipsPagerWrapMode Whether the selected index wraps around the ends. Defaults to None. Created by: Pivot Modifiers: SelectedIndexChanged, Set Property Type Description Items PivotItemData[] OnSelectedIndexChanged Action<int>? SelectedIndex Optional<int> Selected pivot item index. Defaults to Optional.Unset; use Optional<int>.Of(-1) to force no selection. Title string? SelectorBarElement The element record that describes a WinUI SelectorBar control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: SelectorBar Modifiers: SelectedIndexChanged, Set Property Type Description Items SelectorBarItemData[] OnSelectedIndexChanged Action<int>? SelectedIndex Optional<int> Selected item index. Defaults to Optional.Unset; use Optional<int>.Of(-1) to force no selection. TabViewElement The element record that describes a WinUI TabView control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: TabView Modifiers: AddTabButtonClick, AllowDropTabs, CanDragTabs, CanReorderTabs, CloseButtonOverlayMode, FillContentArea, IsAddButtonVisible, IsAddTabButtonVisible, SelectedIndexChanged, Set, ShowAddButton, TabCloseRequested, TabDragCompleted, TabDragStarting, TabStripFooter, TabStripHeader, TabWidthMode Property Type Description AllowDropTabs bool Whether tabs from another TabView can be dropped onto this one. CanDragTabs bool Whether tabs can be dragged out (to a window). CanReorderTabs bool Whether tabs can be reordered within the strip. CloseButtonOverlayMode TabViewCloseButtonOverlayMode Controls when the per-tab close button is visible. Defaults to Auto. FillContentArea bool Opt in to having the tab content area fill the space the TabView is given by its parent (issue #914). IsAddTabButtonVisible bool OnAddTabButtonClick Action? OnSelectedIndexChanged Action<int>? OnTabCloseRequested Action<int>? OnTabDragCompleted Action<int, bool>? Fires when a tab drag finishes — either landed on another TabView (wasOutside == false) or was dropped outside any TabView (wasOutside == true, used by §2.4 to trigger tear-out). OnTabDragStarting Action<int>? Fires when the user starts dragging a tab. tabIndex is the index of the dragged tab in TabViewElement.Tabs. Used by spec 045 §2.4 docking drag pipeline to start a DockDragSession. SelectedIndex Optional<int> Selected tab index. Defaults to Optional.Unset; use Optional<int>.Of(-1) to force no selection. TabStripFooter Element? Element rendered at the trailing edge of the tab strip. TabStripHeader Element? Element rendered at the leading edge of the tab strip. TabWidthMode TabViewWidthMode How tab widths are sized. Defaults to Equal (matches WinUI default). Tabs TabViewItemData[] TitleBarElement The element record that describes a WinUI TitleBar control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: TitleBar Modifiers: AutoRefreshDragRegions, BackButtonEnabled, BackButtonVisible, BackRequested, Content, HeightOption, Icon, LeftHeader, NoIcon, PaneToggleButtonVisible, PaneToggleRequested, PreferredTheme, RightHeader, Set, Subtitle, Tall, WithNavigation Property Type Description AutoRefreshDragRegions bool When true, the WinUI TitleBar re-derives its drag regions on every layout pass (WinApp SDK ≥ 2.1.3). Useful when TitleBarElement.Content changes across renders. Default false (matches the control default; interactive controls are still auto-excluded from the drag region). See spec 059. Content Element? HeightOption WindowTitleBarHeight? System caption height for the hosting window. Tall is the standard layout when the title bar hosts navigation chrome (back button / pane toggle) and is the direct analogue of the XAML NavigationView template's AppWindow.TitleBar.PreferredHeightOption = Tall plus its <RowDefinition Height="48" />. (issue #917) Icon IconData? Icon shown in the title bar's leading slot. Mirrors WinUI 3 TitleBar.IconSource. Pass a SymbolIconData / FontIconData for built-in glyphs, or ImageIconData / BitmapIconData for a bundled .ico / image (e.g. new ImageIconData(new Uri("ms-appx:///Assets/AppIcon.ico"))). Left unset, the title bar inherits the window's icon — WindowSpec.Icon if declared, otherwise the Assets\AppIcon.ico convention — so an app that already has an icon need not restate it here. The WinUI control does not do this itself. An icon that exists only as an executable PE resource is not inherited: that stage yields a raw HICON with no path, and a XAML IconSource needs an image source. Set TitleBarElement.SuppressIcon via .NoIcon() to show none. IsBackButtonEnabled bool IsBackButtonVisible bool IsPaneToggleButtonVisible bool LeftHeader Element? Custom content in the title bar's leading header slot. OnBackRequested Action? OnPaneToggleRequested Action? PreferredTheme WindowTitleBarTheme? Theme of the hosting window's system caption buttons (AppWindow.TitleBar.PreferredTheme). null (the default) leaves the caption alone. (issue #1297) RightHeader Element? Subtitle string? SuppressIcon bool Suppresses the icon entirely, including the one Reactor would otherwise inherit from the window (see TitleBarElement.Icon). Set via .NoIcon(). Title string

Pre-parsed WinUI Geometry. When null, the reconciler resolves from PathElement.PathDataString. Callers that construct PathElement directly (not via D3Path) can set this for non-SVG geometries. Fill Brush? FillRule FillRule How interior regions are determined for fills. Defaults to EvenOdd. PathDataString string? The path markup string (SVG / XAML path syntax). When set, geometry is converted lazily by the reconciler with WinUI's native path-markup converter — only when mounting or when the string changes between renders — so no COM Geometry is created on every tree build. Markup the platform rejects (for example a NaN coordinate) falls back to PathElement.Data, or draws nothing. RenderTransform Transform? Stroke Brush? StrokeDashArray DoubleCollection? Defaults to 0. StrokeEndLineCap PenLineCap Cap rendered at the end of an open stroke. Defaults to Flat. StrokeLineJoin PenLineJoin Join style between two connected stroke segments. Defaults to Miter. StrokeMiterLimit double Maximum extent of a miter join relative to half the stroke thickness. Defaults to 10. StrokeStartLineCap PenLineCap Cap rendered at the start of an open stroke. Created by: InfoBadge Modifiers: Set Property Type Description Icon string? Value int? InfoBarElement The element record that describes a WinUI InfoBar control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Inherits from Element. Created by: InfoBar Modifiers: ActionButtonClick, Closable, Closed, Content, Error, IconSource, Informational, IsClosable, Set, Severity, Success, Warning Property Type Default Description ActionButtonContent string? Content Element? Custom rich content rendered below the message (e.g. links, buttons, an embedded form). IconSource IconData? Custom icon source. When set, overrides the severity-based icon. IsClosable bool Whether the bar shows its built-in close button. Defaults to true. IsOpen bool Whether the bar is shown. Defaults to true, so InfoBar("Title", "Message") is visible without ceremony. Edge-triggered. This declares a transition, not a mirror: Reactor writes the control only when the declared value changes. The user can dismiss the bar with its built-in close button, which sets IsOpen to false on the control without touching the declared value — re-rendering the same declared true will not bring it back, and is not meant to. Wire InfoBarElement.OnClosed (or .Closed(...)) into the state that drives this property; a later false → true transition then re-opens the bar. Message string? null OnActionButtonClick Action? OnClosed Action? Severity InfoBarSeverity Title string? null ProgressElement The element record that describes a WinUI ProgressBar control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. content: Use these types to add your own controls to Reactor or to change how built-in controls are created and updated. Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol, Element Pool Types Type Description Children strategies Records that tell the reconciler how a control holds its children. Descriptor callbacks Delegates and attributes used by control descriptors. Handler contexts Contexts passed to an element handler when it mounts, updates or unmounts a control. ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl> Spec 047 §6 / §14 Phase 2 (Q1 spike) — declarative control description. ControlRegistry Spec 048 §8 — the global, lazy, lock-free control registry that backs the factory-as-registration pattern. DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl> Spec 047 §6 / §14 Phase 2 (Q1 spike) — interpreter that drives a ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl> against the v1 protocol surface. ElementPool Per-CLR-type pool (cap 32 per lane) that recycles unmounted WinUI FrameworkElement instances. IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement> Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 completion — decorator-style V1 handler contract for elements whose returned UIElement identity may change on update or whose unmount disposition diverges from the standard pool-return. IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> Spec 047 §4 / §14 Phase 1 (1.6) — author-facing handler contract for porting a control onto the v1 protocol. PoolPolicy<TControl> Spec 047 §13 Q18 / §14 Phase 1 (1.5) — author-facing pool policy. PropEntry<TElement, TControl> Spec 047 §6 / §14 Phase 2 (Q1 spike) — base class for descriptor entries declared on a ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl>. ReactorBinding Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.4) — public author-facing surface for the echo suppression primitive (§13 Q19). ReactorBinding<TElement> Spec 047 §9 / §14 Phase 1 (1.6) — per-binding event helper. ReactorFeatureFlags Process-wide feature flags that gate risky or in-progress behavior. Reconciler The reconciler diffs old and new element trees and patches the real WinUI control tree.

content: A descriptor is the data-driven alternative to a hand-coded IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>. Authors declare property bindings (OneWay, ControlDescriptor.InitialOnly, ControlDescriptor.Controlled), an optional children strategy, and an optional factory; the interpreter (DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>) executes them against the same v1 protocol surface a hand-coded handler would use. Phase 2 measurement gate (§13 Q1): the descriptor and the hand-coded handler shapes are evaluated head-to-head on the same M1 / M2 / M5 / M7 / M10 micro-benches and the L4 / L9 macros, then the §13 Q1 decision matrix determines which surface ships as the primary author path. See docs/specs/047-extensible-control-model.md §13 Q1. Echo suppression (issue #206). A .Controlled / .HandCodedControlled entry suppresses the echo of its own programmatic write automatically — the interpreter wraps the write in the public ReactorBinding WriteSuppressed primitive (or arms a value-diff predicate when valueDiffEcho is set), so a framework-driven write never echoes back into the user's OnChanged callback. Descriptor authors therefore never touch the suppressor directly; hand-coded IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> authors call WriteSuppressed themselves. See docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md. Fluent author pattern: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor. Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol Constructors ControlDescriptor Properties AfterChildrenMount Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 prelude (Engine A1) — optional post-children mount hook. The interpreter (DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>) surfaces it through IElementHandler.AfterChildrenMount, which the adapter invokes after every child has mounted. Use for events that must subscribe after children-add (TabView SelectionChanged), or for imperative work that must run strictly after the prop loop AND the event subscriptions (FrameElement's mount-time navigation, which would otherwise complete before its own Navigated/NavigationFailed handlers exist). Defaults to null (no hook). Set it from an object initializer, or — from a generated descriptor's Customize hook, which receives an already-constructed descriptor — via ControlDescriptor.WithAfterChildrenMount. Children Optional children strategy. Engine dispatches through it via V1HandlerAdapter after each Mount / Update body returns. Defaults to null (treated as None<TElement, TControl> by the adapter). Factory Optional factory the engine invokes when the pool is empty or ControlDescriptor.PoolPolicy opts out. Defaults to new TControl() via the new() constraint. GetSetters Setters selector — the descriptor needs an opaque way to pull the element's Action<TControl>[] setters chain because each element subclass declares its own Setters property (no common base interface). Authors register e => e.Setters; the interpreter passes the result to Reconciler.ApplySetters after the property entries have run. Defaults to "no setters" if not configured. OnUnmount Optional teardown hook. The interpreter (DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>) surfaces it through IElementHandler.Unmount, which the engine invokes when the control leaves the tree. Use it to invalidate control-scoped state the descriptor created during mount and that the pool reset contract cannot see — a pending deferred write, a one-shot Loaded subscription, a disposable. Defaults to null (no hook). Set it from an object initializer, or — from a generated descriptor's Customize hook, which receives an already-constructed descriptor — via ControlDescriptor.WithUnmount. Not for event trampolines: those anchor to the control's lifetime by design (see the unsubscribe no-op contract on ControlDescriptor.Controlled). Declaring this hook makes DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl> force the control's ReactorState into existence at mount, because the engine's unmount dispatch is tag-gated. That costs one small allocation per mounted control of this type, so declare it only when there is real teardown to do. PoolPolicy Optional pool policy. When null the engine uses the default (poolable if the control type opts in via PoolableTypes). Properties Read-only view of the property entries declared on this descriptor (in declaration order). Methods CoercingOneWay Add a one-way property whose write may coerce a sibling controlled prop's value (e.g. Slider.Minimum coercing Slider.Value). When coercesController returns true the write is wrapped in ReactorBinding.WriteSuppressed so the coercion-driven change event is dropped. Declarative replacement for the imperative if (ctrl.Value < n.Min) WriteSuppressed(...) pattern in the hand-coded SliderHandler. Encodes the §8 audit's "coercion-tolerance" treatment for the 8 audited coercion sites (NumberBox / Slider Min/Max etc.) as a single declarative entry. Parameters Name Type Default Description get Func<TElement, TValue> set Action<TControl, TValue> coercesController Func<TControl, TValue, bool> comparer IEqualityComparer<TValue>? null CollectionDiffControlled §14 Phase 3-final — .CollectionDiffControlled. Two-way bound prop whose value is an IReadOnlyList on the element side and an IList<TItem> on the control side. Each Update applies a keyed hash-set diff and emits per-element Add/Remove ops inside ChangeEchoSuppressor.BeginSuppress. Used by CalendarView for SelectedDates; reusable for any control with a typed IObservableVector<T> two-way slot. The engine writes from element state when get returns a value and leaves the control authoritative when it returns Optional.Unset; writes use echo suppression on Update. The control raises subscribe's event on user interaction; the trampoline invokes the element's callback with readBack's value. Callback gating: if callback returns null on the element passed at Mount, no subscription happens at all — mirrors the hand-coded Ensure*Wiring gate. Parameters Name Type Default Description get Func<TElement, Optional<TValue>> set Action<TControl, TValue> subscribe Action<FrameworkElement, EventHandler<TArgs>> unsubscribe Action<FrameworkElement, EventHandler<TArgs>> callback Func<TElement, Action<TValue>?> readBack Func<TControl, TValue> comparer IEqualityComparer<TValue>? null HandCodedControlled §14 Phase 3 (3.0.1) — escape-hatch builder for controlled (two-way) props on a control that needs a hand-authored trampoline against a user-supplied per-control event payload (TPayload). Required for multi-event controls (e.g. TextBox.Text alongside SelectionChanged) where the single-event fast-path DescriptorControlledPayload would collide if two controlled entries shared the same closed generic. The payload type is typically reused from ControlEventPayloads.cs (e.g. TextBoxEventPayload) which already has a slot per event. slotIsNull + setSlot address the specific slot on the payload this entry owns; subscribe wires the user-supplied native TDelegate directly to the control's event (no EventHandler<TArgs> bridge closure). Mount/Update prop-write semantics are identical to ControlDescriptor.Controlled: unset skips writes, set values perform a bare initial write and a suppressed write on control drift. Subscription is gated on callback returning non-null on the mounted element. valueDiffEcho replaces the Update write's suppress-counter token with the spec 047 §8 value-diff arm, which the trampoline consumes on the next change event and which drops that event only when its readback matches the written value. armOnMount (requires valueDiffEcho) arms the Mount write too. Set it when the control raises its change event after the write returns (e.g. RichEditBox's Document.SetText) and the trampoline cannot tell that echo apart on its own: the echo lands after the trampoline is wired and would otherwise reach the callback. The set lambda stays a plain write; the entry does the arming. Authors supply a per-control payload type and a native trampoline delegate; the entry wires subscription with the same payload-slot gating shape as ControlDescriptor.HandCodedControlled but performs no Mount/Update prop writes. Subscription is gated on callbackPresent returning non-null — the element's callback shape can be anything (e.g. Action<string, int, int>) so the gate is checked against the untyped Delegate. Pure subscription wiring for the "observed-DP callback + Loaded → inner template-part trampoline" pattern. The control's primary DP round-trip stays on a sibling .HandCodedControlled entry. See ImmediatePropEntry for the shape contract (NumberBox is the canonical proof point). Pass loadedHook as null when the DP observation is the whole subscription and there is no template part to walk. Imperative §14 Phase 3 finish — Engine (4). Escape hatch entry that receives mount+(update with BOTH old and new TElement, so the entry can express a diff the per-value get/set lambdas of ControlDescriptor.OneWayConditional can't: comparing one element field while writing a derived value elsewhere, or multi-source error context like Path.PathDataString's path-markup converter/pre-built Geometry branches. When to reach for it: only when the standard entries can't express the diff or the write. Imperative entries skip the engine's value-comparer fast-path, so a misused Imperative entry re-runs on every render. The other entry shapes (OneWay, ControlDescriptor.OneWayConditional, ControlDescriptor.CoercingOneWay, ControlDescriptor.HandCodedControlled) still cover the 95% case. Distinct from Imperative<TElement, TControl> (a ChildrenStrategy<TElement, TControl> that drives the whole CHILD subtree imperatively) — this is a property-level escape hatch that participates in the normal prop loop. Bridged variant of ControlDescriptor.Imperative — the lambdas receive the MountContext / UpdateContext so they can call engine-internal helpers for bindings without owned child lifetime. For an owned secondary Element slot, use ControlDescriptor.ImperativeBridged so the mounted child also receives terminal teardown. This overload is for bindings that do not own child lifetime.
