content: Spec 048 §8 — the global, lazy, lock-free control registry that backs the factory-as-registration pattern. Holds Type → factory-of- IV1HandlerEntry entries; never roots a handler or WinUI control type by itself. Every static reference to a handler/control type lives in the callers of ControlRegistry.Register — per-control factory cctors (Pattern A) or Reg<…> static-field initializers (Pattern B), each on a per-control rooted path. The trimmer therefore keeps a control iff its factory is reachable from the app entry point. Idempotent first-wins. Repeat ControlRegistry.Register calls for the same element type are a silent no-op (spec §12.1). Multiple factories legitimately map to the same element type — e.g. TextBlock(), Heading(), and Subheading() all produce TextBlockElement (spec §10.3) — and a throw from a cctor would surface as a non-deterministic TypeInitializationException at the first-use point. The strict throw-on-duplicate policy from spec 047 §13 Q17 is preserved on the explicit per-host Reconciler.RegisterHandler path. Hot path. Per spec §9, ControlRegistry.Register runs at most once per element type per process, on the cold first-use path. The steady-state per-host dispatch lookup short-circuits in the per-host _v1Handlers cache populated on the first registry hit; the registry itself is consulted at most once per (host, element type) pair. AOT. No reflection, no Type.MakeGenericType; the closed-type capture happens inside the generic ControlRegistry.Register entry point so the AOT compiler can see the closed types statically. The internal map is keyed by Type and stores Func delegates only — no MakeGenericType, no runtime type construction. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol. Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol Methods Register Spec §8 — register a handler factory for TElement. Idempotent first-wins: if an entry already exists for typeof(TElement), this call is a silent no-op. The handler factory is invoked at most once per (host, element type) — on the first dispatch hit — and the resulting adapter is cached into the host's _v1Handlers map so steady-state dispatch is the existing fast per-host lookup. The handlerFactory delegate should be a static lambda (no captures) — Pattern A / Pattern B both rely on the single allocation being interned in a static field at the call site. A capturing lambda is functionally correct but allocates a closure on every Reg<>.Init / cctor run, undoing the cost-model claim in spec §9. Echo suppression for value-bearing controls (issue #206). A custom IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> registered here that writes a value-bearing property in Update must guard that write with the supported public primitive ReactorBinding<TElement>'s WriteSuppressed method (or the static ReactorBinding) so the control's own echo does not flow back as a spurious user edit. Never reach into the internal ChangeEchoSuppressor. Descriptor authors get this through .Controlled / .HandCodedControlled. See docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md. Parameters Name Type Description handlerFactory Func<IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>> A factory that, when invoked, returns a fresh handler. Strongly recommended to be a static lambda (e.g. static () => new MarqueeHandler()) so the delegate is cached in a static field and no closure is allocated. Type parameters Name Description TElement The element record type the handler dispatches against. Used as the dispatch key (Type). TControl The WinUI control the handler mounts. RegisterDecorator Spec 048 §3.4 — decorator sibling of ControlRegistry.Register for handlers that implement IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement> (a separate, non-inheriting interface from IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>). Decorator handlers cover target-wrapping flyouts, modal lifecycle wrappers, polymorphic mounts (IconElement), interop bridges (XamlHost/XamlPage), and the keyed-reconcile panels (Stack/Grid/ Canvas/RelativePanel/WrapGrid/Flex) + Button/CheckBox/Expander — see IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement> for the full use-case list. Stores the same Func shape as the value-handler path, so Reconciler.TryResolveFromControlRegistry (dispatch arm 3) consumes both uniformly — no dispatch changes required. The adapter wrapping is the only difference: V1DecoratorHandlerAdapter versus V1HandlerAdapter. One-shim invariant (§3.4 authoring rule). For any given element type, factories must touch exactly one of Reg<…>.Done or RegDecorator<…>.Done — never both. The first-wins TryAdd silently keeps whichever path's cctor fires first; mixing them creates a non-deterministic dispatch outcome that depends on factory call order across the app's startup graph. This contrasts with the harmless aliasing case where multiple factories share the same closed-generic shim (spec §10.3 Heading/Subheading both touching Reg<TextBlockElement, TextBlock, TextBlockHandler>). Singleton-handler factories. A decorator handler exposed as a public static readonly singleton whose underlying type is a private nested class cannot satisfy RegDecorator's new() constraint. Such a factory registers directly via this method with a static lambda returning the singleton: This is functionally equivalent to RegDecorator<…>.Done — the static lambda still has no captures, the TryAdd still first-wins, and the trim story still routes every reference to the private handler type through the factory call-site path the trimmer can see. (The built-in Icon/XamlPage/XamlHost decorators that formerly used this pattern are now source-generated — spec 058 §15 P5.27/P5.28 — and self-register via a generated Pattern-A cctor.) Parameters Name Type Description handlerFactory Func<IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement>> A factory that, when invoked, returns a fresh decorator handler. Strongly recommended to be a static lambda (e.g. static () => new ButtonHandler()) so the delegate is cached in a static field and no closure is allocated. Type parameters Name Description TElement The element record type the decorator handler dispatches against. Used as the dispatch key (Type). RegisterDecoratorForDerivedTypes Spec 048 §3.4 — decorator sibling of ControlRegistry.RegisterForDerivedTypes. Parameters Name Type Description handlerFactory Func<IDecoratorElementHandler<TBase>> RegisterForDerivedTypes Spec 048 §3.4 — base-derived sibling of ControlRegistry.Register. Registers a handler for TBase that also catches every concrete element type whose runtime Type derives from TBase. Exact-type registrations (via ControlRegistry.Register / ControlRegistry.RegisterDecorator) take precedence over a base-derived registration, matching the per-host V1HandlerRegistry.TryGet precedence. Used for the four cases that registered through Reconciler.RegisterDescriptorForDerivedTypes on the per-host path: TemplatedListElementBase, LazyStackElementBase, ItemsRepeaterElement, and ItemsViewElement — each is a non-generic intermediate base whose closed-T variants (TemplatedListViewElement<Person>, etc.) should all share the same handler. Parameters Name Type Description handlerFactory Func<IElementHandler<TBase, TControl>>

content: Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol AfterChildrenMountCallback<TElement, TControl> Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 prelude (Engine A1) — post-children mount callback signature for ControlDescriptor.AfterChildrenMount. Invoked by V1HandlerAdapter after the descriptor's children strategy has mounted/bound every child, so a descriptor can wire events that must subscribe strictly after children-add (e.g. TabView.SelectionChanged). Takes MountContext by in to preserve the allocation-free ref-struct contract. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor. DescriptorUnmountCallback<TControl> Teardown callback signature for ControlDescriptor.OnUnmount. Invoked by DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl> from the engine's IElementHandler.Unmount dispatch, so a descriptor can invalidate control-scoped state it set up during mount — pending deferred writes, one-shot lifecycle subscriptions, disposables. Takes UnmountContext by in to preserve the allocation-free ref-struct contract. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor. Remarks The engine still runs the pool reset contract afterwards; this hook is for state the reset contract cannot see, such as a Loaded handler the descriptor attached itself. NoClearValueAttribute Suppresses the REACTOR0050 analyzer for a descriptor field or property whose OneWay entries intentionally use Optional<T> without a dependency-property backing value to clear. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor. Inherits from Attribute. Remarks Prefer providing the dp: argument to ControlDescriptor.OneWay whenever the target WinUI property is backed by a dependency property. Use this attribute only for descriptor entries whose unset value should skip the write because there is no dependency property, or because clearing the local value would be semantically wrong for that control. Constructors NoClearValueAttribute OneWayBridgedSetter<TControl, TValue> Spec 047 §14 Phase 3-final — set-lambda signature for OneWayBridgedPropEntry. Named delegate type (not Action<...>) so the MountContext / UpdateContext doesn't need to be passed — the entry projects the two pieces a bridge typically needs (the Reconciler and the rerender callback). Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor.

content: Spec 047 §6 / §14 Phase 2 (Q1 spike) — interpreter that drives a ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl> against the v1 protocol surface. Implemented as a regular IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> so the V1HandlerAdapter dispatch shell is identical between the descriptor and hand-coded handler paths — the only thing that differs between the Q1 A|B variants is the body of Mount / Update. Any measured delta is the interpreter's tax, not a different dispatch shape. Mount sequence (matches the hand-coded handlers' KD-1b ordering): Rent the control via MountContext.RentControl. Iterate ControlDescriptor.Properties and invoke PropEntry.Mount on each — all bare initial writes happen first. Iterate again and invoke PropEntry.EnsureSubscribed — controlled entries wire their change-event trampolines now (no echo on the just- written values because nothing is listening yet). Apply setters. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor. Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol Remarks Spec 048 §7 — unsealed so the built-in catalog can expose a thin, new()-constructible registration subclass per descriptor (e.g. TextBlockDescriptorHandler(): DescriptorHandler<…>(TextBlockDescriptor.Descriptor)). That subclass is what the Reg shim instantiates via its static () => new THandler() lambda, so the descriptor path registers through the exact same zero-closure mechanism as a hand-coded handler. The base interpreter has no virtual members the subclass overrides; unsealing carries no dispatch cost (calls already route through the IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> interface via the adapter). Constructors DescriptorHandler Parameters Name Type Description descriptor ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl> Properties Children Children strategy surfaced to V1HandlerAdapter. Returns the descriptor's strategy except when it's an ItemsHost<TElement, TControl> — that one is dispatched inline by DescriptorHandler.Mount / DescriptorHandler.Update before the prop loop runs so initial writes like SelectedIndex land against a populated collection (matches legacy mount ordering). ChildrenForUnmount Issue #375 — on Unmount the bind-before-props ordering constraint that motivates hiding ItemsHost<TElement, TControl> / IItemsBinderStrategy strategies from DescriptorHandler.Children no longer applies, so expose the descriptor's real strategy here. Lets V1HandlerAdapter's unmount-side dispatch walk descendant items (e.g. TabView tabs whose content holds Components) and fire their UseEffect cleanups. Descriptor The descriptor this handler interprets. Exposed for tests and bench harnesses — not part of the steady-state author API. Methods AfterChildrenMount §14 Phase 3 prelude (Engine A1) — forwards to the descriptor's optional ControlDescriptor.AfterChildrenMount callback. The adapter invokes this after every child has mounted. Without this the descriptor path had no teardown seam at all, so control-scoped state a descriptor set up during mount — most notably a one-shot Loaded subscription carrying a deferred write — could outlive the mount that created it. content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Learn more: Element Pool Remarks Each type has two lanes (spec 066 §7.2). The plain lane holds controls whose composition visual was never taken. The visual lane holds controls whose visual was taken, reset to a fresh control's pixels by ElementPool.ResetTakenVisual. Such a control still refuses the facade transforms and the XAML implicit transitions, so only an element that takes the visual itself and has no setters rents from it. Constructors ElementPool Properties Enabled When false, TryRent always returns null and Return is a no-op. Useful for scenarios like the live previewer where recycled controls with stale property state can cause visual glitches. Methods Clear Empties all per-type stacks and releases the scratch panel. Called from Reconciler.Dispose to release pooled elements. Dispose Releases the resources that this object holds. Return Return an element to the pool after unmount. Cleans it first. Silently drops if the type is not poolable or its lane is full. Parameters Name Type Description element FrameworkElement TryRent Try to rent an element of the given type from the plain lane. Returns null if the lane is empty or the type is not poolable. Parameters Name Type Description type Type
description: Per-CLR-type pool (cap 32 per lane) that recycles unmounted WinUI FrameworkElement instances.
title: ElementPool

content: Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 completion — decorator-style V1 handler contract for elements whose returned UIElement identity may change on update or whose unmount disposition diverges from the standard pool-return. Use this contract instead of IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> for: Target-wrapping decorators (Flyout, MenuFlyout, CommandBarFlyout) where the returned UIElement IS the user's inner Target child — the control type isn't known until the element is inspected, and may change on update if the user swaps Target's element type. Modal lifecycle wrappers (ContentDialog, Popup) where the returned control is a placeholder and the actual modal surface is created lazily or as a sibling. Polymorphic mounts (IconElement) where the concrete control type depends on the element's runtime subtype. Interop bridges (XamlHost, XamlPage) where the returned control hosts arbitrary user-side XAML. Distinct from IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> to keep the §13 Q12 "no substitution" invariant on the standard author-facing surface — only built-in V1 ports use this decorator shape. External authors continue to use IElementHandler<TElement, TControl>. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol. Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol Methods GetSourceTarget Optional source-map override for target-wrapping decorators that return a child element's control but tag that control with the decorator element. Return the child element that created the control so ReactorSourceMap.GetSource reports the target's call site rather than the decorator's. Parameters Name Type Description element TElement Mount Mount the element and return the UIElement the engine installs in the parent's slot. Decorator handlers may recursively mount inner elements via ctx.MountChild(...) and return one of them (e.g., FlyoutElement returns its Target's mounted control). Parameters Name Type Description ctx MountContext element TElement Unmount Unmount the element and return the engine's post-unmount disposition for the control. The element is read from the attached state DP at unmount time; it may be null if the tag was already detached (defensive — should not happen for well-behaved decorator handlers). Parameters Name Type Description ctx UnmountContext element TElement? control UIElement Update Diff old vs. new element and apply updates. Returns the UIElement that should occupy the parent's slot after the update — typically the same control instance for an in-place update, or a different instance when the wrapped target changed type. The engine installs the returned value in the slot (replacing control if different). Parameters Name Type Description ctx UpdateContext oldEl TElement newEl TElement control UIElement
title: IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement>

content: Implementations register themselves via Reconciler.RegisterHandler; dispatch is exact-type by element.GetType() (§13 Q17). Update returns void — substitution is forbidden (§13 Q12); a type change flows through the unmount-and-remount path on the wrapping container. Hot path: dispatch is dictionary lookup + interface call (both already paid by V1HandlerRegistry). Implementations should avoid allocations in IElementHandler.Mount / IElementHandler.Update bodies; the ref struct context types are allocation-free by construction. Echo suppression for value-bearing controls (issue #206). If the control raises the same change event for a programmatic property write as it does for a user edit, a write from IElementHandler.Update would echo back through the trampoline into the owning component's OnChanged state setter — indistinguishable from real input. Guard every programmatic controlled-value write with the supported, RCW-safe public primitive ReactorBinding<TElement>'s WriteSuppressed method (or the static ReactorBinding): ctx.BindFor(ctrl, newEl).WriteSuppressed(() => ctrl.Value = newEl.Value). Pair it 1:1 with the write and gate it on an equality check so the token is always consumed by the engine-provoked echo. Descriptor authors get this for free through .Controlled / .HandCodedControlled. Never reach into the internal ChangeEchoSuppressor. See docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol. Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol Properties Children Optional children strategy. Engine dispatches through it when non-null (and not None<TElement, TControl>); otherwise the handler is a leaf for the purposes of child reconciliation. ChildrenForUnmount Issue #375 — children strategy the engine uses for the unmount-side child walk. Defaults to IElementHandler.Children; some implementations (notably DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>) suppress IElementHandler.Children when they dispatch a strategy inline during Mount/Update for ordering reasons (e.g. items-binder strategies whose collection must be populated before SelectedIndex initial writes land). On Unmount the ordering constraint no longer applies, so they expose the real strategy here so descendant Component UseEffect cleanups still fire. Methods AfterChildrenMount Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 prelude (Engine A1) — optional hook the engine invokes from V1HandlerAdapter after the IElementHandler.Children strategy has mounted/bound every child (and after any items-binder strategy the handler dispatched inline). Default no-op. Override this to wire events whose subscription must happen strictly after children-add — e.g. TabView.SelectionChanged, which WinUI fires spuriously while the first tab is being added if the handler subscribes during the prop-apply phase. Subscribing here side- steps that first-add echo. Returns the control the engine places into the parent's children collection. content: Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol MountContext Spec 047 §4 / §14 Phase 1 (1.6) — mount-time context passed to IElementHandler.Mount. UI-thread guarantee (Q14): handlers run on the reconciler's UI dispatcher. Mount bodies may freely access control state without synchronization. Calls from other threads throw in Debug builds today; Phase 1 plan is to measure first before tightening to unconditional throw. See docs/specs/047/phase1-results/q14-dispatcher-affinity.md. Allocation contract: MountContext is a readonly ref struct, so it cannot escape the call stack and never allocates on its own. Hot path (Mount body) pays only the dictionary lookup + interface call already incurred by the V1HandlerRegistry dispatch. Sample skeleton (per spec §4 ToggleSwitchHandler example): Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol. Obsolete. Provided as an escape hatch for handlers that need to forward a child mount through some non-strategy path. RequestRerender The rerender callback for the owning component subtree. Methods AddRawRoutedHandler Escape hatch (Q11) — attach a raw routed handler directly to the control. Handlers should prefer the typed On* family on ReactorBinding<TElement>; use this only for events the binding doesn't cover (e.g. UIElement.PreviewKeyDown on a non-FrameworkElement, or app-side custom routed events). The returned binding closes over the control identity, not the element — handlers re-fetch the live element via ReactorState.Element on each event fire, so the same binding survives element re-renders. The returned UIElement is whatever the reconciler decided to mount (possibly null for EmptyElement). Used by handlers that mount children which must see an author-supplied context. Returns the control to assign back into the slot. Public counterpart to the engine-internal child reconcile, so external wrappers (not just built-in descriptors) can host stateful secondary element slots — see [WrapElementSlot]. Handlers use UnmountContext.ReturnControl to participate in the pool reset contract; the engine takes care of detaching from the parent tree. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol. Obsolete. Types with embedded references are not supported in this version of your compiler. Properties Reconciler RequestRerender Methods ReturnControl Return a control to its per-type pool via the engine's reset contract. Safe to call twice — the pool dedupes by stack cap. Same shape as MountContext minus RentControl — updates run against an existing control, so allocation is forbidden on this path. UI-thread guarantee applies (see MountContext). See MountContext.ReconcileChild. Parameters Name Type Description oldChild Element? newChild Element? existing UIElement? V1UnmountDisposition Spec 047 §14 Phase 3 completion — controls the engine's pool-return / child-traversal decision after a V1 handler's Unmount body runs. Returned from IV1HandlerEntry.Unmount; the standard hand-coded + descriptor handlers always return V1UnmountDisposition.CollectSelf, matching the pre-Phase-3-completion behavior. Decorator-style handlers (IDecoratorElementHandler<TElement>) return the other dispositions to opt out of pool return / let the engine continue the default unmount traversal into the wrapped child. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol. Values Name Value Description CollectSelf 0 Default for standard handlers. The handler created the control via RentControl; the engine pools the control (if poolable) and stops the traversal — children were already torn down by the handler. ContinueDefaultTraversal 1 The handler's returned control is owned by another element (e.g., a decorator's wrapped Target child element). The engine must NOT pool the control and MUST continue the default unmount traversal as if no V1 handler had claimed it, so the inner element's own teardown runs. SkipPool 2 The handler manages teardown itself; the control is a placeholder/wrapper that should NOT be pooled and whose children were already torn down by the handler. Engine returns immediately without pool collection or traversal.

content: External and built-in V1 handlers attach a PoolPolicy<TControl> to their RentControl / ReturnControl calls to opt out of pooling (e.g. for controls with persistent native resources like MediaPlayerElement, MapControl, SwapChainPanel) or to layer an author-defined reset action on top of the engine's default contract. Pool key is typeof(TControl) only (Q18). Finer keys (e.g. by style hash) are a Phase 3+ addition. Provisional surface — see ReactorBinding for the REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW diagnostic id. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Learn more: Element Pool Constructors PoolPolicy Properties IsPoolable When false, RentControl always allocates a fresh instance and ReturnControl is a no-op (the control is dropped on the floor for the GC to collect). Default true. Reset Optional extra reset action, invoked last when the control is returned to the pool, after the engine's default reset. That reset clears the element pointer, the current modifier callbacks, echo-suppression and unmount state, and the Reactor-set DataContext. It keeps the attached ReactorState and its per-control ControlEventState, so event trampolines subscribed once for the control's lifetime stay subscribed and dispatch to the next element. Don't resubscribe native events here. Use it for control-specific transient state the engine can't know about (e.g. ScrollViewer.ChangeView animation queue).

content: Spec 047 §6 / §14 Phase 2 (Q1 spike) — base class for descriptor entries declared on a ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl>. The interpreter (see DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>) iterates the entry list during Mount and Update. The property's value type stays inside each concrete entry — the interpreter never sees it, so iterating a heterogeneous list of entries does not box value types (each generic specialization keeps its own monomorphic code path). Phase ordering inside Mount: PropEntry.Mount runs once per entry. Controlled entries write their initial value bare — event subscription has not yet been wired, so a synchronous change event has no trampoline to fire (no echo). Mirrors the KD-1b fix on the hand-coded handlers. A control whose change event is raised after the write returns echoes after the wiring below; its entry arms the Mount write instead (HandCodedControlled's armOnMount). PropEntry.EnsureSubscribed runs once per entry. Controlled entries subscribe to their change event here, guarded by DescriptorHandler<TElement, TControl>'s per-control subscription gate (so pool-reused controls do not double-subscribe). On Update, PropEntry.Update runs and writes through ReactorBinding.WriteSuppressed when the entry is controlled. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol.Descriptor. Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol Constructors PropEntry Methods EnsureSubscribed Event subscription hook. Default = no-op (one-way / initial entries do not subscribe to events). Controlled entries override. The interpreter calls this after every PropEntry.Mount in the entry list so all bare initial writes complete before any event trampoline goes live (KD-1b ordering invariant). Parameters Name Type Description binding ReactorBinding<TElement> ctrl TControl el TElement Mount Mount(TControl, TElement) Initial write at Mount. Controlled entries write bare here (no echo suppression — subscription has not yet been wired). Parameters Name Type Description ctrl TControl el TElement Mount(MountContext, TControl, TElement) Spec 047 §14 Phase 3-final — context-carrying Mount overload. Default implementation forwards to the parameterless PropEntry.Mount; entry types that need reconciler/rerender access (e.g. OneWayBridgedPropEntry for Flyout descriptor bridging) override this overload instead. Parameters Name Type Description ctx MountContext ctrl TControl el TElement Update Update(TControl, TElement, TElement) Diff old/new element and apply the minimal write. Controlled entries write through ReactorBinding.WriteSuppressed. Parameters Name Type Description ctrl TControl oldEl TElement newEl TElement Update(UpdateContext, TControl, TElement, TElement) Spec 047 §14 Phase 3-final — context-carrying Update overload. Same forwarding contract as PropEntry.Mount. Parameters Name Type Description ctx UpdateContext ctrl TControl oldEl TElement newEl TElement

content: Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.4) — public author-facing surface for the echo suppression primitive (§13 Q19). Today this delegates to ChangeEchoSuppressor.BeginSuppress; Phase 4 swaps the body for per-control tolerance / coercion metadata as part of the §8 cleanup — the signature does not change. The per-binding wrapper ReactorBinding<TElement> (per spec §4) lands in 1.6; this static class is just the primitive entry point. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls Methods ShouldSuppressEcho Read-side counterpart of ReactorBinding.WriteSuppressed. Call as the first line of a change-event handler: returns true when the current fire is the engine-synthesized echo of a prior WriteSuppressed write against target — consuming one suppression token on that counter-based path — so the handler should return early before invoking the user's callback. It also returns true without consuming a token while inside the non-consuming ApplySetters suppression scope. Returns false for a genuine user interaction (no outstanding token/scope), for a target that is not a FrameworkElement, or when the target carries no Reactor state. This is the public primitive the wrapper generator emits for a [WrapControlled(Deferred = true)] prop, so a deferred-controlled generated wrapper compiles against Reactor's public surface alone (no InternalsVisibleTo) — the read-side gap called out in spec 062 §14. It maps to the counter/scope channel (paired with WriteSuppressed), not the value-diff channel. Parameters Name Type Description target UIElement Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentNullException target is null. WriteSuppressed WriteSuppressed(UIElement, Action) Runs mutate after registering a one-shot suppression token for target. The next change-event handler invocation against target consumes the token via ChangeEchoSuppressor.ShouldSuppress and short-circuits before the user's OnChanged callback fires. No try/finally — the consumption is event-driven and the counter is harmless if a single token is left at +1 after an exceptional path (it gets consumed by the next change event for that control, which by contract should be one the engine itself just provoked). Parameters Name Type Description target UIElement mutate Action WriteSuppressed<T>(T, Action<T>) Typed overload — saves a cast at the call site for the common case where the handler already has a strongly-typed control reference. Parameters Name Type Description target T mutate Action<T> Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentNullException target or mutate is null.

content: One On<Event> method per WinUI true-routed input family (pointer, key, tap, focus). Plain CLR events (Toggled, Click, ValueChanged, TextChanged) go through ReactorBinding.OnCustomEvent; that path stores its delegate in the per-control event payload box (ControlEventStateBox) so pool/recycle correctly clears it. Trampoline-refresh pattern (§3): the handler closure captures ReactorBinding._control but NOT the element. On each event fire, the live element is re-read via Reconciler.GetElementTag; the binding survives re-renders without resubscribing. WriteSuppressed wraps the 1.4 primitive so authors can suppress the next change-event echo on the bound control. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core.V1Protocol. Learn more: Extending Reactor with Native Controls, The Control Reconciler Protocol Properties Control The control the binding is anchored to. Methods OnCustomEvent Spec 047 §9.2 — subscribe to a plain CLR event (Toggled, Click, ValueChanged, TextChanged …). The handler closure re-fetches the live element via Reconciler.GetElementTag on each fire so it survives re-renders. The subscription is anchored to the control's lifetime. The engine's pool reset contract clears the per-control event payload on return, so ported handlers are safe to call this once per Mount. Handlers should NOT call it inside IElementHandler.Update (subscriptions would multiply across renders). content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Remarks A flag lives here only while its feature is rolling out. Once a flag's default flips to true and has soaked for a release, the flag is removed along with the legacy code path it was gating — leaving permanent config knobs here would slow future refactors. Flags are read lazily — changes after a feature has already initialized are not guaranteed to take effect. Tests that need to toggle a flag should save and restore the value around the scope that depends on it. Properties FocusRevalidation When true, stale UseResource entries refetch on window activation / app resume events. Per-resource opt-out is exposed through ResourceOptions.RefetchOnWindowFocus (default false). Remarks Default: false. This mirrors TanStack Query's opt-in posture — window-focus revalidation is surprising in desktop apps where Alt-Tab is a common idiom. HighlightReconcileChanges When true, the reconciler records which UIElements were mounted or modified during each pass and Reactor hosts (ReactorHost and ReactorHostControl, via the shared HighlightOverlayWiring) draw semi-transparent overlays (red = new mount, yellow = property update) so you can visualize reconcile impact. The overlay is rendered via Composition visuals and is hit-test invisible. Remarks Default: false. Intended for interactive debugging sessions. When off, the reconciler skips all collection work so there is zero overhead. UseHookBasedPaging When true, DataGridComponent reads paged data through UseInfiniteResource / UseDataSource instead of the legacy DataPageCache. Part of the Phase-3 migration in docs/specs/020-async-resources-design.md §11. Remarks Default: false. The hook-based path is covered by DataGridParityFixtures but is not yet the default for consumers with custom IDataSource implementations. WarnLayoutFootguns When true, the reconciler emits a one-time diagnostic warning — at mount and on update — for layout "footguns" that silently collapse to 0×0 — most notably an HStack/VStack placed in a Grid GridSize.Auto track with no explicit size and no explicitly-sized children (issue #345). Each warning is written to Debug.WriteLine. Remarks Default: false. In DEBUG builds the detection is always on regardless of this flag — the flag is the opt-in switch for Release builds. When off in Release the detection call site is gated by a single read of this flag per mounted/updated element (the check then no-ops for any non-Grid element), so it is effectively free. Detection runs on both the mount and update reconcile paths, so a warning can appear after a state-driven layout change (e.g. a column flipped to Auto or an explicit size removed), not just on first render. Each distinct offending placement warns at most once per process.
description: Process-wide feature flags that gate risky or in-progress behavior. Each flag is a plain mutable boolean so apps can flip it on startup; the defaults are chosen to preserve existing behavior.
title: ReactorFeatureFlags

content: Split across partial classes, one file per concern, so unrelated changes don't collide: - Reconciler.cs — orchestration: Reconcile entry, components, children, CanUpdate - Reconciler.Mount.cs — Mount() dispatch + composition-primitive handlers - Reconciler.Update.cs — Update() dispatch + composition-primitive handlers - Reconciler.*.cs — one topic each (Modifiers, Keyframes, Transitions, ThemeBindings, Events, Unmount, ReactorState, ...); add code to the matching file Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Learn more: Reconciliation Constructors Reconciler Spec 047 §14 — the V1 protocol is the unconditional production path. The Phase 1 UseV1Protocol feature flag, its AppContext switch, and the descriptor-vs-handler A|B harness ctor were all removed in §4.6 once the legacy MountXxx/UpdateXxx switch was deleted (§4.5). Built-in V1 handlers register automatically into the internal V1HandlerRegistry; external authors add handlers via Reconciler.RegisterHandler / Reconciler.RegisterType (which populate _typeRegistry). Dispatch order is V1 → external → the four composition primitives that sit above the protocol. Parameters Name Type Default Description logger ILogger? null Properties EnableBitmaskDiff LastModifiedElements UIElements that were modified in-place during the last top-level Reconcile pass. Only populated when ReactorFeatureFlags.HighlightReconcileChanges is true; returns an empty list otherwise so callers never see stale data after the flag is toggled off. LastMountedElements UIElements that were newly mounted during the last top-level Reconcile pass. Only populated when ReactorFeatureFlags.HighlightReconcileChanges is true; returns an empty list otherwise so callers never see stale data after the flag is toggled off. Pool The element pool used by this reconciler. Disable via Pool.Enabled = false to prevent recycled controls from retaining stale property state. Methods ApplyDefaultAutomationName Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3) — promoted from internal. Mirrors a control's caption into AutomationProperties.Name when the author has not set one explicitly, so UIA clients that read the attached property directly (not via the peer) still find the name. Provisional API; see REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW. Parameters Name Type Description fe FrameworkElement caption string? ApplyResourceOverrides ApplyResourceOverrides(FrameworkElement, ResourceOverrides?, ResourceOverrides?) Applies per-control resource overrides (lightweight styling) to a FrameworkElement. Literal values are set directly; ThemeRef-based values are resolved from Application.Current.Resources using the element's own effective theme. Parameters Name Type Description fe FrameworkElement oldOverrides ResourceOverrides? newOverrides ResourceOverrides? Remarks Binary-compatible original 3-arg surface (Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3), promoted from private per audit existing-api-surface.md). Delegates to the 4-arg overload with ElementTheme.Default; the reconciler uses the 4-arg form to pass an explicit ancestor-aware theme (needed at mount, before the control is parented). Provisional API; see REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW. ApplyResourceOverrides(FrameworkElement, ResourceOverrides?, ResourceOverrides?, ElementTheme) Applies per-control resource overrides (lightweight styling), resolving ThemeRef-backed values against an explicit effectiveTheme. Provisional API (Spec 047 §14 Phase 1); see REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW. Parameters Name Type Description fe FrameworkElement The control whose Resources receive the overrides. oldOverrides ResourceOverrides? The previously-applied overrides, or null at mount. newOverrides ResourceOverrides? The overrides to apply, or null to clear managed keys. effectiveTheme ElementTheme The ancestor-aware effective theme threaded by the reconciler. When non-Default, ThemeRef-backed overrides resolve their concrete brush against it via ThemeRef.Resolve — necessary at mount, where the element is not yet parented and so an ancestor RequestedTheme is unreachable through fe's own visual-tree walk. Pass ElementTheme.Default to fall back to fe-based resolution (for example, callers of the 3-arg overload). ApplySetters Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3) — promoted from internal. Runs each setter inside the §8.2 echo-suppression scope so user-authored .Set(c => c.IsOn = true) writes don't echo through the engine-wired OnXChanged callback. Provisional API; see REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW. Parameters Name Type Description setters Action<T>[] control T ApplyThemeBindings Applies ThemeRef bindings as a synthesized {ThemeResource}-driven Style. Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3), promoted from private (per audit existing-api-surface.md); provisional API, see REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW. Parameters Name Type Description fe FrameworkElement bindings IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ThemeRef> Remarks WinUI handles theme-reactive resolution natively: the live {ThemeResource} Style setter re-resolves on the control's effective-theme change, which tracks the per-element/inherited ActualTheme (an ancestor RequestedTheme override included), not just the app-level theme. This native self-heal is why a ThemeBindings-only element is safe to structurally skip (#758; empirically verified in ThemeBindingsSkipSelfHealFixtures across immediate and inherited ancestor RequestedTheme toggles). Contrast a ResourceOverrides.ThemeRef, which resolves to a CONCRETE brush at reconcile and does NOT self-heal (so it stays theme-sensitive for the skip gate). A Style already on the control is kept: the themed Style is built BasedOn it, and calling this again re-wraps the same base rather than chaining another level. When that base cannot be a BasedOn of the control's WinUI type (a Style whose TargetType is an app subclass), the themed Style replaces it, as before Styles were kept, and a warning is logged once. Failures are logged, never thrown. DetachReactorState Fully detaches reactor state from a control: nulls the Element and clears the ModifierEventHandlerState's Current* delegates so any already- attached trampoline on the native event source becomes a no-op if it fires. Use when the control leaves reactor's ownership for good (XamlHost / XamlPage unmount) but may remain alive because the app holds a reference — without this, captured closures stay reachable and stale reactor callbacks can still fire. Parameters Name Type Description fe FrameworkElement Dispose Releases the resources that this object holds. FlushConnectedAnimations Starts all queued connected animations. Call AFTER the new tree has been attached to the visual tree (e.g., after Window.Content = newControl). Remarks Source and destination must appear in the SAME reconcile pass — that is the shape Reactor's model produces, since a single state change swaps both subtrees. GetElementTag GetElementTag(FrameworkElement) Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3) — promoted from internal. Provisional API; see REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW. Parameters Name Type Description fe FrameworkElement Remarks For the built-in Flyout, MenuFlyout, and CommandBarFlyout decorators, this reads the target's tag; decorator identity is stored separately. GetElementTag(UIElement) Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3) — promoted from internal. Retrieves the element associated with a control, or null. Provisional API; see REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW. Parameters Name Type Description control UIElement Remarks For the built-in Flyout, MenuFlyout, and CommandBarFlyout decorators, this reads the target's tag; decorator identity is stored separately. Mount Creates a WinUI control tree from an Element tree. Returns null for EmptyElement. Parameters Name Type Description element Element requestRerender Action Reconcile Reconciles one child slot: brings existingControl, the control mounted for oldElement, up to date with newElement, and returns the control the slot should now hold. Parameters Name Type Description oldElement Element? newElement Element? existingControl UIElement? requestRerender Action Remarks When newElement has the element type and key of oldElement, the control is patched in place and returned unchanged, unless the update had to build a new control. In every other case the old control is unmounted before the new one is returned: a changed element type or key, an update that built a new control, or a null or empty newElement, which returns null. Without an existingControl the new element is mounted. Put the result in the slot when it differs from existingControl. A custom control updates the child elements it hosts with this method; in an IElementHandler, UpdateContext.ReconcileChild does the same. RegisterHandler Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.6 / 1.9) — register a v1 IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> for the given element type. Dispatched ahead of Reconciler.RegisterType callbacks. Throws on duplicate (including across registries) and on open-generic element types (spec §13 Q17). Parameters Name Type Description handler IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> Remarks Value-bearing handlers (a control whose programmatic property write raises the same change event as a user edit) must suppress their own write echo with the supported public primitive ReactorBinding<TElement>'s WriteSuppressed method (or the static ReactorBinding); descriptor authors get it via .Controlled / .HandCodedControlled. See IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> and docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md (issue #206). RegisterHandlerForDerivedTypes §14 Phase 3 close-out — register a v1 handler that catches every closed runtime type whose chain reaches TBase. Used by the typed templated-list descriptor ports (TemplatedListViewElement<T> family) so a single registration on a non-generic intermediate base routes every closed-T variant — same T-erasure pattern the legacy Reconciler.Mount switch uses. Exact-type registrations via Reconciler.RegisterHandler always win over a derived-type registration. Throws on duplicate base-type registration. Parameters Name Type Description handler IElementHandler<TBase, TControl> RegisterType Registers a custom element type so the reconciler knows how to mount, update, and unmount it. Registered types take priority over built-in types. Spec 047 §13 Q17 / §14 Phase 1 (1.9) — v1 semantics: - Exact-type lookup via element.GetType(); no base-class fallback. - Throws InvalidOperationException on duplicate registration, including duplicates against a previously-registered V1 handler (V1HandlerRegistry). - Throws on open-generic element types. The mount and update handlers receive the Reconciler instance so they can recursively mount/update/unmount child elements without capturing external state. The reconciler records the element on the control it gets back from mount or update (the element tag) wherever it reads the tag back itself: keyed reconciliation, the unmount lookup, .Ref(...) cleanup and exit transitions. The callbacks don't call Reconciler.SetElementTag for those. Code of your own that reads the element back with Reconciler.GetElementTag, such as an event handler, still tags the control itself. The tag lives on a FrameworkElement. TControl may be declared as UIElement, but in WinUI 3 FrameworkElement is its only subclass, so every control a registration returns is tagged the same way. mount and update are expected to return a control the registration owns. The tag holds one element, so a control that already carries the tag of an element of another type (registration is by exact type, so a derived type counts), for example one mount got from Reconciler.Mount for a child element, keeps that tag: overwriting it would silence that element's own callbacks (the collision issue #942 tracks for target-wrapping decorators). The registration's key, ref, transitions and unmount are not tracked for such a control. To wrap built-in elements, compose them in a component instead. update returns null after patching the control in place; returning the control it was handed means the same. Return a different control only when you replaced it. unmount runs when the reconciler unmounts the control, in place of its own walk over the control's children: a child the callbacks mounted through the reconciler has to be torn down there, for example with Reconciler.UnmountChild. Calling Reconciler.UnmountChild on the control itself from unmount walks its children once rather than calling unmount again. Without an unmount callback the reconciler walks the control's children itself. A control that update replaced is unmounted wherever the reconciler reconciles the slot that holds it: a panel, a Border, a named slot such as SplitView.Pane, a tab's content. A few slots that a control fills by hand still swap a replaced control out without unmount: CommandBar content, Expander content and header template, ContentDialog, Flyout and Popup content, content attached with .WithFlyout, .WithContextFlyout or .WithToolTip(element), and the realized item content of ListView, GridView, TreeView<T> and templated FlipView. Not part of the REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW surface — this is the legacy type-registry path, public since before Spec 047. The §13 Q17 hardening (throw on duplicate, no base-class fallback, no open generics) tightens previously-undefined behavior; it does not change the shape of this API. Parameters Name Type Default Description mount Func<Reconciler, TElement, Action, TControl> update Func<Reconciler, TElement, TElement, TControl, Action, UIElement?> unmount Action<Reconciler, TControl>? null Remarks A value-bearing custom control (one that raises the same change event for a programmatic write as for a user edit) must suppress its own write echo from the update callback. Use the supported public primitive ReactorBinding's WriteSuppressed method — wrap the programmatic write, gate it on an equality check, and pair it 1:1 with the write. For new controls prefer the V1 path: a ControlDescriptor<TElement, TControl> (the primary, descriptor-first authoring shape — its .Controlled / .HandCodedControlled handle echo suppression for you), or a hand-coded IElementHandler<TElement, TControl> via Reconciler.RegisterHandler only for irregular controls (its ReactorBinding<TElement> wraps the same primitive). See docs/guide/extending-reactor-controls.md (issue #206). RentControl Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.5) — rent a control instance, either from the per-type pool (if poolable and a pooled instance is available) or via factory / new T(). Pool key is typeof(T) only. Parameters Name Type Default Description policy PoolPolicy<T>? null factory Func<T>? null ReturnControl Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.5) — return a control to its per-type pool, after running the Q18 reset contract: Clear ControlEventState (per-control event payload box, §9.2). Clear ModifierEventHandlerState (modifier / routed-input handler state). Clear ReactorAttached.StateProperty Tag / DataContext set by Reactor. Invoke policy.Reset last (author-defined extra cleanup). Double-return is safe: ElementPool.Return dedupes via the per-type stack cap (MaxPerType). Parameters Name Type Default Description control T policy PoolPolicy<T>? null SetElementTag Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3) — promoted from internal. Associates a control with its current Reactor element via the ReactorAttached.StateProperty attached DP so that trampolines can resolve the live element on dispatch. Provisional API; see REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW. Parameters Name Type Description control FrameworkElement element Element? UnmountChild Unmounts a child control. Public so registered type handlers can unmount children. Parameters Name Type Description control UIElement UpdateChild Low-level update of one child control, for callers that have already checked the new element can update it in place. Code outside the framework should call Reconciler.Reconcile, which makes that check and unmounts a control it replaces. Parameters Name Type Description oldEl Element newEl Element control UIElement requestRerender Action Remarks Patches control to match newEl and returns null, or returns a new control when the update had to build one. The caller then unmounts control with Reconciler.UnmountChild and puts the new control in its slot, in that order, as Reconciler.Reconcile does: unmounting reads state from the control while it is still in the tree, such as a connected-animation snapshot. It doesn't check that newEl has the element type and key of oldEl: a changed type throws InvalidCastException for a built-in control. The analyzer rule REACTOR_LIFECYCLE_003 flags calls to this method and offers to switch them to Reconciler.Reconcile. UpdateDefaultAutomationName Spec 047 §14 Phase 1 (1.3) — promoted from internal. Update-time pair for Reconciler.ApplyDefaultAutomationName; overwrites the automation Name only when it matches the previous caption (i.e. the author hasn't intervened). Clears that default when the new content has no caption. Provisional API; see REACTOR_V1_PREVIEW. Parameters Name Type Description fe FrameworkElement oldCaption string? newCaption string? Fields DebugElementsDiffed Per-reconcile counters for diagnosing diff and mount/update volume. Reset before each top-level Reconcile() call; read afterward. Always populated (including Release builds) so ETW trace consumers can read them off the ReconcileStop event payload. DebugElementsSkipped DebugUIElementsCreated DebugUIElementsModified

content: Each factory method returns an element record. Most are on Factories, so using static Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Factories; covers them. A factory declared on another class names the using static it needs. Learn more: Components, Advanced Patterns Component Overload Description Component<T>() Embed a Component class as a child element. Usage: Component<MyWidget>() Component<T, TProps>(TProps) Embed a Component class with typed props as a child element. Returns ComponentElement<TProps> so callers can use a record with-expression to produce a modified copy with updated typed props (records are immutable — with clones, it does not mutate). Usage: Component<MyWidget, string>("param") Returns: ComponentElement, ComponentElement<TProps>. Parameters Name Type Description props TProps Empty Renders nothing. Useful as a default/fallback. Returns: Element. ErrorBoundary Overload Description ErrorBoundary(Element, Element) Wraps a child subtree in an error boundary with a static fallback element. ErrorBoundary(Element, Func<Exception, Element>) Wraps a child subtree in an error boundary. If any component in the subtree throws during rendering, the fallback function is called with the exception. When the ErrorBoundary re-renders, it retries the child (error recovery). Returns: ErrorBoundaryElement. Parameters Name Type Description child Element fallback Element or Func<Exception, Element> Expr Inline block-expression escape hatch: invokes render and returns its element, or EmptyElement.Instance when the lambda returns null. Lets callers write multi-statement bodies inside a DSL tree without extracting a local function or relying on the ((Func<Element?>)(() => …))() cast trick. Returns: Element. Parameters Name Type Description render Func<Element?> Remarks Spec 033 §5. Expr performs no memoization, owns no RenderContext, and is not a reconciler boundary — it is purely composition sugar. If the body needs hooks, use Memo(...) or a Component<TProps> instead. Exceptions thrown inside render propagate unchanged so the surrounding error-boundary path applies. Example Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentNullException render is null. ForEach Overload Description ForEach<T>(IEnumerable<T>, Func<T, Element>) Map a list to elements (like .map() in React JSX): ForEach(items, item => TextBlock(item.Name)) When T implements IReactorKeyed, each projected element is keyed from item.Key unless the projection already set one, so the reconciler matches rows by identity instead of by position. ForEach<T>(IEnumerable<T>, Func<T, int, Element>) Map with index: ForEach(items, (item, i) => TextBlock($"{i}: {item}")) Keys from IReactorKeyed items exactly as the single-parameter overload does. Returns: Element. Parameters Name Type Description items IEnumerable<T> render Func<T, Element> or Func<T, int, Element> Group Groups elements without introducing a layout container (like React's Fragment). Children are flattened into the parent container. Returns: Element. Parameters Name Type Description children Element?[] If If/else as an expression: If(loggedIn, () => TextBlock("Welcome"), () => Button("Login", ...)) Returns: Element. Parameters Name Type Default Description condition bool then Func<Element> otherwise Func<Element>? null LocaleProvider Returns: ComponentElement<TProps>. Parameters Name Type Default Description locale string child Element resourceProvider IStringResourceProvider? null defaultLocale string "en-US" pseudoLocalize bool false Memo Overload Description Memo(Func<RenderContext, Element>, object?[]) Define a memoized inline function component. Skips re-render when dependencies haven't changed. Empty deps array = render once + own state changes only. Non-empty = re-render when any dep changes. Usage: Memo(ctx => TextBlock("stable"), someProp, otherProp) Memo<TKey>(TKey, Func<Element>) Opt-in typed keyed memo for virtualized rows (issue #327). Wrap a row body in Memo(key, () => …) to assert the body is a pure function of key. Inside a virtualized list (VirtualList, LazyVStack<T>, …) the owning ElementFactory<T> caches the built element per key in a bounded LRU, so a container recycle that re-asks for the same key returns the same element instance — the reconciler then skips the row's rebuild + per-row diff entirely (sub-µs). This targets the fast-scroll cost of variable-height rows, where every recycle otherwise rebuilds and diffs the row from scratch. Usage: renderItem: i => Memo(items[i].Id, () => Border(BigVariableHeightRow(items[i]))) Purity is your responsibility. The key must capture every input the factory reads. If the body also depends on, say, a selection flag, fold it into the key: Memo((items[i].Id, isSelected), () => …). Closing over unkeyed mutable state will serve stale content. The cache is cleared automatically when the list's items/renderItem change. Apply modifiers inside the factory, not on the wrapper. The cross-recycle cache only unwraps a bare Memo(key, …) — one with no fluent modifiers, no .WithKey(…), and no attached state (Grid/Canvas attached properties, .Provide(…) context, or theme bindings) on the wrapper itself. Decorating the wrapper (Memo(id, () => …).Padding(8)) opts the row out of caching and silently loses the perf benefit; put modifiers on the element the factory returns instead: Memo(id, () => Border(…).Padding(8)). Outside a virtualized factory the wrapper is transparent but keyed: a re-render with the same key is a no-op (the factory is not re-invoked and the inner subtree is not diffed), while a changed key replaces the inner (unmount + fresh mount of the new factory output). The exception is a component inside the subtree that updates its own state: the factory then runs again so the reconciler can walk down to that component. The cross-recycle cache only applies on the virtualized-list path. It is always safe to use anywhere an element is expected. Returns: MemoElement, KeyedMemoElement. Parameters Name Type Description render Func<RenderContext, Element> dependencies object?[] key TKey Stable identity that fully determines factory's output. factory Func<Element> Builds the row element. Invoked once per key on a cache miss. Type parameters Name Description TKey Key type. Boxed to Object and compared with Object.Equals / Object.GetHashCode, so value keys (ints, strings, records, value tuples) dedupe by value. This is what lets the int-index VirtualList path hit the cache. PropertyGrid Creates a PropertyGrid element for editing the target object's properties. Keyed by target type so switching between different target types creates a fresh component (avoiding broken reconciliation of different structures). Returns: ComponentElement<TProps>. Parameters Name Type Default Description target object registry TypeRegistry onRootChanged Action<object>? null RenderEachTime Define an inline function component that re-renders on every parent render (no memoization), keeping its own hook scope. Made explicit so the reader can tell the always-re-render case apart from a missing deps array. Returns: FuncElement. Parameters Name Type Description render Func<RenderContext, Element> Remarks Spec 033 §4. Use sparingly — components that re-render on every parent render defeat the memoization story and can amplify render storms. Prefer Memo with an explicit deps array whenever the re-render trigger can be enumerated. VirtualList Creates a VirtualList element — a count-based virtualized list. Items are rendered on demand via the renderItem callback. Returns: ComponentElement<TProps>. Parameters Name Type Default Description itemCount int renderItem Func<int, Element> getItemKey Func<int, string>? null itemHeight double? null estimatedItemHeight double 40 spacing double 0 ref Action<VirtualListRef>? null onVisibleRangeChanged Action<int, int>? null When Renders element only when condition is true. Reads nicely: When(items.Any(), () => TextBlock("Has items")) Returns: Element. Parameters Name Type Description condition bool then Func<Element>

content: Hooks are how Reactor components subscribe to state, schedule effects, and reach into the framework's lifecycle from a function-shaped Render body. Call them on the RenderContext (or from a Component), always in the same order, and never inside a condition or a loop. Learn more: Hooks, Effects and Lifecycle, Rules of Reactor State Hooks that keep values between renders. Hook Description UseCollection Subscribes to an ObservableCollection and re-renders on Add/Remove/Reset. UseExternalStore Subscribes to an external store that exposes a current snapshot getter. UseObservable Subscribes to an INotifyPropertyChanged source and re-renders when any property changes. UseObservableProperty Subscribes to a specific property on an INotifyPropertyChanged source. UseObservableTree Observes an object and all nested INotifyPropertyChanged values reachable through its properties. UsePersisted Like UseState, but the value survives unmount/remount via an in-memory cache. UseReducer Declares a piece of state with a functional updater variant. UseRef Returns a mutable ref object that persists across renders. UseState Declares a piece of state. Effects and memoization Hooks that run side effects or cache values between renders. content: Learn more: Hooks PendingComponent Component backing the Pending element. Hosts a PendingScope, subscribes to its PendingScope.Changed event, and chooses between PendingProps.Fallback and PendingProps.Child. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hooks. Inherits from Component<TProps>. Remarks The child subtree is always rendered. When the scope reports any loading resource, the child's Visibility is flipped to Collapsed and the fallback is shown instead. Because the subtree stays mounted, its hooks keep running, their fetches complete in the background, and the UI swaps to the real content on the next render frame after the scope reports clean. Constructors PendingComponent Methods Render PendingFactory Entry-point factory for the Pending bubble-up element. See docs/specs/020-async-resources-design.md §10 for the full mechanism. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hooks. Methods Pending Wraps child with a fresh PendingScope. Renders fallback instead of child while any UseResource/UseInfiniteResource in the subtree is in the Loading state. Reloading(previous) does not trigger the fallback — spec §10.1. Parameters Name Type Description fallback Element child Element Remarks The child subtree is always mounted so its hooks register with the scope. The element simply chooses which rendered tree to show — there is no unwinding of rendering, and no reconciler involvement. Marked [ReactorSourceTransparent] (see ReactorSourceTransparentAttribute, spec 010) because it is a pure forwarder: the element is really built by the Component<,> call on the next line, inside Reactor's own assembly, where no consumer call site exists to intercept. Without the annotation a Pending(...) element reports no location at all. With it, the interceptor in the consumer's compilation stamps the line they wrote Pending( on, which is the answer they were looking for. PendingProps Props for PendingComponent. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hooks. Constructors PendingProps Props for PendingComponent. Parameters Name Type Description Fallback Element Child Element Properties Child Fallback PendingScope Shared loading-state ref-count consumed by the Pending element and populated by UseResource / UseInfiniteResource hooks inside the scope. When the scope observes any registered resource in the Loading state (not Reloading), the owning Pending element renders its fallback instead of the child subtree. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hooks. Remarks Semantics. Only Loading triggers the fallback — spec §10.1. A Reloading(previous) is "we already have something to show" and the subtree continues to render normally. Threading. All members are thread-safe. PendingScope.Changed fires on the thread that caused the mutation — consumers (typically Pending's re-render trigger) marshal it to the dispatcher themselves. Scope nesting. Each Pending provides a fresh scope to its subtree, so nested Pendings are independent. A hook registers only with its nearest ancestor scope. Constructors PendingScope Properties AnyLoading True iff any tracked token is currently Loading. Count Snapshot the number of registered tokens (loading or not). Diagnostic only. Methods Register Start tracking token with the given initial isLoading state. A hook typically uses its own this-equivalent as the token. Parameters Name Type Description token object isLoading bool SetLoading Update token's loading state. Silently ignored if the token was never registered (defensive — avoids forcing the caller to track whether they registered). Parameters Name Type Description token object isLoading bool Unregister Stop tracking token. Idempotent. Parameters Name Type Description token object Events Changed Fires when a resource joins, leaves, or changes its loading state.

content: Processes a Command for use in a component. Always consumes a stable hook shape (independent of whether the command is sync/async or debounced), so a command at a given call site can flip between sync↔async or Command.DebounceMs 0↔N across renders without ever reordering hook slots. For a pure sync command with no Command.DebounceMs the original command is returned unchanged (identity preserved). For async commands, wraps ExecuteAsync with automatic IsExecuting tracking and re-entrance guards. When Command.DebounceMs > 0, wraps the dispatch with a leading-edge debounce: a fire within the window of the prior accepted fire is dropped and Command.IsDebouncing (hence Command.IsEnabled=false) reflects the window so the bound control disables, re-enabling when the window elapses. The returned command has a sync Execute action, ExecuteAsync = null, and preserves the authored DebounceMs value (re-passing it through UseCommand is a no-op — debounce is never applied twice). content: Declared on RenderContext. Learn more: Reactivity Model, Hooks Parameters Name Type Default Description subscribe Func<Action, Action> getSnapshot Func<TSnapshot> comparer IEqualityComparer<TSnapshot>? null Remarks subscribe is the effect dependency that decides whether the subscription is torn down and re-established, so it must be a stable delegate across renders. Pass a method group (e.g. store.Subscribe) or a UseCallback-memoized delegate. A fresh capturing lambda (onChanged => store.Subscribe(onChanged)) is a new delegate every render and will unsubscribe/resubscribe on each one. This mirrors React's guidance for useSyncExternalStore. getSnapshot must return a cached/stable value that only changes identity when the underlying data changes. Returning a fresh, never-equal value on every call (e.g. () => items.ToArray()) combined with an unstable subscribe can spin: re-render re-runs the effect, the immediate re-check observes a "change", and that forces another render. Memoize the snapshot or return a value the supplied comparer treats as equal when nothing changed. Use from a class component Class components can call the same hook directly. content: Memoize cell construction for items. On the first render the builder runs for every index; on subsequent renders, an item that compares Object.Equals against the previous render's value at the same index reuses the previous element. Any change to dependencies invalidates the entire cache and rebuilds every cell. An extension method on RenderContext, declared in UseMemoCellsExtensions. Learn more: Hooks, Performance Parameters Name Type Description items IReadOnlyList<T> Source items, one cell per item. builder Func<T, int, Element> Builder for a single cell. Must be a pure function of (item, index) plus dependencies. Closure captures missing from the deps list are flagged by the REACTOR_HOOKS_007 analyzer. dependencies object[] Trailing-params list of values the builder closes over. content: Memoize cell construction when the data source already knows which indices changed. Skips the per-cell Object.Equals scan entirely; the builder runs only for indices in changedIndices. When the item count changes between renders the overload falls back to a full rebuild (changedIndices is treated as "rebuild everything") because the index space no longer matches the prior render. Callers whose lists grow or shrink frequently will get better incremental reuse from UseMemoCells or UseMemoCellsByKey, both of which can short-circuit per-cell on value or key equality across length changes. On the steady-state path (unchanged count) the returned array reuses the previous render's element instance for every index NOT named in changedIndices, and publishes a positional structural-skip hint (Spec 034 §C) keyed by reference on that array so the reconciler can update only the changed cells and skip the reference-equal remainder. The returned array is therefore the hook's retained memoized state AND the key of that hint: treat it as immutable and declare every change through a subsequent render's changedIndices (React-style immutability — see AGENTS.md "Never mutate"). Mutating an unchanged slot in place both corrupts the memo's view of the previous render and can cause the reconciler to skip the mutated cell. An extension method on RenderContext, declared in UseMemoCellsExtensions. Learn more: Hooks, Performance Parameters Name Type Description items IReadOnlyList<T> Source items. changedIndices IReadOnlyList<int> Indices whose item differs from the previous render. Negative indices and indices >= items.Count throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Duplicate indices are a caller-contract violation but are tolerated: they are de-duplicated before the named cells are rebuilt, so each cell is rebuilt exactly once and the structural-skip hint's theme tally stays exact. builder Func<T, int, Element> Cell builder; same contract as UseMemoCells. dependencies object[] Trailing-params deps. Remarks Spec 034 §C. A cell is "theme-sensitive" when it carries ThemeBindings or a ThemeRef-backed ResourceOverride; the hook tracks how many cells are theme-sensitive (carried forward incrementally) so the reconciler falls back to the full walk — which re-resolves themed brushes against the current effective theme — instead of structurally skipping such a range. Use from a class component Class components can call the same hook directly. These overloads forward to the ones above:
title: UseMemoCellsByIndex

content: Open or reuse a secondary window keyed by key. Renders that pass the same key share the same ReactorWindow; if the spec changes across renders the live window is updated via ReactorWindow.Update. The returned handle is identity-stable across renders so long as the key is stable. Declared on RenderContext. Learn more: Windows, Hooks Parameters Name Type Description key WindowKey spec WindowSpec factory Func<Component> Remarks Unmount semantics: when the calling component unmounts, the opened window stays open. Components that want the inverse behavior must close the window explicitly — e.g. by registering a UseEffect cleanup that calls ReactorWindow.Close on the returned handle. (spec 036 §4.3 / §15.6) Note — asymmetry with UseTrayIcon: tray icons are component-scoped and close on unmount; opened windows are app-scoped and survive unmount. The asymmetry is deliberate (a window is normally expected to outlive the menu item that opened it, while a tray icon belongs to the component that declared it), so the two hooks behave inversely despite the matching naming. Returns null when no UI dispatcher has been captured — happens in unit-test contexts where no ReactorApp.Run is in flight. In production this is unreachable. content: When threadSafe is true, reads and writes are synchronized with a per-hook lock so concurrent setter calls from many threads serialize. When false (default), cross-thread setter calls are auto-marshaled onto the captured UI dispatcher — the write and the rerender both run on the UI thread, so background-thread setters from Task.Run, PeriodicTimer, or callbacks after await … ConfigureAwait(false) work correctly without any extra opt-in. Use threadSafe: true when you need many concurrent setters to apply in-place (i.e., without an intervening UI thread hop) or when the setter result must be visible to its caller before the next UI tick. File pickers Options for the open file, save file and folder pickers. Launch and activation How the app was started, and requests to embed it. Parameters Name Type Description Kind LaunchKind Arguments string? Files IReadOnlyList<string> Properties Arguments Files Kind Normal Sentinel for Phase 1, when no real activation parsing exists yet. Methods TryResolve Resolve LaunchActivation.Arguments as a deep-link URI through the supplied DeepLinkMap<TRoute>. Returns true only when LaunchActivation.Arguments is non-empty and the map matched a registered pattern. The shell-launch convention for Reactor is that jump-list / tray / thumbnail-toolbar entries carry deep-link URIs in their argument strings (see JumpListItem.ForUri); this helper plumbs that convention into the navigation system. Remarks The OS shell presents jump-list entries, tray "Open" / double-click commands, and thumbnail-toolbar buttons as plain process re-launches — all three arrive at OnLaunched with the same shape (a non-empty argument string and no extended activation kind). Reactor cannot distinguish them from the WinUI surface, so all three roll up under LaunchKind.JumpList. Apps that need finer granularity should encode it in the argument URI itself (e.g. a path prefix or query parameter) and inspect LaunchActivation.Arguments.
