content: Learn more: Persistence ApplicationPersistedScope Process-lifetime persisted-state scope (spec 033 §2). Replaces the previous ConcurrentDictionary-based reject-on-full implementation with an LRU-bounded scope that: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Remarks The legacy internal-static PersistedStateCache shim is preserved for callers inside this assembly, delegating to ApplicationPersistedScope.Default. Constructors ApplicationPersistedScope Parameters Name Type Description capacity int Properties Capacity Count Default Process-wide singleton instance. Methods ApplyMemoryPressureTrim Public for tests: trim to 25% of capacity. Production callers use the memory-pressure event; tests invoke this directly to exercise the shrink path without depending on the OS callback. Dispose Releases the resources that this object holds. Remove Parameters Name Type Description key string Set Parameters Name Type Description key string value T Trim Trims to the given target count. Exposed publicly so tests and callers that need a clean slate (e.g. test harnesses between cases) can drive the cache below its 25%-of-capacity memory-pressure floor without disposing the singleton. Parameters Name Type Description targetCount int TryGet Parameters Name Type Description key string value T Fields DefaultCapacity Default capacity for the singleton process-wide scope. IPersistedStateScope A keyed object cache used by UsePersisted. Two implementations: ApplicationPersistedScope (process-global, LRU-bounded, memory-pressure-aware) and WindowPersistedScope (host-scoped, LRU-bounded, disposed on host unload). Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Remarks Spec 033 §2. UsePersisted hooks consult these scopes at hook-entry time on the UI thread; the underlying LruCache synchronizes its own mutations so background-thread invalidations (memory pressure events) are safe. Properties Capacity The maximum number of entries this scope retains. Count The number of entries currently held in the scope. Methods Remove Removes the entry under key, if any. Parameters Name Type Description key string Set Stores value under key. Promotes the entry to MRU. When the scope is at capacity, evicts the LRU entry before inserting (no refusal). Parameters Name Type Description key string value T TryGet Try to read a previously-stored value for key. Returns false when the key is absent or the stored value is not assignable to T. Reads promote the entry to MRU. Parameters Name Type Description key string value T IWindowPersistenceStore Storage adapter for WindowSpec.PersistenceId. Implementations retain opaque per-id byte payloads; Reactor handles the serialization shape (WINDOWPLACEMENT + monitor-layout fingerprint). (spec 036 §8) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting.Persistence. Remarks Implementations must be thread-safe for concurrent reads from arbitrary threads (Reactor reads on the UI thread today, but production callers may share a store across multiple processes / consoles). Writes happen on the UI thread on close. Implementations must never throw into the caller. Read failures return false with the out-parameter data set to null; write failures are swallowed with a diagnostic log line. Reactor treats the store as best-effort — a corrupt or missing entry simply falls back to the spec's default placement. Methods TryRead Try to read the payload stored under id. Returns true when an entry exists and was deserialized successfully. Parameters Name Type Description id string data byte[]? Write Persist data under id. Best effort — implementations must not throw. Parameters Name Type Description id string data byte[] JsonFileStore Default unpackaged-app persistence store. Writes a JSON document (one base64 string per persistence id) to %LOCALAPPDATA%/<ProcessName>/reactor-windows.json. Atomic via write-then-rename; bounded at JsonFileStore.MaxFileSizeBytes (1 MB) on read to refuse pathological payloads. (spec 036 §8 / §0.5) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting.Persistence. Remarks Read failures (missing file, malformed JSON, oversize) return false from JsonFileStore.TryRead with no exception bubbling out — the spec calls for "warn-and-default" semantics on corruption. Writes are best-effort and survive disk-full / permission denied without throwing. Concurrency. Read-merge-write is serialized two ways: an in-process lock orders threads sharing an instance, and a named CrossProcessWriteGuard extends that ordering across separate instances and separate processes. Without the latter, two writers could each read the pre-merge document and the second rename would silently discard the first's entry — even when the two wrote different persistence ids. Each write stages through a temp file named for the writing process and thread, so a crash mid-write cannot leave a shared temp that another process renames over the real file. Readers take no guard, but they do open with FileShare.Delete in addition to FileShare.Read, and the commit uses File.Replace rather than File.Move(overwrite: true). Measured on Windows: Move cannot replace a destination any process still holds open — it fails even when that reader granted delete sharing — whereas Replace succeeds precisely when the reader does grant it. Both halves are required; with only one, a concurrent reader in a second app instance silently kills the write, because write failures are swallowed by contract. The reader then continues against the file it opened, seeing either the previous document or the next one, never a torn one. Constructors JsonFileStore JsonFileStore() Construct the default unpackaged store rooted at %LOCALAPPDATA%/<ProcessName>/reactor-windows.json. JsonFileStore(string) Construct with an explicit file path. Used by unit tests. Parameters Name Type Description path string Properties Path The on-disk file path. Methods DefaultPath Compute the default unpackaged-store path. Uses a sanitized process name segment so a process named foo/bar can't traverse out of LocalAppData. (spec 036 §0.5 / §9.5) TryRead Parameters Name Type Description id string data byte[]? Write Parameters Name Type Description id string data byte[] Fields MaxFileSizeBytes Hard ceiling on the persistence file size. A 1 MB cap is generous — real-world payloads are ~80 bytes per window — and rejects pathological payloads from a tampered file. (spec 036 §0.5) PackagedSettingsStore Default packaged-app persistence store. Routes through ApplicationData.Current.LocalSettings using a "Reactor" container and WindowPersistence_<id> keys. These differ from WinUIEx's container and keys, so placements saved by WinUIEx are not picked up. (spec 036 §8) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting.Persistence. Remarks Constructing this store from an unpackaged process throws on first access (the WinRT API requires package identity). Callers must check PackagedSettingsStore.IsAvailable before instantiating, or fall back to JsonFileStore. All read failures (missing key, type mismatch) return false; write failures are swallowed with a stderr diagnostic. Constructors PackagedSettingsStore Methods IsAvailable Detect whether the current process has WinRT package identity. Constructing PackagedSettingsStore in an unpackaged context still works at construction time; this static check lets auto-detection logic pick the right default. TryRead Parameters Name Type Description id string data byte[]? Write Parameters Name Type Description id string data byte[] PersistedScope Selector for the lifetime/visibility scope of UsePersisted values. Spec 033 §2. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Values Name Value Description Window 0 Bound to the lifetime of the hosting ReactorHost or ReactorHostControl. State is dropped when the host unloads. Recommended default for new code. Application 1 Process-lifetime. State persists across windows in the same process. Replaces the legacy default (which was implicit application-scope). UnpackagedAppDataStore Unpackaged-app persistence store backed by the Windows App SDK's first-class app-data root, Microsoft.Windows.Storage.ApplicationData.GetForUnpackaged() (Windows App SDK ≥ 2.2.0). Persists to <ApplicationData.LocalPath>/reactor-windows.json. (spec 063 §4) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting.Persistence. Remarks Opt-in. Auto-detection still selects JsonFileStore for unpackaged processes; assign an instance to ReactorApp.WindowPersistenceStore before the first OpenWindow to use this one instead. The two stores key their data differently — this one by the publisher/product pair you supply, JsonFileStore by the entry process's name — so switching does not migrate an existing app's saved layouts. (spec 063 §6, D2 / D3) Why the path surface and not LocalSettings. This store uses ApplicationData.LocalPath and deliberately does not use the sibling LocalSettings key/value surface. On the runtime this repo pins, GetForUnpackaged().LocalSettings opens HKCU\SOFTWARE\<publisher>\<product> — a roaming hive — rather than the machine-local HKCU\SOFTWARE\Classes\Local Settings\Software\… it is contracted to use (WindowsAppSDK issue 6559, RuntimeCompatibilityChange ApplicationData_GetForUnpackaged_LocalSettings). Window placement is monitor-topology- and DPI-dependent, so roaming it between a user's machines restores windows onto monitors that do not exist there. LocalPath resolves under %LOCALAPPDATA%, which does not roam. (spec 063 §3.1) That behaviour is a property of the installed 2.x Windows App Runtime, which services in place, rather than of the SDK version an app pins — so it can differ machine to machine for the same build. LocalPath has no such variance, which is a second reason this store is built on it. (spec 063 §3.2) Concurrency. Safe to share across instances and processes: the underlying JsonFileStore serializes read-merge-write with a named cross-process guard. That matters more for this store than for JsonFileStore's own default path, because this identity is deliberately shared — two differently-named executables from one publisher/product resolve the same file, where the process-name-keyed default would have given them separate ones. (spec 063 §5) Read/write failures follow the IWindowPersistenceStore "warn-and-default" contract — they never throw into the caller. The constructor may throw, matching JsonFileStore: an invalid publisher/product is an authoring error, not a runtime condition. Constructors UnpackagedAppDataStore Resolve the Windows App SDK app-data root for publisher/product and persist beneath it. Parameters Name Type Description publisher string Publisher segment of the app-data root. The SDK validates this and rejects path-traversal, rooted, and empty values with an ArgumentException; Reactor does not sanitize it further. product string Product segment of the app-data root. Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentException publisher or product is empty, or the SDK rejected it as invalid. Methods TryRead Parameters Name Type Description id string data byte[]? Write Parameters Name Type Description id string data byte[] WindowPersistedScope Per-host (per-window) persisted-state scope. Owned by a ReactorHost / ReactorHostControl and disposed when the host unloads — so window-scoped state is bounded by window lifetime, not process lifetime. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Remarks Spec 033 §2. Bounded LRU (default capacity 1024). Window-scoped state is the recommended default for new UsePersisted calls because most apps want "preserved across an unmount/remount within this window" rather than "preserved across every window in the process." Memory-pressure registration is deliberately omitted — the lifetime is already bounded by the host. Remove Parameters Name Type Description key string Set Parameters Name Type Description key string value T TryGet Parameters Name Type Description key string value T Fields DefaultCapacity Default capacity for a per-window scope.

content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Learn more: Windows Properties ActiveHost Legacy alias for the host of the first window opened in this process. (spec 036 §4.3 / §12.4) Obsolete. Use ReactorApp.PrimaryWindow.Host or ReactorApp.Windows. AppLogger DefaultRenderErrorHandler App-wide replacement for the built-in render-error fallback, which shows the full exception text (type, message, stack trace). null (the default) keeps the built-in fallback. (issue #1291) Remarks Consulted at error time by every ReactorHost and ReactorHostControl that has no handler of its own — including windows opened after this is set, tray flyouts, and embedded host controls. A host overrides it with ReactorHost.RenderErrorHandler, and a window with WindowSpec.RenderErrorHandler. Covers every place Reactor catches a render-time exception outside an ErrorBoundary: the root render, child component renders, the reconcile pass, effect flushes, and effect cleanups during dispose. See RenderErrorHandler. DevtoolsEnabled PrimaryWindow The first window opened during this process's startup callback, or null when none has been opened (tray-only / pre-startup). ShutdownPolicy Process-shutdown policy. Defaults to ShutdownPolicy.OnPrimaryWindowClosed. Remarks Settable from any thread and at any point in the process lifetime, and read back immediately. Reactor takes ownership of the event loop at startup (see ReactorApp.TakeOwnershipOfDispatcherLifetime), so this value is consulted when a decision is due rather than mirrored into platform state — there is no window in which the policy and the platform can disagree. Two moments consult it. A surface close reaches ReactorApp.EvaluateShutdownPolicy, which reads the value then, so a change made any time beforehand counts. Startup is the exception: ReactorApp.ExitIfStartupOpenedNoSurface runs the instant the launch path finishes, so a zero-surface startup is judged against whatever the policy holds at that instant. Set it before Run, or on the UI thread before the startup callback returns — a write posted from another thread during startup can land too late to be seen. TrayIcons Snapshot of every open ReactorTrayIcon. Copy-on-write; safe to enumerate from any thread. (spec 036 §11.4) UIDispatcher The UI DispatcherQueue captured at OnLaunched — null until the first window has been bootstrapped. WindowPersistenceStore Process-wide store backing WindowSpec.PersistenceId. Defaults are picked lazily on first window open: packaged apps get PackagedSettingsStore; unpackaged apps get JsonFileStore. Setting this property after the first OpenWindow throws — windows that already loaded their placement from the previous store would get a half-populated state. (spec 036 §8) Remarks Unpackaged apps can opt into UnpackagedAppDataStore by assigning one here before the first OpenWindow. It persists under the Windows App SDK's app-data root for an explicit publisher/product pair instead of the entry process's name, so saved layouts survive an executable rename. It is not the auto-detected default because the two stores key their data differently, so switching does not migrate existing saved layouts. (spec 063 §4) Windows Snapshot of every open ReactorWindow. Copy-on-write; safe to enumerate from any thread. Methods Exit Exit the process. UI-thread only. With exitCode set to its default (0), routes through Application.Exit so WinUI gets a clean unwind. With a non-zero exit code, calls Application.Exit first to release resources, then Environment.Exit with the requested code so the parent process sees it (assigning Environment.ExitCode would only take effect on a natural managed-entry-point return, which an app under Application.Start does not perform). Parameters Name Type Default Description exitCode int 0 FindTrayIcon Look up an open tray icon by WindowKey. Parameters Name Type Description key WindowKey FindWindow Look up an open window by WindowKey. Parameters Name Type Description key WindowKey OpenTrayIcon Open a system-tray icon. UI-thread only. The returned handle stays alive until ReactorTrayIcon.Close / ReactorTrayIcon.Dispose is called or the process exits. (spec 036 §11.4) Parameters Name Type Description spec TrayIconSpec OpenWindow OpenWindow(WindowSpec, Func<Component>, Action<ReactorHost>?) Open a window with a Component root. UI-thread only. (spec 036 §4.3) Parameters Name Type Default Description spec WindowSpec Declarative description of the window's chrome. root Func<Component> Factory invoked once to materialize the root component. configure Action<ReactorHost>? null Optional callback invoked on the UI thread before the root mounts. Use it for pre-mount setup that needs the live ReactorHost (logger wiring, custom reconciler registrations, host-level event hooks). Parameters Name Type Default Description spec WindowSpec render Func<RenderContext, Element> configure Action<ReactorHost>? null RegisterAllBuiltIns Registers every built-in Reactor control handler with the global ControlRegistry in one call. Remarks When to call. Call this once at process startup if your app constructs element records directly (the new TextBlockElement(…) { … } hot-loop idiom documented in docs/guide/advanced.md "Hot loops") rather than exclusively through factory methods. Factory methods already self-register on first call, so an app that only ever builds UI through the fluent/factory DSL does not need this. Trimming. This method is the deliberate opt-out of spec-048's lazy-registration trim story: calling it roots the entire built-in catalog, so a NativeAOT/trimmed build that calls it keeps every built-in handler and WinUI control. Apps that want a minimal trimmed binary should not call this and instead let each factory register only the controls it uses — or register specific controls explicitly: ControlRegistry.Register for control-backed handlers, or ControlRegistry.RegisterDecorator for decorator-backed elements (overlays, validation, composite wrappers). Because this is an ordinary method (not a [ModuleInitializer]), the trimmer removes it — and everything it names — when it is unreachable. Registration is idempotent and process-wide; calling it more than once is a cheap no-op after the first call. RegisterControlAssembly RegisterControlAssembly(IXamlMetadataProvider) Registers a XAML metadata provider so its types are visible to the WinUI XAML loader for this process. Required when a third-party control library is referenced from a Reactor app that has no XAML files of its own (and therefore no compiler-generated provider that would auto-chain to the library). Call before ReactorApp.Run. Idempotent (same instance is added at most once) and thread-safe. See https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/142. Parameters Name Type Description provider IXamlMetadataProvider RegisterControlAssembly(Assembly) Convenience overload that locates the XAML-compiler-generated IXamlMetadataProvider in assembly (the type the XAML compiler emits when the project has at least one XAML file) and registers it. Throws if no such provider is found — pass the IXamlMetadataProvider instance directly if your library uses a non-standard provider type. Reflection discovery does not preserve the provider under trimming/NativeAOT; use the instance overload with a statically constructed provider in that case. Parameters Name Type Description assembly Assembly Run Run(Action<ReactorAppContext>) Multi-window startup entry. The startup callback runs on the UI thread after WinUI bootstraps and before any default window is opened. Open windows or tray icons (Phase 8) directly from inside the callback. Launches the app with a full WindowSpec for the primary window, so it gets the same declarative surface as a secondary window opened via ReactorApp.OpenWindow — icon, min/max size, backdrop, corner style, start position, and placement persistence. Run(WindowSpec, Func<RenderContext, Element>, Action<ReactorHost>?) Launches the app with a render function and a full WindowSpec for the primary window. See ReactorApp.Run for the spec semantics. Parameters Name Type Default Description spec WindowSpec rootRender Func<RenderContext, Element> configure Action<ReactorHost>? null Run<TRoot>(string, double?, double?, bool, WindowIcon?, Action<ReactorHost>?) Launches the app. width / height are DIPs; leave them null (the default) to let the OS pick the initial window size, exactly as a plain XAML Window does. Enable the Reactor.DevtoolsSupport runtime host configuration switch in DEBUG builds to allow the mur devtools / --devtools surface: component switching via VS Code, MCP agent tools, and component listing. Use an .ico: build it with WindowIcon.FromPath for a file beside the app, or WindowIcon.FromResource for a packaged ms-appx:/// asset. When omitted, Reactor falls back to Assets\AppIcon.ico and then to the executable's embedded icon. Distinct from TitleBar(...).Icon(...), which sets the app mark drawn inside the window. Note that in a packaged app this does not change the taskbar button or Task Manager — the shell draws those from package identity and the manifest's Square44x44Logo; see WindowSpec.Icon. configure Action<ReactorHost>? null Optional callback invoked on the UI thread before the root mounts. content: The argument to ReactorApp.Run's startup callback. Carries the launch activation; all surface-management operations (open / find a window or tray icon, register events) go directly through the static ReactorApp API — call sites mix freely. (spec 036 §4.3) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Learn more: Windows Remarks Keep the context small on purpose: the static ReactorApp surface is the single source of truth for windows / tray icons / shutdown policy, and remains valid before Run enters this callback and after it returns. Doubling the API on the context just doubled the discovery cost without adding capability. Properties LaunchActivation How the process was launched. See LaunchActivation.

If set, called before deciding whether to handle. Return true to mark the exception as handled; return false (or leave null) to let it crash. That call is made by Reactor itself, not by WinUI, so it happens even when the app's Application is not a ReactorApplication (for example a XAML app hosting ReactorHostControl). Learn more: Reactor for XAML Developers Constructors ReactorHost Parameters Name Type Default Description window Window logger ILogger? null Properties ContentTarget Optional: when set, Reactor renders into this Border instead of Window.Content. Useful for embedding Reactor content in a pre-existing layout (e.g., a test harness with a persistent TitleBar). Mirrors the early-out predicate inside ReactorHost.WaitForIdleAsync; exposed so test harnesses can drive bounded-convergence wait loops without polling the same fields reflectively. The renderPending read uses Volatile.Read so off-thread callers see a stable snapshot of the Interlocked-managed field. A disposed host reports idle (nothing left to render, ever) to match the disposed-arm short-circuit in ReactorHost.WaitForIdleAsync; otherwise convergence loops would spin to their pass cap during/after host teardown and emit misleading non-idle diagnostics. content: Usage in XAML (xmlns:reactor="using:Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting"): <reactor:ReactorHostControl ComponentType="local:StatsCard" /> — or declare an empty host and mount it from code-behind — <reactor:ReactorHostControl x:Name="reactorHost" /> Usage in code-behind: reactorHost.Mount(new MyComponent()); — or — reactorHost.Mount(ctx => VStack(TextBlock("Hello from Reactor!"))); — or — reactorHost.ComponentFactory = () => new MyComponent(); Features: - Thread-safe render batching (setState from any thread) - Low-priority re-enqueue so layout/paint/input aren't starved - Render performance stats (FPS, frame timing) - Automatic theme change detection and re-render - Connected animation flushing - Error boundary with fallback UI - Clean lifecycle via Loaded/Unloaded Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting. Inherits from ContentControl. Learn more: Reactor for XAML Developers Constructors ReactorHostControl ReactorHostControl() Creates an empty host. This is the constructor XAML uses (<reactor:ReactorHostControl ... />); set ReactorHostControl.ComponentType or ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory, or call Mount, to give it a root. ReactorHostControl(Component?, ILogger?) Parameters Name Type Default Description component Component? null logger ILogger? null Properties ComponentFactory Factory to create the root component. Set this or use Mount() for more control. If set, the component is created and mounted when the control is Loaded. Example: ComponentFactory = () => new MyComponent(); ComponentType The root component's type, for declaring a host in XAML: <reactor:ReactorHostControl ComponentType="local:StatsCard" />. When the control is Loaded and nothing has been mounted, an instance is created and mounted, receiving ReactorHostControl.Props like a ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory root. ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory wins when both are set. Remarks The instance is created through the app's XAML type information (Application.Current as IXamlMetadataProvider), not reflection: naming a type in markup makes the XAML compiler generate an activator for its public parameterless constructor, so this stays trim- and AOT-safe. A type that is only ever assigned from code has no such entry, and the host shows an error saying so in place of the root; set ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory there instead. Read once, at Loaded, like ReactorHostControl.ComponentFactory; changing it after the root has mounted does not remount. Use ReactorHostControl.Mount to swap roots. Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentException The type does not derive from Component, or is abstract or an open generic. EffectiveRenderErrorHandler The handler this control would use right now: its own ReactorHostControl.RenderErrorHandler, else ReactorApp.DefaultRenderErrorHandler, else null (built-in fallback). IsIdle True when the render loop has no pending or in-flight render and no re-render queued for the next tick — same contract as ReactorHost.IsIdle. Safe to read from any thread. A disposed control reports idle: it will never render again. OnRenderComplete Optional callback invoked after each render pass with phase timings (ms): treeBuildMs, reconcileMs, effectsMs. Used by perf harnesses to capture the breakdown of a Reactor render cycle. Props Optional props to pass to the root component created by ComponentFactory. Reconciler Provides access to the underlying reconciler for RegisterType calls. RenderErrorHandler Replaces the built-in render-error fallback for this control only. null (the default) falls through to ReactorApp.DefaultRenderErrorHandler at error time. See RenderErrorHandler. (issue #1291) Stats Live render performance snapshot, updated every ~1 second. Always available (FPS, frame time). DEBUG builds include per-reconcile element counters. Remarks Returned by value, unlike ReactorHost.Stats: the XAML compiler emits type metadata for every public property of a control declared in markup, and a ref-returning property becomes typeof(RenderStats&) in the app's generated XamlTypeInfo.g.cs, which does not compile. The copy is a few dozen bytes, read about once a second. Methods Dispose Releases the resources that this object holds. Mount Mount(Component) Mount a Component instance directly. Starts the render loop immediately. Parameters Name Type Description component Component Mount(Func<RenderContext, Element>) Mount a function component. Starts the render loop immediately. Parameters Name Type Description renderFunc Func<RenderContext, Element> WaitForIdleAsync Completes once the render loop is idle (see ReactorHostControl.IsIdle) — after a setState, a ReactorHostControl.Mount, or any other change that schedules a render, await this before reading the realized tree back. Yields to the dispatcher at Low priority so Normal-priority renders and Low-priority re-renders all complete first; gives up after maxYields yields, or immediately if the dispatcher is shutting down. Same contract as ReactorHost.WaitForIdleAsync; callable from any thread. Parameters Name Type Default Description maxYields int 50
description: A fully self-contained WinUI ContentControl that hosts a Reactor component tree. Drop this into any vanilla WinUI app — no ReactorApp, ReactorApplication, or special bootstrapping needed. Each instance owns its own Reconciler and render loop.
title: ReactorHostControl

content: Owns one OS top-level Window and one ReactorHost. Created via ReactorApp.OpenWindow. (spec 036 §3.2 / §4.2) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Learn more: Windows Remarks Public mutators (ReactorWindow.Activate, ReactorWindow.Hide, ReactorWindow.Show, ReactorWindow.Close, ReactorWindow.Update, ReactorWindow.SetSize, ReactorWindow.SetPosition, ReactorWindow.CenterOnScreen, ReactorWindow.Mount) must be called on the UI thread captured by ReactorApp.UIDispatcher. Read-only properties (ReactorWindow.Spec, ReactorWindow.Dpi, ReactorWindow.Position, ReactorWindow.State, ReactorWindow.IsVisible, ReactorWindow.IsActive) snapshot a Volatile.Read field and are safe from any thread. Disposal is idempotent — a second ReactorWindow.Close or ReactorWindow.Dispose is a no-op, not an exception. Properties AppWindow The WinUI ReactorWindow.AppWindow for this window. DipScale DIP scale factor (Dpi / 96). 1.0 at 100%, 1.5 at 150%, 2.0 at 200%. Dpi Per-window DPI in raw units (96, 120, 144, 192, ...). Phase 2 makes this observable. Host The ReactorHost driving this window's render loop. Id Stable id, e.g. "win-3". Allocated monotonically per process. IsActive Whether the window currently holds activation. IsVisible Whether the window is currently shown (post ReactorWindow.Activate / pre ReactorWindow.Hide). Key Optional stable identity (from WindowSpec.Key). NativeWindow The underlying WinUI Window. Overlay Taskbar overlay icon ("badge"). Lazily allocated. Shortcut kept for compatibility; equivalent to TaskbarItem.Overlay. (spec 036 §11.2) PersistedScope Per-window persisted-state scope. Bounded by this window's lifetime — disposed when the window closes. Used by UsePersisted when PersistedScope.Window is requested. (spec 036 §3.4 / §4.4) Position DIP top-left position of the window, rounded to the nearest DIP. Progress Taskbar progress indicator for this window. Lazily allocated on first read; apps that never touch it pay no shell-COM init cost. Shortcut kept for compatibility; equivalent to TaskbarItem.Progress. (spec 036 §11.1) Spec Last applied WindowSpec snapshot. State Coarse window state. TaskbarItem Grouped taskbar features for this window. Lazily allocated. Methods Activate Show and focus the window. UI-thread only. No-op after disposal. BeginDragMove Begin a window drag/move loop as if the title bar had been clicked-and-dragged. Remarks Call from a left-button PointerPressed handler. We snapshot the initial cursor + window screen position, then run a dispatcher timer that polls GetCursorPos at ~60Hz and calls AppWindow.Move until GetAsyncKeyState(VK_LBUTTON) reports the button is no longer pressed. The timer-based approach is necessary because WinUI 3 routes pointer input through a child InputSiteBridge HWND, so synthesizing WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN (or WM_SYSCOMMAND + SC_MOVE | HTCAPTION) on the top-level HWND silently falls into keyboard/cursor-track move mode rather than mouse-driven click-drag (DefWindowProc doesn't see a recent WM_LBUTTONDOWN message). The polling approach is simple, reliable, and doesn't depend on the OS's non-client message routing. The trade-off vs. the OS modal drag loop is no Aero Snap during the drag — acceptable for the small floating windows (command palettes, tool palettes) that need IsMovableByBackground. CenterOnScreen Center on the window's current monitor. UI-thread only. ClearThumbnailToolbar Hide all thumbnail-toolbar buttons. Shortcut kept for compatibility; equivalent to TaskbarItem.ClearThumbnailToolbar(). Idempotent; safe to call before ReactorWindow.SetThumbnailToolbar has been called. (spec 036 §11.5) Close Close the window. UI-thread only. The ReactorWindow.Closing event (Phase 3) will run first; if any subscriber sets WindowClosingEventArgs.Cancel the close aborts. Idempotent — a second call after disposal is a no-op. Dispose Idempotent dispose. Detaches event handlers and disposes the host. The native window has typically already been closed by this point — this is the cleanup that runs after Window.Closed fires. Hide Hide the window without closing. UI-thread only. No-op after disposal. Mount Mount(Component) Mount a new component root. UI-thread only. Parameters Name Type Description root Component Mount(Func<RenderContext, Element>) Mount a new render-function root. UI-thread only. Parameters Name Type Description render Func<RenderContext, Element> SavePlacement Force-save the current window placement when placement persistence is enabled. SetAspectRatio Set or clear the width/height aspect lock used during interactive resize. Parameters Name Type Description ratio double? SetIgnorePointerInput Toggle the WS_EX_TRANSPARENT extended style on the underlying HWND. When set, mouse events pass THROUGH the window to whatever's underneath. The window must already be layered (via ReactorWindow.SetOpacity with a value < 1.0) when enabling — the OS only honors transparent on layered windows. UI-thread only. No-op after disposal. Parameters Name Type Description ignore bool Exceptions Exception Condition InvalidOperationException Thrown when ignore is true but the window is not currently layered. Call ReactorWindow.SetOpacity with a value < 1.0 first. SetNoActivate Toggle the WS_EX_NOACTIVATE extended style on the underlying HWND. When set, the window appears without stealing foreground activation (matches VS tool-window / drag-preview behavior). UI-thread only. No-op after disposal. Parameters Name Type Description noActivate bool SetOpacity Set window-wide alpha in [0..1]. 1.0 strips the layered-window extended style; values below 1.0 install it and call SetLayeredWindowAttributes. UI-thread only. No-op after disposal. Parameters Name Type Description opacity double SetPosition Move to x,y DIPs. UI-thread only. Parameters Name Type Description x double y double Remarks The DIP→physical conversion uses the current window's DPI. On mixed-DPI multi-monitor setups, moving across to a monitor with a different scale factor can land at a slightly different physical position than a caller expects, because Windows virtual-screen coordinates are physical pixels with no global DIP coordinate space. For predictable cross-monitor placement, prefer ReactorWindow.CenterOnScreen (which resolves against the destination DisplayArea) or move in two steps — SetPosition onto the target monitor, then adjust within it. (spec 036 §5.2) SetSize Resize to width x height DIPs. UI-thread only. Parameters Name Type Description width double height double SetThumbnailToolbar Replace the thumbnail-toolbar buttons for this window. Shortcut kept for compatibility; equivalent to TaskbarItem.SetThumbnailToolbar(...). Up to seven buttons; duplicate ids throw. The first call adds the button set, later calls diff and update only the changed slots. (spec 036 §11.5) Parameters Name Type Description buttons IReadOnlyList<ThumbnailToolbarButton> Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentException Thrown when more than seven buttons are supplied or when ids are duplicated. Show Show a previously hidden window. UI-thread only. No-op after disposal. Update Diff next against the current spec and apply only the fields that changed. UI-thread only. Parameters Name Type Description next WindowSpec Events Activated Fires on the UI thread when the window gains activation. Closed Fires on the UI thread after the window closes and the host disposes. Closing Fires on the UI thread before the window closes. Set WindowClosingEventArgs.Cancel to abort. Synchronous — see UseClosingGuard for the async pattern. (Phase 3) Deactivated Fires on the UI thread when the window loses activation. DpiChanged Fires on the UI thread when per-window DPI changes. (Phase 2) PositionChanged Fires on the UI thread when the window's DIP top-left position changes. SizeChanged Fires on the UI thread when the window's DIP size changes. (Phase 3) StateChanged Fires on the UI thread when ReactorWindow.State changes. (Phase 3) ZOrderChanged Fires on the UI thread when Win32 reports a z-order transition. WindowZOrderChangedEventArgs.IsCovered is a covered hint based on HWND insertion order, not a pixel-accurate occlusion guarantee.
title: ReactorWindow

content: Snapshot of render loop performance, updated every ~1 second by ReactorHost. Always available: FPS, frame timing, render count. DEBUG builds add per-reconcile element counters from the last render pass. Threading contract: this struct is written field-by-field on the UI thread and exposed via ref readonly. Readers on other threads may observe torn values. Always read on the UI thread or copy the entire struct atomically via assignment. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting. Learn more: Reactor for XAML Developers Properties AvgEffectsMs Average effects flush time (ms) over the last window. AvgReconcileMs Average reconcile time (ms) over the last window. AvgTotalMs Average total frame time (ms) over the last window (tree + reconcile + effects). AvgTreeBuildMs Average tree-build time (ms) over the last window. Fps Renders per second over the last measurement window. LastCreated New UIElements created (mounted) in the last reconcile pass. LastDiffed Elements diffed in the last reconcile pass. LastModified UIElements modified (property updates) in the last reconcile pass. LastSkipped Elements skipped (memo/ShallowEquals) in the last reconcile pass. RendersInWindow Number of renders in the last measurement window (~1 second). TotalRenders Total renders since the ReactorHost was created.
title: RenderStats

content: JumpList Process-scoped jump list — the right-click flyout that appears on the app's taskbar button or Start tile. Driven through Windows.UI.StartScreen.JumpList for packaged apps and Win32 ICustomDestinationList for unpackaged. (spec 036 §11.3) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Remarks Security note: JumpListItem.Arguments are command-line strings handed to a freshly launched process by the shell. Apps must parse them through Reactor.Cli's arg parser before acting on them — a malformed shortcut, a forged jump-list entry left by another process, or a stale entry from an earlier installation will otherwise reach the new process unchecked. Reactor itself never auto-acts on these strings; ReactorAppContext.LaunchActivation surfaces them so the app can validate before dispatching. Unpackaged apps must set JumpList.AppUserModelId before the first JumpList.UpdateAsync call — without it the shell has no stable identity to attach the jump list to. Properties AppUserModelId Application User Model ID used by the shell to associate the jump list with this process. Required for unpackaged apps; ignored when the process runs under an MSIX package (the package manifest supplies it). ShowFrequent Whether the OS-managed "Frequent" category is shown. The list contents are owned by the shell — apps can only toggle visibility. ShowRecent Whether the OS-managed "Recent" category is shown. The list contents are owned by the shell — apps can only toggle visibility. Methods ClearAsync Clear all user-defined jump-list entries. UI-thread only. Returns: The removed arguments observed by the clear transaction. Remarks Like JumpList.UpdateAsync, a successful clear consumes Windows' removal records. Retain the returned arguments before publishing destinations again. GetRemovedArgumentsAsync Read the argument strings of entries removed by the user. UI-thread only. Remarks This does not update the list or acknowledge removals. Call before JumpList.UpdateAsync and remove matching entries from the app's destination tracking data. A successful update clears its removal records; also retain the arguments returned by that update to capture removals that occurred after this query. Only reintroduce a destination after new user activity. On unpackaged apps, only shell links targeting the current executable are returned; shell-item destinations are not created by this wrapper. Argument strings are compared ordinally, not as parsed command lines. UpdateAsync Replace the jump list's user-defined entries. UI-thread only. Parameters Name Type Description items IEnumerable<JumpListItem> Returns: All distinct removed arguments observed in this update transaction, including removals not present in items. The result reports observations, not commit success; logged shell HRESULT failures retain the existing non-throwing behavior. Remarks Clears any previously-set entries first; the OS-managed Recent and Frequent categories are unaffected (toggle them via JumpList.ShowRecent / JumpList.ShowFrequent). COM activation and marshaling failures propagate as exceptions — callers may catch if fire-and-forget is desired. Individual HRESULT failures from shell APIs (e.g., BeginList, CommitList) are logged via DiagnosticLog but do not throw. Entries currently recorded as removed by Windows are omitted. A successful update clears the platform's removal records. Retain the returned arguments in the app's destination tracking data to avoid reintroducing them on the next update without new user activity. JumpListItem Shape of a single jump-list entry. (spec 036 §11.3 / §11.6) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Constructors JumpListItem Shape of a single jump-list entry. (spec 036 §11.3 / §11.6) Parameters Name Type Default Description Title string User-visible label for the entry. Arguments string Command-line arguments handed to a fresh process invocation when the user activates the entry. Recommended convention: use a deep-link URI string (the same shape DeepLinkMap.Resolve accepts) and resolve via LaunchActivation.TryResolve in the startup callback. The JumpListItem.ForUri factory makes that convention discoverable. Security: these strings round-trip through the shell back into the next process launch. Apps must validate them via Reactor.Cli's arg parser or DeepLinkMap<TRoute> before acting on them — Reactor itself never auto-executes the arguments. Kind JumpListItemKind JumpListItemKind.Task Whether this is a regular task, a separator, or part of a custom group. Description string? null Optional tooltip / accessible description. Icon WindowIcon? null Optional icon shown next to the title. The two jump-list paths want different things, and each silently skips what it cannot use: Packaged — WindowIcon.FromResource only. The WinRT JumpListItem.Logo takes a packaged Uri, so a filesystem path is skipped. Unpackaged — WindowIcon.FromPath only. The Win32 path hands the source to IShellLink.SetIconLocation, which wants a filesystem path, so an ms-appx: URI is skipped instead. See JumpListComInterop.BuildShellLinkArray. Binary sources (WindowIcon.FromBytes / FromRgba) work on neither: they have no URI and no path. Both arms skip them via the empty-Source guard. Ship a sidecar .ico or a packaged asset for jump-list entries. GroupCategory string? null Group label for JumpListItemKind.Custom items. Properties Arguments Command-line arguments handed to a fresh process invocation when the user activates the entry. Recommended convention: use a deep-link URI string (the same shape DeepLinkMap.Resolve accepts) and resolve via LaunchActivation.TryResolve in the startup callback. The JumpListItem.ForUri factory makes that convention discoverable. Security: these strings round-trip through the shell back into the next process launch. Apps must validate them via Reactor.Cli's arg parser or DeepLinkMap<TRoute> before acting on them — Reactor itself never auto-executes the arguments. Description Optional tooltip / accessible description. GroupCategory Group label for JumpListItemKind.Custom items. Icon Optional icon shown next to the title. The two jump-list paths want different things, and each silently skips what it cannot use: Packaged — WindowIcon.FromResource only. The WinRT JumpListItem.Logo takes a packaged Uri, so a filesystem path is skipped. Unpackaged — WindowIcon.FromPath only. The Win32 path hands the source to IShellLink.SetIconLocation, which wants a filesystem path, so an ms-appx: URI is skipped instead. See JumpListComInterop.BuildShellLinkArray. Binary sources (WindowIcon.FromBytes / FromRgba) work on neither: they have no URI and no path. Both arms skip them via the empty-Source guard. Ship a sidecar .ico or a packaged asset for jump-list entries. Kind Whether this is a regular task, a separator, or part of a custom group. Title User-visible label for the entry. Methods EncodeArgument Encode a single argv value per CommandLineToArgvW rules. Public so callers building command lines piecewise can reuse the same escaper Reactor uses internally for jump-list entries. Parameters Name Type Description argument string EncodeArguments Encode a sequence of argv-style argument values as a single command-line string compatible with CommandLineToArgvW. Whitespace, quotes, and trailing-backslash sequences are quoted/escaped per the documented MSVC parsing rules so that round-tripping the result through the OS command-line parser yields back the original sequence. Parameters Name Type Description arguments IEnumerable<string> Remarks Useful directly for jump-list entries (see JumpListItem.ForCommandLine), thumbnail-toolbar buttons, and any other surface where an argument string is handed to the shell for re-launch. Reactor's own CLI parser (Reactor.Cli) consumes CommandLineToArgvW-encoded input, so encoded strings round-trip without further escaping. ForCommandLine Build a jump-list entry whose JumpListItem.Arguments string is tokenized: each element of arguments becomes one argv slot when the launched process parses its command line via CommandLineToArgvW. Values containing whitespace, quotes, or backslashes are escaped so a malicious value can't break out into a neighbouring argument. Use this factory whenever the arguments include data that did not originate from a string literal in your source code (deep-link payloads, file paths, user-typed identifiers). The raw-string JumpListItem constructor and JumpListItem.ForUri are still appropriate when the caller has already produced a well-formed deep-link URI. (spec 036 §11.3 security checklist) Parameters Name Type Default Description title string arguments IEnumerable<string> description string? null icon WindowIcon? null groupCategory string? null ForUri Convenience factory for the recommended "Arguments == deep-link URI" convention. Equivalent to new JumpListItem(title, uri, Task, ...); makes the navigation bridge discoverable so apps don't need to read the Arguments doc to know they can hand the activation to a DeepLinkMap<TRoute>. (spec 036 §11.3 / §11.6) Parameters Name Type Default Description title string uri string description string? null icon WindowIcon? null groupCategory string? null JumpListItemKind Kind of jump-list entry. (spec 036 §11.3) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description Task 0 A regular task in the standard "Tasks" group. Custom 1 A task in a custom JumpListItem.GroupCategory. Separator 2 A horizontal separator in the same group as the previous item. TaskbarItem Grouping facade for the taskbar features associated with a ReactorWindow. Existing ReactorWindow.Progress, ReactorWindow.Overlay, ReactorWindow.SetThumbnailToolbar, and ReactorWindow.ClearThumbnailToolbar shortcuts remain available. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Properties Description Shell thumbnail tooltip / description for the taskbar button. The property keeps the last value assigned; native application is best-effort. Overlay Taskbar overlay icon for the owning window. Progress Taskbar progress indicator for the owning window. Methods ClearThumbnailToolbar Hide all thumbnail toolbar buttons for the owning window. SetThumbnailToolbar Replace the thumbnail toolbar buttons for the owning window. Parameters Name Type Description buttons IReadOnlyList<ThumbnailToolbarButton> TaskbarOverlay Taskbar overlay icon ("badge") for a top-level window. Backs ReactorWindow.Overlay. (spec 036 §11.2) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Remarks Setting TaskbarOverlay.Icon to null clears the overlay. The icon should be 16×16 logical pixels — larger images are downscaled by the shell with quality loss; we emit a one-shot Debug.WriteLine when a WindowIcon.FromPath source can't be loaded as an HICON. The overlay needs a raw HICON, so it accepts a filesystem path or in-memory data (WindowIcon.FromBytes / WindowIcon.FromRgba) and skips WindowIcon.FromResource. A procedurally-drawn badge is a natural fit for WindowIcon.FromRgba, which needs no file on disk. Accessibility: TaskbarOverlay.AccessibleDescription flows through the pszDescription parameter of ITaskbarList3.SetOverlayIcon — without it the overlay is invisible to assistive tech (spec §0.6). Properties AccessibleDescription Accessible description handed to the shell's SetOverlayIcon(pszDescription) — required for assistive tech to announce the overlay. (spec 036 §0.6) Icon The current overlay icon. Null clears. TaskbarProgress Visual taskbar progress for a top-level window. Backs ReactorWindow.Progress. (spec 036 §11.1) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Remarks All writes are best-effort. The shell is the source of truth — Reactor keeps the last-applied state for round-trip queries and idempotent re-apply only. A TaskbarProgressState.None assignment clears both state and value; an TaskbarProgressState.Indeterminate state ignores TaskbarProgress.Value. Properties State Last-applied progress state. (spec 036 §11.1) Value Progress fraction in [0.0, 1.0]. Ignored when TaskbarProgress.State is TaskbarProgressState.Indeterminate or TaskbarProgressState.None. Out-of-range values throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Methods Clear Shorthand for State = None + Value = 0. TaskbarProgressState State of the taskbar progress indicator for a window. Wire-compatible with the shell's TBPF_* values. (spec 036 §11.1) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description None 0 No progress shown (default). Indeterminate 1 Marquee animation; TaskbarProgress.Value is ignored. Normal 2 Standard determinate progress, green. Paused 3 Determinate progress, yellow (paused). Error 4 Determinate progress, red (error). ThumbnailToolbarButton One button in a window's thumbnail toolbar (taskbar live-preview UI). Constructed declaratively and handed to ReactorWindow.SetThumbnailToolbar. (spec 036 §11.5) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Constructors ThumbnailToolbarButton One button in a window's thumbnail toolbar (taskbar live-preview UI). Constructed declaratively and handed to ReactorWindow.SetThumbnailToolbar. Must be unique within a single set. Icon WindowIcon Filesystem-backed icon (WindowIcon.FromPath) or in-memory icon data (WindowIcon.FromBytes / WindowIcon.FromRgba). content: Learn more: Windows ReactorTrayIcon Top-level system-tray icon — a peer of ReactorWindow. Created via ReactorApp.OpenTrayIcon. Provides the icon bitmap, tooltip, and click events; reconciles a Reactor Element as its flyout via ReactorTrayIcon.ShowFlyout. (spec 036 §11.4) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Remarks Public mutators must run on the UI thread captured by ReactorApp.UIDispatcher. Disposal is idempotent — a second ReactorTrayIcon.Close / ReactorTrayIcon.Dispose call is a no-op. The flyout-content reconciliation runs in a RenderContext without an owning ReactorWindow; hooks like UseWindow return their documented fallback values (spec 036 §7.1). Properties Icon The icon bitmap source. Mutating triggers a shell re-apply. Id Stable id, e.g. "tray-1". Allocated monotonically per process. IsVisible Whether the icon is currently shown. Mutating triggers a shell re-apply. Key Optional stable identity (from TrayIconSpec.Key). Spec Last-applied TrayIconSpec snapshot. Tooltip Tooltip text. Mutating triggers a shell re-apply. Methods Close Remove the icon from the tray and dispose. UI-thread only. Idempotent. Dispose Releases the resources that this object holds. HideFlyout Dismiss the tray flyout. UI-thread only. Idempotent. ShowFlyout Show a Reactor Element as the tray icon's flyout. UI-thread only. The flyout reconciles in a context without an owning window (UseWindow returns null inside). Light-dismisses automatically when the user clicks outside it or presses Escape. (spec 036 §7.1, §11.4) Parameters Name Type Description flyoutContent Element Update Diff next against the current spec and re-apply only changed fields. UI-thread only. Parameters Name Type Description next TrayIconSpec Events Click Fires on the UI thread when the user left-clicks the icon. Security: see ReactorTrayIcon.DoubleClick remarks. Treat click handlers as triggers for reversible UI actions only. DoubleClick Fires on the UI thread when the user double-clicks the icon. Security — clicks are not authenticated: the tray click callback arrives as a Win32 WM_APP+1 message that any process at the same Integrity Level can synthesise via PostMessage to the hidden tray window. Use click handlers for reversible UI actions only (open a window, toggle state, show a flyout); gate any privileged or destructive operation behind a deliberate in-app confirmation step. (W-6, threat model 2026-05-08.) RightClick Fires on the UI thread when the user right-clicks the icon. Security: see ReactorTrayIcon.DoubleClick remarks. TrayIconSpec Immutable (init-only) declarative description of a system-tray icon. Hand to ReactorApp.OpenTrayIcon to register; hand to ReactorTrayIcon.Update to diff and re-apply only changed fields. (spec 036 §11.4) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Constructors TrayIconSpec Immutable (init-only) declarative description of a system-tray icon. Hand to ReactorApp.OpenTrayIcon to register; hand to ReactorTrayIcon.Update to diff and re-apply only changed fields. (spec 036 §11.4) Parameters Name Type Default Description Icon WindowIcon The icon to display in the notification area. Must be a filesystem path (WindowIcon.FromPath) pointing at an .ico, or icon data held in memory (WindowIcon.FromBytes / WindowIcon.FromRgba). Packaged resources (WindowIcon.FromResource) are not usable here: the notification area needs a raw HICON, which is loaded via LoadImageW or CreateIconFromResourceEx, and neither can read an ms-appx:/// URI. A resource icon is skipped with a diagnostic — ship a sidecar .ico alongside the app, or hand the bytes to WindowIcon.FromBytes instead. See ReactorTrayIcon.LoadHIcon. Tooltip string User-visible tooltip that surfaces as the icon's accessible name to Narrator / UIA. (spec 036 §0.6) Key WindowKey? null Optional stable identity for UseTrayIcon reuse and shell lookups. IsVisible bool true Whether the icon is currently shown. Hidden icons are still registered with the shell but suppressed via NIS_HIDDEN. Properties Icon The icon to display in the notification area. Must be a filesystem path (WindowIcon.FromPath) pointing at an .ico, or icon data held in memory (WindowIcon.FromBytes / WindowIcon.FromRgba). Packaged resources (WindowIcon.FromResource) are not usable here: the notification area needs a raw HICON, which is loaded via LoadImageW or CreateIconFromResourceEx, and neither can read an ms-appx:/// URI. A resource icon is skipped with a diagnostic — ship a sidecar .ico alongside the app, or hand the bytes to WindowIcon.FromBytes instead. See ReactorTrayIcon.LoadHIcon. content: Marks a method or property setter that must be invoked on the UI thread — the annotated method (or the property's setter) calls ThreadAffinity.ThrowIfNotOnUIThread, which throws InvalidOperationException when reached from a background thread once the UI dispatcher has been captured. (The guard is a no-op before the first window bootstraps, while ReactorApp.UIDispatcher is still null.) Property getters are not guarded, so the REACTOR_THREAD_001 analyzer flags writes to an annotated property, not reads. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting. Inherits from Attribute. Learn more: Reactor for XAML Developers Remarks The marker exists for the REACTOR_THREAD_001 analyzer (UIThreadAffinityAnalyzer). In a consumer compilation the Reactor framework is a metadata-only reference, so the analyzer cannot inspect a callee's body for the runtime guard — DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty and IL is not available. A metadata-visible attribute is the committed mechanism the analyzer keys off, so this type must be public. This is a plain marker attribute with no members and no reflection surface, so it is trim- and AOT-safe. Keep it in sync with the members that call ThreadAffinity.ThrowIfNotOnUIThread; the analyzer reads the attribute rather than a hard-coded member list. Constructors UIThreadOnlyAttribute

content: Learn more: Windows, Advanced Windowing AspectRatioBasis Whether WindowSpec.AspectRatio applies to the outer window rectangle (caption + borders included) or to the client (content) area. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Remarks AspectRatioBasis.Window is the simpler / cheaper mode and matches the raw shape of the OS WM_SIZING contract — the framework just enforces a ratio on the rect the OS hands us. AspectRatioBasis.Client is what most media/game/canvas apps want (a 1:1 client area for a square video player, a 16:9 client area for a game viewport). The framework computes the chrome inset via AdjustWindowRectExForDpi at the current window style + DPI, so the ratio stays accurate across DPI changes and across WindowStyle flips. Has no effect when WindowSpec.AspectRatio is null. Values Name Value Description Window 0 Ratio applies to the outer window rect, including caption and borders. Default. Client 1 Ratio applies to the client area. The framework auto-accounts for chrome. PresenterKind Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description Overlapped 0 Standard chrome with caption and a system menu. FullScreen 1 Borderless full-screen presentation. CompactOverlay 2 Compact-overlay (PIP-style) presentation. ShutdownPolicy Process-shutdown policy. Evaluated whenever a window or tray icon closes. (spec 036 §6.2) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description OnPrimaryWindowClosed 0 Default. Closing the primary window exits the process. OnLastSurfaceClosed 1 Exit when the last window AND the last tray icon have closed. Explicit 2 Surfaces close, but the process keeps running until ReactorApp.Exit is called. WindowCornerStyle Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description Default 0 Let the OS choose the default corner style. Square 1 Request square window corners. Rounded 2 Request rounded window corners. RoundedSmall 3 Request small rounded window corners. WindowEmbedStyle Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description Child 0 Owner 1 WindowIconKind Which kind of source a WindowIcon was constructed from. (spec 036 §4.1) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Remarks Consumers differ in what they can accept, because most need a raw Win32 HICON while a few need a Uri. See the remarks on WindowIcon for the per-surface support matrix. Values Name Value Description Path 0 A filesystem path, from WindowIcon.FromPath. Resource 1 An ms-appx:/// resource URI, from WindowIcon.FromResource. Binary 2 Icon data held in memory, from WindowIcon.FromBytes or WindowIcon.FromRgba. WindowLevel Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description Normal 0 Normal z-order behavior. Floating 1 Keep above other Reactor app windows when they activate. AlwaysOnTop 2 Use the Win32 topmost tier. WindowResizeMode Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description CanResize 0 User can drag borders; minimize and maximize buttons are enabled subject to the spec masks. NoResize 1 User cannot drag borders; minimize and maximize buttons are disabled subject to the spec masks. CanMinimize 2 User cannot drag borders, but the minimize button stays enabled subject to the spec mask. WindowSizeToContent Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description Manual 0 Window size is controlled manually or by the OS default. Width 1 Window width tracks content desired width; height stays unchanged. Height 2 Window height tracks content desired height; width stays unchanged. WidthAndHeight 3 Window width and height both track content desired size. WindowStartPosition Initial placement strategy for a ReactorWindow when it opens. (spec 036 §3.2 / §4.1) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description Default 0 WinUI default placement — the OS picks based on prior windows. CenterOnPrimary 1 Center the window on the primary monitor. CenterOnOwner 2 Center the window on its WindowSpec.Owner's monitor. Manual 4 Place at WindowSpec.ManualPosition. Both must be set together. CenterOnCurrent 5 Center on the monitor nearest the current cursor position. WindowState Lifecycle/state of a ReactorWindow. Exposed via ReactorWindow.State and the UseWindowState hook. (spec 036 §3.2) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description Normal 0 Not minimized, not maximized — the default. Minimized 1 Minimized to the taskbar. Maximized 2 Maximized to fill the work area. FullScreen 3 Borderless full-screen presentation. CompactOverlay 4 Compact-overlay presentation. WindowStyle Coarse classifier for the WinUI AppWindowPresenterKind presenter applied to a window. (spec 036 §3.2 / §4.1) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Values Name Value Description Default 0 Standard overlapped window chrome. None 1 No border, caption, or system menu. ToolWindow 2 Tool-window chrome; hidden from the taskbar unless explicitly overridden. WindowTitleBarHeight Caption height for a window whose content extends into the title bar. Mirrors Microsoft.UI.Windowing.TitleBarHeightOption. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Remarks The native option only sizes the system caption (caption buttons, drag region, insets). The WinUI TitleBar control does not follow it — see TitleBarElement.HeightOption, which sizes both. Values Name Value Description Standard 0 Standard 32 DIP caption. Tall 1 Tall 48 DIP caption — the layout used when the title bar hosts navigation chrome. Collapsed 2 No caption area at all. WindowTitleBarTheme Theme of the window's system caption (the minimize / maximize / close buttons). Mirrors Microsoft.UI.Windowing.TitleBarTheme. (issue #1297) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Remarks WinUI does not carry an element's RequestedTheme through to the caption, so an app that themes its content opposite to the system declares the caption theme too — see WindowSpec.TitleBarTheme and TitleBarElement.PreferredTheme. Values Name Value Description Legacy 0 Legacy caption theming. UseDefaultAppMode 1 Follows the app's default mode (the system light / dark setting). Light 2 Light caption buttons. Dark 3 Dark caption buttons.

content: Abstraction over AppWindow.SetIcon and AppWindow.SetIcon. Pass to WindowSpec.Icon, to a tray icon, or to a taskbar overlay. (spec 036 §4.1) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Learn more: Windows, Advanced Windowing Remarks Three source kinds are supported: a filesystem path (WindowIcon.FromPath) for .ico resources alongside an unpackaged app, an ms-appx:///-style packaged-app resource URI (WindowIcon.FromResource), and icon data held in memory (WindowIcon.FromBytes / WindowIcon.FromRgba). Empty strings and empty buffers are rejected at construction so a malformed icon never reaches the WinUI APIs. Consumers differ in what they can accept, because most of them need a raw Win32 HICON while a couple need a Uri: WindowSpec.Icon — WindowIcon.FromPath and WindowIcon.FromResource. An ms-appx: source is mapped to a file beside the app before it reaches AppWindow.SetIcon, which needs a filesystem path: handed the URI itself inside a packaged app it silently applies a default icon. A binary source is not accepted here — see WindowIcon.FromBytes. Tray icons, taskbar overlays, and thumbnail-toolbar buttons — WindowIcon.FromPath and the binary factories. They need an HICON, which comes either from LoadImageW on a file or from CreateIconFromResourceEx on in-memory data; neither can read a packaged resource URI, so WindowIcon.FromResource is skipped with a diagnostic. Jump lists — WindowIcon.FromResource on the packaged path (the WinRT API takes the URI directly) and WindowIcon.FromPath on the unpackaged one. Every other kind is silently skipped. Instances are immutable and safe to share: a binary source copies the caller's buffer, so a later write to that array cannot change what the shell renders. Properties IsBinary True when constructed via WindowIcon.FromBytes or WindowIcon.FromRgba. IsResource True when constructed via WindowIcon.FromResource. Kind Which factory produced this icon. Source The path or resource URI this icon was constructed from, or String.Empty for a WindowIconKind.Binary icon, which has no addressable source. Test WindowIcon.Kind rather than inferring it from here. Methods FromBytes Create an icon from encoded icon data held in memory — an .ico container, a PNG, or a bare RT_ICON DIB blob — so an app whose icon lives in an embedded resource, a database, or a download does not have to write a temporary file first. (issue #1185) Parameters Name Type Description data ReadOnlySpan<byte> The encoded bytes. Copied, so the caller may reuse or overwrite its buffer. Remarks Consumed by the tray icon, the taskbar overlay, and thumbnail-toolbar buttons, which need a raw HICON and get one via CreateIconFromResourceEx. A multi-frame .ico is honoured: the frame nearest the size the surface asks for is selected, exactly as LoadImageW would have done from a file. Not accepted by WindowSpec.Icon. Putting a binary icon on a window means owning the HICON for the window's lifetime, which AppWindow.SetIcon(IconId) does not do for you. A binary icon declared there is reported as not applied, so the window falls back to Assets\AppIcon.ico or its PE icon rather than showing nothing. Jump lists and the TitleBar icon default skip it for the same reason they skip a PE icon: both need a Uri. An unrecognised signature is logged via System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine rather than throwing, mirroring WindowIcon.FromPath's treatment of an unrecognised extension — the loader is the authority on what it accepts, and refusing data it would have loaded is worse than letting it report the failure. The bytes are held for this instance's lifetime. That is the point of the API, but it is worth knowing when a long-lived spec holds a large multi-resolution .ico. FromPath Create an icon from a filesystem path (typically a .ico) for an unpackaged app. Throws on null/empty input. An unrecognised extension or missing file is logged via System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine so misconfiguration is diagnosable, but no exception is raised — apps that deploy assets asynchronously, or icons that exist as a sidecar to a relocated executable, still construct successfully and surface the underlying load failure on WindowIcon.Apply. (W-4 hardening.) Parameters Name Type Description path string FromResource Create an icon from a packaged-app resource URI (e.g. ms-appx:///Assets/AppIcon.ico). Throws on null/empty input. The URI is mapped to a file beside the app (the package install root when packaged) before it reaches AppWindow.SetIcon, which requires a filesystem path. Manifest visual assets (Square44x44Logo and friends) are named by resource identifier rather than filename and are not addressable this way. Parameters Name Type Description uri string FromRgba Create an icon from a raw straight-alpha RGBA8 pixel buffer — the shape Rust's tray crates expose as Icon::from_rgba. (issue #1185) Parameters Name Type Description pixels ReadOnlySpan<byte> Exactly width * height * 4 bytes, top-down, one pixel as R, G, B, A. Copied (as an assembled icon image), so the caller may reuse or overwrite its buffer. width int Icon width in pixels, between 1 and 4096. height int Icon height in pixels, between 1 and 4096. Remarks The buffer is converted once, at construction, into the 32-bpp icon-resource layout the platform loader wants (bottom-up BGRA plus an AND mask). See WindowIcon.FromBytes for which surfaces consume a binary icon. Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentOutOfRangeException width or height is outside 1–4096. ArgumentException pixels is not exactly width * height * 4 bytes.

content: Immutable (init-only) declarative description of a top-level Reactor window. Hand to ReactorApp.OpenWindow to open a window; hand to ReactorWindow.Update to diff against the current spec and apply only changed fields. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Learn more: Windows, Advanced Windowing Remarks All sizes and positions are DIPs (device-independent pixels) — no Win32 / no SizeInt32 in user code. (spec 036 §4.1) WindowSpec.Validate enforces the cross-field invariants and is called by the hosting layer (the ReactorWindow constructor and ReactorWindow.Update) before the spec is used; tests may call it directly. It requires Width/Height to be positive when set (null defers the initial extent to the OS), max ≥ min when both are set, and WindowSpec.ManualPosition iff WindowSpec.StartPosition is WindowStartPosition.Manual. Constructors WindowSpec Construct with explicit field values. Validation runs after the record auto-init. Properties ActivateOnOpen Whether the window auto-activates after content mounts. Default: true. AspectRatio Optional width / height aspect lock applied during interactive resize. AspectRatioBasis Whether WindowSpec.AspectRatio constrains the outer window rect or the client (content) area. Default is AspectRatioBasis.Window; switch to AspectRatioBasis.Client when the ratio describes the content (e.g. 1:1 for a square video, 16:9 for a game viewport) and the framework should auto-account for chrome. Backdrop Optional declarative backdrop. Seeds the per-host modifier. CornerStyle DWM corner preference. On Windows 10 the platform ignores this setting. Embed Optional request to embed this window into an external HWND host. ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar Whether app content extends into the title-bar region. When null, a mounted TitleBar(...) element infers true; otherwise the explicit value wins. Hot reload cannot migrate the previous bool field shape across this type change; restart after editing this field during HR. Height Initial DIP height. Must be positive when set. null (the default) leaves the initial height to the OS. See WindowSpec.Width. Icon Optional window icon — the Win32 HICON Windows shows in the window's caption and the Alt-Tab switcher. Build it with WindowIcon.FromPath for a file beside the app or WindowIcon.FromResource for a packaged ms-appx:/// asset. Remarks Distinct from TitleBar(...).Icon(...), which draws an app mark inside the window's client area. A window may set both, and they may legitimately differ. When this is null, Reactor falls back to Assets\AppIcon.ico beside the app and then to the executable's embedded icon. In an unpackaged app this also drives the taskbar button and Task Manager, because there is no package identity to take precedence. In a packaged app it does not: the shell resolves those two surfaces through package identity and the manifest's Square44x44Logo, never looking at the window handle. A packaged app that wants a consistent icon everywhere must ship a matching manifest logo in addition to setting this. A binary source (WindowIcon.FromBytes / WindowIcon.FromRgba) is not accepted here — this surface needs a filesystem path, because that is what AppWindow.SetIcon takes. Declaring one falls through to the same convention/PE fallback as declaring no icon at all, so the window is never left barer than it would otherwise have been. Binary sources are for the tray icon, the taskbar overlay, and thumbnail-toolbar buttons. IgnorePointerInput Apply the Win32 WS_EX_TRANSPARENT extended style so mouse events pass THROUGH the window to whatever's underneath. Default false. Used by spec 045 §2.6 tear-off so the drag preview doesn't block clicks on drop-target overlays below it. Remarks Requires WindowSpec.Opacity < 1.0 — the OS only honors WS_EX_TRANSPARENT on layered windows. WindowSpec.Validate throws when this field is true with Opacity == 1.0; the runtime mutator ReactorWindow.SetIgnorePointerInput(true) also throws if the live window is not layered. IsMaximizable Whether the maximize caption button is enabled (Overlapped only). IsMinimizable Whether the minimize caption button is enabled (Overlapped only). IsMovableByBackground Whether pressing non-interactive background starts an OS window drag. Key Optional stable identity for UseOpenWindow reuse and shell lookups. Level Z-order tier for this window. ManualPosition DIP top-left position. Set together with WindowStartPosition.Manual; otherwise null. Remarks The DIP→physical conversion uses the window's initial DPI (the monitor it opens on). Coordinates that target a different monitor on a mixed-DPI desktop may land at a slightly different physical position because Windows virtual-screen coordinates are physical pixels with no global DIP coordinate space. For absolute placement on a specific non-primary monitor, prefer WindowStartPosition.CenterOnOwner (with an owner already on that monitor) or call ReactorWindow.SetPosition after the window opens. MaxHeight Optional maximum DIP height. MaxWidth Optional maximum DIP width. MinHeight Optional minimum DIP height. MinWidth Optional minimum DIP width. NoActivate Apply the Win32 WS_EX_NOACTIVATE extended style so the window appears without stealing foreground activation. Matches VS tool-window / drag-preview behavior. Default false. The flag is applied during chrome setup (before Activate) so the first show observes it. Opacity Window-wide alpha in [0..1]. 1.0 = fully opaque (default, no layering overhead). Values below 1.0 are applied via Win32 SetLayeredWindowAttributes on the underlying HWND. Used by the docking subsystem to render an in-flight tear-off floating window at reduced opacity (spec 045 §2.6 tear-off follow-up); apps may also set it for HUD overlays etc. Owner Optional parent window for owned-window semantics. PersistPlacement Restore window placement from the registered store on open and save on close. Ignored when WindowSpec.PersistenceId is null. PersistenceFallback Initial placement used when persistence is enabled but no placement exists yet. PersistenceId Optional persistence id for placement and future per-window persistence subsystems. Presenter Coarse presenter selection. RenderErrorHandler Optional replacement for the built-in render-error fallback in this window. Applied to the window's ReactorHost.RenderErrorHandler before the first render (and again by ReactorWindow.Update). null (the default) falls through to ReactorApp.DefaultRenderErrorHandler. See WindowSpec.RenderErrorHandler. (issue #1291) ResizeMode Resize/chrome policy for overlapped windows. ShowInSwitcher Whether the window appears in Alt-Tab / shell switchers. ShowInTaskbar Whether the window appears in the taskbar. SizeToContent Content-driven sizing mode. Size changes are applied after the first layout pass, so apps may see one frame at the initial Width/Height (or the OS-chosen size when those are null) before content settles. StartPosition Initial placement strategy. Style Window chrome style for overlapped windows. Title Window caption text. Defaults to "Reactor App". TitleBarHeight System caption height. null (the default) leaves the platform default alone; a mounted TitleBar(...) element's HeightOption then applies instead, if it declares one. Remarks Requires a content-extended window — the native AppWindow.TitleBar.PreferredHeightOption setter throws ERROR_INVALID_STATE otherwise. Reactor applies the value only once the window is content-extended (including the deferred flip a TitleBar(...) element performs at mount) and warns instead of throwing when the window never extends. This sizes the system caption only. A mounted WinUI TitleBar control does not follow it, which is why TitleBar(...).Tall() — which sizes both — is the preferred spelling when the window renders a TitleBar(...) element. (issue #917) TitleBarTheme Theme of the system caption buttons (AppWindow.TitleBar.PreferredTheme). null (the default) leaves the platform default alone; a mounted TitleBar(...) element's PreferredTheme then applies instead, if it declares one. (issue #1297) Remarks WinUI does not derive the caption theme from the content's RequestedTheme; an app that themes its content opposite to the system sets this to match. Removing a declaration restores the value the caption had before Reactor first applied one; a value set imperatively and never declared is left alone. Width Initial DIP width. Must be positive when set. null (the default) leaves the initial width to the OS — Reactor does not override that axis, so the window keeps the width Windows picks for a new top-level window (the same behavior a plain XAML Window gets). When both axes are null no AppWindow.Resize call is made at all. Methods Validate Throws ArgumentException when any cross-field invariant is violated. Called by ReactorWindow (constructor and ReactorWindow.Update) before the spec is applied; tests may also call this directly to verify a spec. WithPersistence Configure placement persistence in one call. Parameters Name Type Default Description id string fallback WindowStartPosition WindowStartPosition.Default

content: Learn more: Reactor for XAML Developers PageHelper Helper methods for hosting Reactor components inside XAML Pages that participate in Frame-based navigation. IMPORTANT: WinUI's Frame.Navigate requires pages to have XAML metadata (IXamlType registration). Code-only Page subclasses — including generic base classes like ReactorPage<T> — crash with a null access violation in ActivationAPI::ActivateInstance because GetXamlTypeNoRef() returns null. The correct pattern for Reactor pages in Frame navigation: 1. Create a minimal .xaml file for the page: <Page x:Class="MyApp.Pages.ButtonPage" ... /> 2. In the code-behind, use PageHelper to mount the component: public sealed partial class ButtonPage: Page { private ReactorHostControl? _host; public ButtonPage() { InitializeComponent(); } protected override void OnNavigatedTo(NavigationEventArgs e) { base.OnNavigatedTo(e); _host = PageHelper.Mount<MyComponent>(this, e); } protected override void OnNavigatedFrom(NavigationEventArgs e) { base.OnNavigatedFrom(e); PageHelper.Unmount(ref _host); } } Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting. Methods Mount Mount<TComponent>(Page, NavigationEventArgs) Creates a ReactorHostControl, mounts the component, and sets it as the page's content. Passes navigation parameters as props if the component accepts them. Parameters Name Type Description page Page e NavigationEventArgs Mount<TComponent, TProps>(Page, NavigationEventArgs) Creates a ReactorHostControl, mounts the component with typed props, and sets it as the page's content. Parameters Name Type Description page Page e NavigationEventArgs Unmount Disposes the ReactorHostControl and clears the reference. Parameters Name Type Description host ReactorHostControl? XamlInterop Registers the reverse-embedding element types with a Reconciler. Call this once during app startup or ReactorHostControl initialization. Usage: XamlInterop.Register(reconciler); Then in a Reactor component (the factories record a call site for the source map; the record constructors work too, without one): XamlPage(typeof(ExistingXamlPage), "param") XamlHost(() => new MyUserControl(), ctrl => ((MyUserControl)ctrl).Value = 42) Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Hosting. Methods Register Parameters Name Type Description reconciler Reconciler
