content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Learn more: Commanding Constructors Command Properties Accelerator Keyboard shortcut for this command. AccessKey Access key (Alt+key) for this command. CanExecute Whether the command's action can be invoked. Defaults to true. DebounceMs Leading-edge debounce window, in milliseconds. 0 (the default) disables debouncing and preserves the un-debounced behavior exactly. When > 0 and the command is processed through UseCommand, the first fire is accepted and any subsequent fire within DebounceMs of it is dropped (a no-op). For the duration of the window Command.IsDebouncing is true, so Command.IsEnabled reports false and the bound control visibly disables, then re-enables when the window elapses. This is the framework-owned replacement for the "wrap a sync action in Task.Delay to absorb double-clicks" pattern (issue #136). For async commands, Command.IsExecuting already tracks the lambda's lifetime; DebounceMs is the time-based generalization that keeps the disabled window open past the lambda's return (the effective disabled window is the longer of the two). DebounceMs only works through UseCommand. The debounce state (last-fire window + re-enable timer) lives in the UseCommand hook's backing store, which is the only place that persists across renders (the Command record itself is reconstructed every render). A raw new Command { DebounceMs = … } bound directly to a control — without being passed through UseCommand — has nowhere to persist that state and is therefore inert: it does NOT debounce. Always wrap a debounced command with UseCommand: Description Tooltip / accessibility description. Execute Synchronous action. Mutually exclusive with Command.ExecuteAsync. ExecuteAsync Asynchronous action. Use with UseCommand to get automatic IsExecuting tracking and re-entrance guards. Icon Icon to display alongside the command. IsDebouncing Whether the command is currently inside its leading-edge debounce window. This is framework-managed state set by UseCommand when Command.DebounceMs > 0; it is read-only to app authors (internal init). IsEnabled Computed: the command is enabled only when it can execute, is not currently executing, and is not inside its leading-edge debounce window. IsExecuting Whether the command is currently executing an async operation. Managed by UseCommand. Label Human-readable label shown on buttons, menu items, tooltips, etc.
description: Immutable (init-only) command descriptor that bundles an action with its metadata (label, icon, keyboard accelerator, enabled state). Define once, use in any surface: var save = new Command { Label = "Save", Execute = () => Save(), Icon = SymbolIcon("Save") }; AppBarButton(save) // toolbar MenuItem(save) // menu Button(save) // inline

content: Learn more: Input and gestures ElementRef Opaque ref to a mounted FrameworkElement. Populated by the reconciler when the element is mounted; consumed by FocusManager.Focus and friends. Null until the target element is mounted. Survives re-renders — the same ElementRef instance is reused by the reconciler while the underlying control is recycled from the element pool. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input. Constructors ElementRef Properties Current The currently-mounted control, or null if the referenced element has not mounted yet (or has been unmounted without a replacement). ElementRef<T> Strongly-typed wrapper around ElementRef that surfaces the mounted element as T instead of the base FrameworkElement, removing the (Button)ref.Current cast at every consumer. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input. Remarks Spec 033 §3. Construct via ctx.UseElementRef<T>() and bind to an element via .Ref(typedRef). The typed wrapper is reflection-free and AOT-safe — T is used only for the cast on read. Threading: the reconciler populates the underlying ref on the UI thread during element mount/update. Reading ElementRef.Current from a non-UI thread is permitted but the value may be stale by the time the caller dereferences it. Accessibility: programmatic focus via Current?.Focus() moves the keyboard focus and triggers WinUI's standard focus-changed UIA event, but it does not by itself produce a screen-reader announcement of surrounding content. When the focus change should be accompanied by an announcement (e.g. "saved", "validation error") use UseAnnounce in addition to the focus call. Modifiers applied to the element (notably .AutomationName(...)) are preserved across re-renders, so the typed ref does not affect the UIA tree shape. Type parameters Name Description T The concrete WinUI control type the ref will be attached to. Constrained to FrameworkElement so the safe-cast in ElementRef.Current is well-defined. Properties Current The mounted control as T, or null when the referenced element has not mounted yet, has been unmounted, or the concrete control is not assignable to T. Remarks In RELEASE builds a type mismatch silently yields null; in DEBUG builds the reconciler raises Debug.Fail at attach time so the mismatch is loud during development. Methods ToString Returns a string that represents this object. Operators op_Implicit Implicit conversion to the untyped ElementRef so the typed wrapper composes with the existing .Ref(...) modifier and FocusManager overloads without overload bloat. Parameters Name Type Description typed ElementRef<T> TypedElementRef Factory helpers for ElementRef<T>. Prefer the ctx.UseElementRef<T>() hook from a render path; this helper is for the rare case of constructing a typed ref outside a render context (e.g. for tests). content: Learn more: Input and gestures GesturePhase Phase of a continuous gesture (pan / pinch / rotate / long-press). The callback contract: GesturePhase.Began fires exactly once at the start, GesturePhase.Changed fires zero or more times as the gesture progresses, then either GesturePhase.Ended (normal completion) or GesturePhase.Cancelled (system aborted, pointer lost, escape key, …) fires exactly once. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input. Values Name Value Description Began 0 Gesture has just become recognized and its parameters are stable. Changed 1 Gesture is in progress; deltas are being reported. Ended 2 Gesture completed normally. Cancelled 3 Gesture was cancelled (pointer capture lost, window focus lost, …). LongPressGesture Immutable snapshot of a long-press gesture. Fires GesturePhase.Began the moment the press threshold is crossed, GesturePhase.Ended when the pointer is released after that point, or GesturePhase.Cancelled if the pointer moves beyond the cancel distance or capture is lost. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input. Constructors LongPressGesture Immutable snapshot of a long-press gesture. Fires GesturePhase.Began the moment the press threshold is crossed, GesturePhase.Ended when the pointer is released after that point, or GesturePhase.Cancelled if the pointer moves beyond the cancel distance or capture is lost. Parameters Name Type Description Position Point Pointer position in element-local space at the moment of the event. Duration TimeSpan Elapsed time since the initial press. Phase GesturePhase Current gesture phase. Properties Duration Elapsed time since the initial press. Phase Current gesture phase. Position Pointer position in element-local space at the moment of the event. LongPressGestureConfig Immutable configuration for a .OnLongPress gesture recognizer. Touch/pen input routes through UIElement.Holding. Mouse input is opt-in via LongPressGestureConfig.EnableMouseEmulation; when enabled, the reconciler arms a dispatcher timer on UIElement.PointerPressed and cancels it on release, capture loss, or pointer motion beyond LongPressGestureConfig.CancelDistance. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input. Constructors LongPressGestureConfig Immutable configuration for a .OnLongPress gesture recognizer. Touch/pen input routes through UIElement.Holding. Mouse input is opt-in via LongPressGestureConfig.EnableMouseEmulation; when enabled, the reconciler arms a dispatcher timer on UIElement.PointerPressed and cancels it on release, capture loss, or pointer motion beyond LongPressGestureConfig.CancelDistance. Parameters Name Type Description OnTriggered Action<LongPressGesture> Properties CancelDistance Cumulative pointer motion (device pixels) that cancels an in-progress press. EnableMouseEmulation When true, mouse input arms a dispatcher timer in addition to touch/pen Holding. MinimumDuration Minimum press duration before the gesture triggers. Vertical 2 Only vertical (Y) translation is tracked. PanGesture Immutable snapshot of a pan gesture update. All coordinates are in the element's local space. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Input. Velocity Point Instantaneous velocity in device-independent pixels per second. Position Point Current pointer position in element-local space. IsInertial True once WinUI is extrapolating inertia (after the user lifts their finger). Phase Current gesture phase. Position Current pointer position in element-local space. StartPosition Pointer position at GesturePhase.Began, in element-local space. Translation Total translation since GesturePhase.Began. Velocity Instantaneous velocity in device-independent pixels per second. PanGestureConfig Immutable configuration for a .OnPan gesture recognizer attached to an element. content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Learn more: Layout Remarks Spec 033 §1. The smart constructors GridSize.Auto, GridSize.Star, and GridSize.Px validate their inputs at the boundary; the implicit conversion to GridLength lets the typed form compose with anything that takes a WinUI GridLength. The string parser (GridSize.Parse) is invariant-culture only — track strings are never localized. Whitespace is trimmed; "Auto" matches case-insensitively; numeric forms use CultureInfo.InvariantCulture. When Min or Max are specified, the track size is clamped to that range. For example, GridSize.Px(100) with { Min=50 and Max=200 } will be set to 100 initially and depending on changes clamped to 50 and 200. Min can be set higher as Max in which case the track size will be clamped to the Max value. Constructors GridSize Parameters Name Type Default Description value double type GridUnitType min double? null max double? null Properties Auto The auto-sized track. Equivalent to the WinUI Auto length. Max The maximum size of the track. If specified, the track size will not be greater than this value. Min The minimum size of the track. If specified, the track size will not be less than this value. Type The type of the track size: Auto, Star, or Pixel. Value The value of the track size. For Pixel types, this is the pixel size; for Star types, this is the star weight; for Auto, this is always 1. Methods Parse Parses a track string into a GridSize. Accepts: "Auto" / "auto", "*", "<n>*", "<n>.<m>*", "<n>", "<n>.<m>". Whitespace is trimmed. Parameters Name Type Description s string Exceptions Exception Condition FormatException Thrown for any other input. ArgumentNullException Thrown when s is null. Px A pixel-sized track. pixels must be >= 0. Parameters Name Type Description pixels double Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentOutOfRangeException Thrown when pixels is < 0. Star A star-weighted track. weight defaults to 1 (i.e. "*"); 1.5 produces "1.5*", 0.33 produces "0.33*". Parameters Name Type Default Description weight double 1 Exceptions Exception Condition ArgumentOutOfRangeException Thrown when weight is <= 0. Operators op_Implicit Implicit conversion to GridLength so the typed form composes with any WinUI surface that takes a GridLength. Parameters Name Type Description s GridSize

content: Production implementation of IStringResourceProvider that reads .resw files directly from disk as XML. NOTE: This bypasses MRT (Modern Resource Technology) and the Windows PRI resource system. The standard approach would be to use ResourceLoader from Microsoft.global::Windows.ApplicationModel.Resources, which relies on the .resw files being compiled into a .pri (Package Resource Index) at build time. However, ResourceLoader has significant friction in unpackaged app scenarios: - ResourceLoader(subtreeName) fails with FileNotFoundException for named .resw files in unpackaged apps, even when the PRI contains the resources. - MRT locale negotiation uses the OS language settings, not the app's explicit locale choice, which conflicts with Reactor's LocaleProvider model where the app controls the active locale at runtime. By reading .resw XML directly, we get: - Identical behavior for packaged and unpackaged apps - Locale resolution driven by LocaleProvider, not the OS - No dependency on MRT initialization or PRI packaging REVISIT: If Reactor apps move to packaged deployment (MSIX) as the default, or if MRT Core improves unpackaged support, consider switching back to ResourceLoader for better OS integration (e.g., per-language resource packs, system-level font/layout negotiation). content: Modifiers are extension methods that return a changed copy of the element, so you can chain them. Learn more: Animation Animate Enables implicit compositor animation on visual property changes. All visual property changes (Opacity, Scale, Rotation, Translation, CenterPoint) will animate using the specified curve. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description curve Curve properties AnimateProperty AnimateProperty.All BackgroundTransition Adds an implicit BrushTransition on Background. Only available on Grid and Stack (VStack/HStack) — WinUI only supports BackgroundTransition on Grid, StackPanel, and ContentPresenter. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: GridElement, StackElement. Parameters Name Type Default Description duration TimeSpan? null ConnectedAnimation Declares this element as a participant in a connected animation. When the element is unmounted (e.g., parent container changes type), the reconciler captures its visual snapshot. When a new element with the same key is mounted, the snapshot animates to the new element's position. Both source and destination must use the same key string. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description key string ContentTransitions Custom TransitionCollection applied to the expanding content area. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: ExpanderElement. Parameters Name Type Description transitions TransitionCollection InteractionStates Declares zero-reconcile interaction state visual changes (hover, pressed, focused). The reconciler registers pointer event handlers that drive compositor animations and direct brush swaps — no state variables or re-renders needed. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description configure Func<InteractionStatesBuilder, InteractionStatesBuilder> curve Curve? null ItemContainerTransitions Sets ItemContainerTransitions declaratively on ListView, GridView, etc. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description transitions Transition[] Keyframes Attaches a trigger-based keyframe animation. The animation plays when the trigger value changes between renders. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description name string trigger object? configure Func<KeyframeBuilder, KeyframeBuilder> LayoutAnimation Declared in ElementExtensions. Overload Description LayoutAnimation<T>(T) Enables smooth layout animation: when WinUI repositions this element (e.g., list reorder, grid reflow), it animates from the old position to the new position via the Composition layer. Default duration: 300ms. Elements should have stable keys (.WithKey()) for the reconciler to match them across reorders. LayoutAnimation<T>(T, LayoutAnimationConfig) Enables layout animation with a fully custom configuration. LayoutAnimation<T>(T, TimeSpan) Enables layout animation with a custom duration. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description config LayoutAnimationConfig duration TimeSpan OpacityTransition Adds an implicit ScalarTransition on Opacity. Applied by the reconciler after .Set() callbacks — always safe to combine. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description duration TimeSpan? null RotationTransition Adds an implicit ScalarTransition on Rotation. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description duration TimeSpan? null ScaleTransition Adds an implicit Vector3Transition on Scale. Pass a pre-configured transition to set Components for axis-specific animation. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description transition Vector3Transition? null ScrollLinked Attaches scroll-linked expression animations driven by a ScrollViewer. Expressions run on the compositor at display refresh rate with zero managed code. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description scrollViewer ScrollViewer configure Func<ScrollAnimationBuilder, ScrollAnimationBuilder> SpringLayoutAnimation Enables layout animation with spring physics for a natural, bouncy feel. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description dampingRatio float 0.6f period float 0.08f Stagger Adds incrementing animation delays to children in a container. Child N gets N * delay applied to its compositor animations. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description delay TimeSpan curve Curve? null Transition Enables enter/exit transitions when this element is conditionally rendered. Enter: animates from initial state to visible. Exit: animates out before unmount. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description transition Transition curve Curve? null TranslationTransition Adds an implicit Vector3Transition on Translation. Pass a pre-configured transition to set Components for axis-specific animation. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description transition Vector3Transition? null WithTransitions Sets theme transitions declaratively. The reconciler applies ChildrenTransitions on panels, ChildTransitions on borders, ContentTransitions on content controls. Works on any element type. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description transitions Transition[]

content: Modifiers are extension methods that return a changed copy of the element, so you can chain them. Learn more: Styling and Theming, Theming Tokens ApplyStyle Apply a named WinUI Style to the element's control. Style is on FrameworkElement — works on any element. Usage: TextBlock("Hello").ApplyStyle("BodyTextBlockStyle") Applied at mount only. This routes through OnMount, and the reconciler runs OnMountAction only when there is no previous element (first mount). Conditionally chaining a style therefore will not apply or remove it when the condition flips on an in-place update — give the variants different WithKey values to force a remount when the style itself must change. Unresolved keys do not throw. If styleName is not found in the application's resources (including merged dictionaries), or is found but is not a Style, the element keeps its default appearance and a warning naming the key is emitted on the Microsoft-UI-Reactor ETW provider (and to Debug.WriteLine in DEBUG builds). Earlier versions threw out of the mount action instead. The warning fires once per distinct key, so one bad key in a virtualized list does not warn per realized item; past a few hundred distinct unresolved keys the de-duplication stops and every miss warns again, because staying quiet there would hide a real typo. Under NativeAOT the ETW half is compiled out unless the app sets EventSourceSupport=true; the DEBUG mirror is unaffected. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description styleName string Backdrop Declared in BackdropExtensions. Overload Description Backdrop<T>(T, BackdropKind) Sets the system backdrop on the hosting window using a built-in BackdropKind selector. Backdrop<T>(T, Func<SystemBackdrop?>) Sets the system backdrop on the hosting window using a custom factory. Use this overload to apply tinted Mica, custom blur tints, or any other SystemBackdrop subclass. Applies to: any element. Usage: VStack(children).Background(Theme.CardBackground) Background<T>(T, Brush) Background<T>(T, string) Sets the background from a color string (named color or #RRGGBB / #AARRGGBB). Returns a fresh, caller-independent brush per call (see BrushHelper.Parse — the parsed color is cached, the brush is not); the diff compares brushes structurally (color + opacity). Use the Background overload to supply an explicit brush. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description theme ThemeRef brush Brush color string BorderBrush Declared in ElementExtensions. content: Modifiers are extension methods that return a changed copy of the element, so you can chain them. Learn more: Controls, Commanding AccentButton Applies the WinUI AccentButtonStyle — the accent-color primary-button look. The Style is resolved from Application.Current.Resources once; its colors still follow light/dark/contrast switches because the Style's own setters use {ThemeResource} values, which WinUI re-resolves on theme change. Applied at mount only. Like ApplyStyle this runs through OnMount, which the reconciler gates on first mount — so conditionally chaining it (e.g. isPrimary? btn.AccentButton(): btn) will not apply or remove the style when the condition flips on an in-place update. Give the two variants different WithKey values to force a remount when the style must change. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: ButtonElement, DropDownButtonElement, SplitButtonElement, ToggleSplitButtonElement. CheckedState Sets the three-state value (null = indeterminate). Active only when IsThreeState is true. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: ToggleButtonElement. Parameters Name Type Description state bool? Click Declared in ElementExtensions. Overload Description Click(ButtonElement, Action?) Wires a click handler (sets ButtonElement.OnClick). Passing null clears any existing handler. Click(HyperlinkButtonElement, Action?) Wires a click handler (sets HyperlinkButtonElement.OnClick). Passing null clears. Click(RepeatButtonElement, Action?) Wires a click handler that fires repeatedly while held. Passing null clears. Click(SplitButtonElement, Action?) Wires the primary-button click handler. Passing null clears. Applies to: ButtonElement, HyperlinkButtonElement, RepeatButtonElement, SplitButtonElement. Parameters Name Type Description handler Action? Command Declared in ElementExtensions. Overload Description Command(ButtonElement, Command) Binds a Command to a custom-content ButtonElement by lifting it onto the typed ButtonElement.Command property (issues #133, #153, unified in #637). The reconciler invokes Execute/ExecuteAsync on click, folds the command's Command.IsEnabled into the IsEnabled descriptor entry (re-applied when the command's derived enabled state changes — field-aware, not on every render — and coexisting with .IsDisabledFocusable()'s coercion), and flows Description / Accelerator / AccessKey — all field-aware, with no per-render ButtonElement.Setters lambda. Pairs with Button(content) so icon-plus-label buttons auto-disable like the Button(Command) factory. The modifier makes the command fully take over: any ButtonElement.OnClick already on the element is cleared so the command — not a stale click handler — dispatches (issue #637; matches the pre-#637 modifier, and the Button(Command) factory which builds the element with no OnClick). A raw .Set(...) setter runs after the command metadata and therefore overrides it. Command(HyperlinkButtonElement, Command) Binds a Command to a HyperlinkButtonElement, clearing any existing OnClick so the command takes over dispatch. See Command. (issues #133, #637) Command(RepeatButtonElement, Command) Binds a Command to a RepeatButtonElement, clearing any existing OnClick so the command takes over dispatch. See Command. (issues #133, #637) Command(ToggleButtonElement, Command) Binds a Command to a ToggleButtonElement. The command fires on each toggle (check and uncheck), matching the ToggleButton(Command) factory; any existing toggle callback (OnIsCheckedChanged / OnCheckedStateChanged) is cleared so the command takes over dispatch. See Command. (issues #133, #637) Applies to: ButtonElement, HyperlinkButtonElement, RepeatButtonElement, ToggleButtonElement. Parameters Name Type Description command Command Delay Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: RepeatButtonElement. Parameters Name Type Description delay int DisabledFocusable Keeps the button keyboard-focusable while presenting it as disabled (visually dimmed, click suppressed). Use for submit buttons gated on validation: a true .IsEnabled(false) removes the button from tab order, which combined with commit-on-blur inputs like NumberBox/ DatePicker produces a focus trap where Tab skips a Submit that is *about* to become valid. Conceptually the Fluent UI React disabledFocusable / ARIA aria-disabled pattern; UIA still sees the button as enabled (a custom AutomationPeer override for full AT "unavailable" reporting is a tracked follow-up). Declared in ElementExtensions. Obsolete. Use IsDisabledFocusable() — aligns with WinUI naming (see #268). Applies to: ButtonElement. Parameters Name Type Default Description disabled bool true Interval Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: RepeatButtonElement. Parameters Name Type Description interval int IsDisabledFocusable Keeps the button keyboard-focusable while presenting it as disabled (visually dimmed, click suppressed). Use for submit buttons gated on validation: a true .IsEnabled(false) removes the button from tab order, which combined with commit-on-blur inputs like NumberBox/ DatePicker produces a focus trap where Tab skips a Submit that is *about* to become valid. Conceptually the Fluent UI React disabledFocusable / ARIA aria-disabled pattern; UIA still sees the button as enabled (a custom AutomationPeer override for full AT "unavailable" reporting is a tracked follow-up). Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: ButtonElement. Parameters Name Type Default Description disabled bool true IsThreeState Enable the three-state cycle. Pair with .CheckedState(...) and the .CheckedStateChanged(...) event fluent. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: ToggleButtonElement. Parameters Name Type Default Description isThreeState bool true NavigateUri Sets the navigation target for the hyperlink. Pairs naturally with the HyperlinkButton(Command) factory when a command-driven hyperlink also needs an external URI. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: HyperlinkButtonElement. Parameters Name Type Description uri Uri SubtleButton Applies the WinUI SubtleButtonStyle — chromeless transparent-background button look. Theme-aware. Applied at mount only — see ApplyStyle. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: ButtonElement, DropDownButtonElement, SplitButtonElement, ToggleSplitButtonElement. TextLink Applies the WinUI TextBlockButtonStyle — chromeless inline-link rendering. Use for the "Learn more" pattern inside body text. Theme-aware. Applied at mount only — see ApplyStyle. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: ButtonElement, HyperlinkButtonElement.

title: ElementExtensions

content: Cross-cutting "extras" bucket for Element (spec 047 §4.4). Holds the 14 rarely-set fields (attached properties, transitions, theme bindings, animation configs, resource overrides, context values) that used to sit inline on every element. Bucketing them into a lazy sub-record lets the common case (a leaf with none of these) pay one reference slot instead of 14. The fields are exposed on Element via get/init shim properties that read from / write into this record, so call sites see no API change. Value-equality (default record) so equality helpers and with-writers behave exactly as before. Unlike ElementModifiers nothing merges Extras, so there is no Merge. Construction-cost tradeoff (spec 047 §4.4 / §11.6): the common no-extras leaf now saves a reference slot (the §4.4 win), but each extra-setting fluent call (.Grid(), .Background(Theme…), .Animate(), .Provide(), …) clones this sub-record in addition to the Element clone — so an element that sets several extras does N small ElementExtras allocations during construction where the inline layout did zero. Net win for the common case; watch the §11.6 byte-gate M2/M3 (callback/modifier-heavy leaves) when it is measured on the baseline box, as those are the construction-cost-sensitive scenarios. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Learn more: Modifier System Remarks Spec 047 §4.4. Constructors ElementExtras Properties AnimationConfig Compositor property animation configuration (.Animate() modifier). When set, the reconciler creates ImplicitAnimationCollection entries on the element's Visual for Opacity/Scale/Rotation/Offset/CenterPoint. Attached Attached properties from parent containers (Grid.Row, Canvas.Left, etc.). Set via fluent extension methods: TextBlock("hi").Grid(row: 1, column: 2) Stored as a type-keyed dictionary so each provider defines its own data record. CallSite Spec 010 — the DSL call site that produced the owning element. Bucketed here rather than declared inline on Element so that an element nobody stamped pays nothing. An inline SourceLocation? widens EVERY element instance by 24 bytes in every build and every configuration — measured at +24.0 B/op on the M12 control-model bench with source mapping switched off — which is a permanent retail tax for a debug-only feature. Living in the §4.4 extras bucket makes the cost proportional to the number of stamped elements instead of the number of elements. It is NOT free, and the trade is worth stating precisely. As a nullable struct this field is stored inline, so it widens the bucket itself: measured at 152 B/instance with it and 24 B of that attributable to this field (an 8-byte path reference, a 4-byte line, the nullable flag, padded). Any element carrying a behavioral extra — Attached, ThemeBindings, animations, ResourceOverrides, ContextValues — pays that whether or not source mapping is on, and whether or not the consumer even has the generator. The M12 benchmark cannot see it, because M12 leaves are extras-free and allocate no bucket at all. Accepted because it is bounded and proportional to elements that already allocate this object, versus +24 B on EVERY element (measured) for the inline-on-the-record alternative. ElementExtrasAllocationTests pins both halves. Read through Element.CallSite, which is the public shim; the bucket is an implementation detail. Remarks Spec 047 §4.4 bucketing; spec 010 slot. ConnectedAnimationKey Connected animation key for cross-container transitions. When set, the reconciler automatically captures a visual snapshot on unmount (via ConnectedAnimationService.PrepareToAnimate) and starts the animation on mount if a prepared animation with the same key exists. Set via fluent extension method: Border(child).ConnectedAnimation("hero") ContextValues Context values provided to this element's subtree via .Provide(). The reconciler pushes these onto the context scope when entering this element's subtree and pops them when leaving. ElementTransition Element enter/exit transition configuration (.Transition() modifier). When set, the reconciler animates mount (enter) and unmount (exit) with compositor animations, deferring removal until exit animation completes. ImplicitTransitions Implicit transitions (opacity, scale, rotation, translation, background). Set via fluent extension methods: Rectangle().OpacityTransition() Applied by the reconciler after mount/update, so they are always present when property values are set via .Set() callbacks. InteractionStates Interaction states configuration (.InteractionStates() modifier). When set, the reconciler registers pointer event handlers that drive zero-reconcile visual state transitions (hover, pressed, focused). KeyframeAnimations Keyframe animation definitions (.Keyframes() modifier). Trigger-based: plays when the trigger value changes between renders. LayoutAnimation Composition-layer layout animation configuration. When set, the reconciler attaches implicit animations to the element's Visual so that layout-driven position (and optionally size) changes animate smoothly. Set via fluent extension methods: Border(child).LayoutAnimation() ResourceOverrides Per-control resource overrides (lightweight styling). When set, the reconciler injects these into FrameworkElement.Resources so that the control's VisualStateManager picks them up for hover/pressed/disabled states. Set via fluent extension: Button("Go").Resources(r => r.Set("ButtonBackground", "#0078D4")) ScrollAnimation Scroll-linked expression animation configuration (.ScrollLinked() modifier). Expression animations run on the compositor, driven by ScrollViewer position. StaggerConfig Stagger configuration for container children (.Stagger() modifier). When set, child animations (enter, layout, property) have incrementing DelayTime = childIndex * staggerDelay. ThemeBindings Theme-resource bindings for brush properties (Background, Foreground, BorderBrush). When set, the reconciler resolves from WinUI theme resources instead of using local values. Set via fluent extension methods: TextBlock("hi").Background(Theme.Accent) ThemeTransitions Theme transitions (children, item container). Set via fluent extension methods: VStack(children).WithTransitions(...)

Overload Description OnLongPress<T>(T, Action, TimeSpan?, double, bool) Zero-argument convenience overload for long-press. Use when you don't need the gesture snapshot (Position, Duration, Phase). Fires exactly ONCE per recognized long-press, at the moment it triggers (GesturePhase.Began) — not again on release (GesturePhase.Ended) or cancel. The underlying OnTriggered contract fires Began then Ended/Cancelled; a phase-agnostic convenience action must filter to Began or it double-fires. (This was previously masked when a per-render capturing action went stale across a skipped render — both calls became idempotent; the skip-path closure refresh in #721 exposed it, so the filter makes the single-fire contract explicit.) OnLongPress<T>(T, Action<LongPressGesture>, TimeSpan?, double, bool) Attaches a long-press gesture recognizer (spec 027 Tier 3 Part 2). Touch and pen route through UIElement.Holding (IsHoldingEnabled = true is auto-set). Mouse input is ignored by default — WinUI's Holding event does not raise for mouse pointers. Pass enableMouseEmulation true to arm a dispatcher timer on UIElement.PointerPressed that fires after minimumDuration and cancels on motion > cancelDistance, pointer release, or capture loss. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description onTriggered Action or Action<LongPressGesture> minimumDuration TimeSpan? null cancelDistance double 10 enableMouseEmulation bool false Example OnLostFocus Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description handler Action<object, RoutedEventArgs> OnPan Attaches a pan (single-finger translation) gesture recognizer. The reconciler wires UIElement.ManipulationDelta and computes UIElement.ManipulationMode based on the chosen axis and withInertia flag. minimumDistance gates callbacks until the cumulative translation exceeds that distance — on first crossing, onBegan fires once with GesturePhase.Began, then a GesturePhase.Changed follows. content: Modifiers are extension methods that return a changed copy of the element, so you can chain them. Learn more: Components, Context OnMount Runs an action once when the element is first mounted (not on re-renders). Use this instead of .Set() when attaching event handlers to avoid accumulation. Usage: Button("Go", null).OnMount(fe => { ((Button)fe).Click += ...; }) Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description action Action<FrameworkElement> OnMountAdd Like OnMount, but composes with any mount action already on the element instead of overwriting it. Useful for framework code that wants to apply defensive defaults (e.g. IsHitTestVisible = false) to a caller-supplied Element without silently dropping the caller's own mount-time wiring. The pre-existing action runs first, then the new one. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description action Action<FrameworkElement> OnSizeChanged Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description handler Action<object, SizeChangedEventArgs> OnUnmount Runs an action once when the element is unmounted (removed from the tree), receiving the native control. The teardown half of OnMount — the React useEffect cleanup / Compose DisposableEffect { onDispose } shape — for controls that need an imperative stop/dispose (e.g. stopping a camera preview, releasing a media session). Runs on genuine unmount, not on re-render/update. Disposing the host drops its tree without unmounting it, so this callback is not guaranteed to run then. Release anything that must not outlive the host from a UseEffect cleanup, which disposal does run. Usage: CameraPreview(...).OnMount(fe => Start(fe)).OnUnmount(fe => Stop(fe)) Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description action Action<FrameworkElement> OnUnmountAdd Like OnUnmount, but composes with any unmount action already on the element instead of overwriting it (pre-existing action runs first). Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description action Action<FrameworkElement> Provide Provides a context value to this element's subtree. Any descendant can consume it via UseContext(). Multiple .Provide() calls on the same element merge into a single dictionary. Providing the same context twice on the same element is last-write-wins. Declared in ContextExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description context Context<TValue> value TValue Ref Declared in ElementExtensions. Overload Description Ref<T>(T, ElementRef) Binds this element to an imperative ElementRef. Obtain the ref from ctx.UseElementFocus() (or construct one manually) and use FocusManager.Focus to imperatively focus the referenced element after mount. Ref<T, TElement>(T, ElementRef<TElement>) Strongly-typed overload of Ref. Accepts a typed ElementRef<T> and forwards to the untyped form via the implicit conversion. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description target ElementRef or ElementRef<TElement> Remarks Spec 033 §3. Behaviorally identical to passing the inner untyped ref; the typed overload exists so callers see the typed surface in IntelliSense and so the reconciler's DEBUG mismatch-assert can fire on a wrong-type binding. Example WithKey Declared in ElementExtensions. Overload Description WithKey<T>(T, string) Assigns a stable reconciliation key. Reuses the element when it already holds the same string reference; otherwise returns an immutable copy. WithKey<T, TKey>(T, TKey) Assigns the stable identity from an IReactorKeyed data item directly to a hand-built element — equivalent to el.WithKey(item.Key) but lets call sites avoid hoisting the item to read .Key. (spec 042 §5) Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description key string item TKey Remarks Typical use: FlexColumn(items.Select(item => TextBlock(item.Name).WithKey(item))). The TKey parameter is independent of the element type so the usual fluent inference (return the element type) is preserved.

WithNavigation<TRoute>(NavigationViewElement, NavigationHandle<TRoute>, Func<TRoute, string?>, Func<string, TRoute>, Func<TRoute>?) Auto-syncs this NavigationView with a NavigationHandle: sets SelectedTag from the current route, navigates on selection change, wires OnBackRequested to GoBack, and IsBackEnabled to CanGoBack. NavigationView's recommended transition is forwarded to the navigation host, so pane navigation uses WinUI's entrance motion and top navigation slides horizontally according to the selected item's position. Selection is wired through an internal transition-aware callback rather than the public NavigationViewElement.OnSelectedTagChanged, which this deliberately leaves null: setting that property yourself afterwards then takes precedence and suppresses the auto-navigation, so an author can observe selection without this fighting them. The same applies to NavigationViewElement.OnSettingsSelected. The built-in settings item is opt-in: pass settingsRoute to make selecting it navigate. It is a separate parameter rather than a NavigationViewElement.SettingsTag lookup through tagToRoute because that delegate must return a route for every string it is handed — callers typically throw on an unrecognized tag — so there is no way for it to decline. Left null, settings selection does not navigate. To show the settings item as selected while its route is current, return NavigationViewElement.SettingsTag from routeToTag. Return null for routes without a corresponding menu item, or NavigationViewElement.SettingsTag for the built-in settings item. tagToRoute Func<string, TRoute> Maps a NavigationViewItem tag back to a route for OnSelectedTagChanged. Never called with NavigationViewElement.SettingsTag — that value is reserved and routed via settingsRoute instead, so an ordinary item must not carry it or it will select without navigating. settingsRoute Func<TRoute>? null Route to navigate to when the built-in settings item is selected. Null (the default) leaves settings selection unrouted. WrapMode Whether the selected index wraps around the ends. Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: PipsPagerElement. TransformOrigin Sets the pivot for .Scale() and .Rotation() as a fraction of the element's laid-out size: (0.5f, 0.5f) is the centre, (0, 0) the leading top corner. The pivot follows resizes and size animations, and x is flow-relative, so 0 is the right edge in a right-to-left layout. A .CenterPoint() on the same element is added as a pixel offset. Without this modifier the pivot is the .CenterPoint() value, or the leading top corner. Grow from the centre on hover: Border(card).TransformOrigin(0.5f, 0.5f).InteractionStates(s => s.PointerOver(scale: 1.05f)) Declared in ElementExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description x float y float Remarks Spec 066 §8. The pivot is an expression on the element's composition visual, so the modifier takes the visual (like the other transform modifiers). While .LayoutAnimation() animates the size, the pivot follows the animating size, not the final layout size.

Overload Description Validate<T>(T, string, IValidator[]) Attaches validators to this element. The element's value will be validated against the provided validators, with results pushed to the nearest ValidationContext. Validate<T>(T, string, object?, IValidator[]) Attaches validators to this element along with the current field value, and — when called from inside a component's Render() — runs them immediately against the enclosing ValidationContext. Running during render rather than during reconcile is what makes the results readable by the same Render() that produced them, so When(ctx.IsTouched(f) && ctx.HasError(f), …) placed after this call sees the current verdict instead of the previous pass's. The validators are still attached, so FormField keeps working for elements built outside a render pass. Re-running them is harmless: results are applied with a structural diff. The visualizers only *display* what a context already holds — they never run attached validators — so an element that reaches neither a render pass nor a FormField contributes no verdict. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description fieldName string Field name for validation messages. validators IValidator[] One or more validators to apply. value object? ValidateAsync Declared in ValidateExtensions. Overload Description ValidateAsync<T>(T, string, IAsyncValidator[]) Attaches async validators to this element (in addition to any sync validators). ValidateAsync<T>(T, string, object?, IAsyncValidator[]) Attaches async validators to this element along with the current field value, and registers the field so MarkAllTouched() covers it. This overload is attach-only: it does not run the validators. Nothing consumes ValidationAttached.AsyncValidators automatically — not the render scope, which must stay synchronous, and not FormField. Run them yourself from an effect via ValidationReconciler.ValidateFieldAsync, which carries the generation guard that discards a result superseded by a newer value. Registration happens here for an element built during a render, and again when FormField mounts or updates it, which is the only chance an element assembled outside a render pass gets. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Description fieldName string asyncValidators IAsyncValidator[] value object? WithErrorStyling Applies error styling to an element based on ValidationContext state. Returns the element with appropriate border styling applied. Declared in ErrorStylingExtensions. Applies to: any element. Parameters Name Type Default Description ctx ValidationContext fieldName string showWhen ShowWhen ShowWhen.WhenTouched submitAttempted bool false

content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Navigation. Learn more: Navigation Remarks Thread safety (issue #234). The mutating methods (NavigationHandle.Navigate, NavigationHandle.GoBack, NavigationHandle.GoForward, NavigationHandle.Replace, NavigationHandle.Reset, NavigationHandle.PopTo, NavigationHandle.SetState) are thread-safe by default. When called from the UI thread the cost is a single thread-id compare. When called off-thread (e.g. from Task.Run or after await … ConfigureAwait(false)) the whole mutation — stack edit, NavigationHandle.Navigated/RouteChanged events, and the component re-render — is auto-marshaled onto the captured UI dispatcher, mirroring the UseState/UseReducer contract from issue #212. An off-thread call throws InvalidOperationException loudly — rather than corrupting the back/forward stacks — in two cases: when no UI dispatcher is available (unit-test / headless contexts), and when the captured dispatcher refuses the enqueue (its TryEnqueue returns false, e.g. once it has begun shutting down near window close). The bool-returning mutators return true when an off-thread call is accepted and scheduled; the actual guard/empty-stack outcome is then resolved on the UI thread. Off-thread callers must therefore not treat that true as confirmation that the navigation actually happened — only that it was scheduled. (On the UI thread the bool keeps its original meaning: whether the navigation succeeded.) Properties BackStack Readonly view of the back stack. CanGoBack True if there are entries in the back stack. CanGoForward True if there are entries in the forward stack. CurrentRoute The currently active route. Depth Total depth: back stack count + 1 (current). ForwardStack Readonly view of the forward stack. Methods GetState Returns a snapshot of the full navigation state — back stack, current route, and forward stack — as a plain POCO. Persist it however you like (JSON, MessagePack, hand-rolled binary): Reactor intentionally does not pick a serialization format for you. Remarks For JSON persistence, declare a JsonSerializerContext covering NavigationState<TRoute> and your route type so the call is AOT-safe. For polymorphic route hierarchies, annotate the base route type with [JsonPolymorphic] and [JsonDerivedType]. GoBack Go back to the previous route. Returns: On the UI thread, true if navigation succeeded, or false if the back stack is empty or a guard cancelled it. When called off the UI thread, true means the call was marshaled and scheduled onto the UI dispatcher — not that it succeeded; the empty-stack/guard outcome is resolved later on the UI thread (see the type-level thread-safety remarks). GoForward Go forward to the next route in the forward stack. Returns: On the UI thread, true if navigation succeeded, or false if the forward stack is empty or a guard cancelled it. When called off the UI thread, true means the call was marshaled and scheduled onto the UI dispatcher — not that it succeeded; the empty-stack/guard outcome is resolved later on the UI thread (see the type-level thread-safety remarks). Navigate Navigate to a new route. By default pushes the current route onto the back stack. If NavigateOptions.PushToBackStack is false, replaces the current route instead. Parameters Name Type Default Description route TRoute options NavigateOptions? null Returns: On the UI thread, true if the navigation succeeded, or false if a guard cancelled it. When called off the UI thread, true means the call was marshaled and scheduled onto the UI dispatcher — not that it succeeded; the real outcome is resolved later on the UI thread (see the type-level thread-safety remarks). PopTo Pop entries from the back stack until the predicate matches. Parameters Name Type Description predicate Func<TRoute, bool> Returns: On the UI thread, true if a matching entry was popped to, or false if no back-stack entry matches the predicate or a guard cancelled it. When called off the UI thread, true means the call was marshaled and scheduled onto the UI dispatcher — not that it succeeded; the real outcome is resolved later on the UI thread (see the type-level thread-safety remarks). Replace Replace the current route without modifying back/forward stacks. Parameters Name Type Description route TRoute Returns: On the UI thread, true if the route was replaced, or false if a guard cancelled it. When called off the UI thread, true means the call was marshaled and scheduled onto the UI dispatcher — not that it succeeded; the real outcome is resolved later on the UI thread (see the type-level thread-safety remarks). Reset Reset the entire stack to a single root route. Clears back and forward stacks. Parameters Name Type Description route TRoute Returns: On the UI thread, true if the stack was reset, or false if a guard cancelled it. When called off the UI thread, true means the call was marshaled and scheduled onto the UI dispatcher — not that it succeeded; the real outcome is resolved later on the UI thread (see the type-level thread-safety remarks). SetState Restores a previously captured NavigationState<TRoute>. Replaces the back stack, current route, and forward stack, then fires NavigationHandle.Navigated with NavigationMode.Reset. content: Color and brush parsing utilities. Supports named colors, hex (#RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB), and direct Color values. Parsed colors are cached by string (an immutable value type, safe to share), but a fresh SolidColorBrush is created per call: a brush is a DependencyObject with thread affinity and mutable Color/Opacity, so a single instance cannot be safely shared across controls. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor. Learn more: Styling and Theming Methods Parse Parses a color string into a fresh SolidColorBrush owned by the caller. Supports named colors (red, green, blue, white, black, gray, lightgray, transparent) and hex codes (#RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB). The parsed color is cached, but a new brush instance is returned on every call, so callers may safely mutate it and a brush is never shared between controls. Any other string silently yields a gray brush; the REACTOR_DYM_006 analyzer flags constant strings that do. Parameters Name Type Description color string

Learn more: Theming Tokens Properties Accent AccentDisabled AccentSecondary AccentTertiary AccentText CardBackground CardStroke ControlFill ControlFillDisabled ControlFillInputActive ControlFillSecondary ControlFillTertiary ControlStroke ControlStrokeSecondary DisabledText DividerStroke LayerFill PrimaryText SecondaryText SmokeFill SolidBackground SubtleFill SurfaceStroke SystemAttention SystemAttentionBackground SystemCaution SystemCautionBackground SystemCritical SystemCriticalBackground SystemNeutral SystemNeutralBackground SystemSolidAttention SystemSolidNeutral SystemSuccess SystemSuccessBackground TertiaryText Methods NotifyResourcesChanged Tells Reactor that application resources were edited at runtime, so theme references resolve again and every live host re-renders with the new values. Remarks Call it after changing Application.Current.Resources in a way that is not a theme change — replacing a brush in a ThemeDictionaries entry, merging or removing a brand dictionary, or an inspector's live resource edit. Reactor caches each resolved (resource key, theme) brush and only drops that cache when the effective theme or the system palette changes, so without this call such an edit is not seen. Not needed for a Light/Dark/high-contrast switch (RequestedTheme) or for mutating an existing brush's Color; both are already picked up. What it does: clears the resolution cache behind ThemeRef, then asks every live ReactorHost and ReactorHostControl for a full re-render that bypasses component memoization and the reconciler's skip of unchanged elements, so memoized and reused subtrees are refreshed too. That re-resolves .Resources(...) theme overrides, re-applies ThemeRef modifiers such as .Background(Theme.Accent), and re-runs any ThemeRef.Resolve call in a Render method. Callable from any thread; the re-renders are scheduled on each host's UI thread. Await a host's WaitForIdleAsync() to observe the result. On a host's UI thread, a host that has no content yet re-renders inline, and its render can throw. Every other host is still notified; then the exception is rethrown (an AggregateException when several hosts threw). Ref Reference any WinUI theme resource by key name. The resource must exist in the WinUI resource tree (e.g., defined in XamlControlsResources or added via app resources). Parameters Name Type Description resourceKey string

content: A reference to a WinUI theme resource that resolves at render time. Use via Theme tokens or Theme.Ref for custom keys. Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Core. Learn more: Theming Tokens Constructors ThemeRef A reference to a WinUI theme resource that resolves at render time. Use via Theme tokens or Theme.Ref for custom keys. Parameters Name Type Description ResourceKey string Properties ResourceKey Methods Resolve Resolves a theme resource using an explicit isDark flag. Useful for resolving during Render() before controls are in the tree. Parameters Name Type Description resourceKey string isDark bool Remarks The brush is the one a {ThemeResource} reference gets on an element in that theme, so either theme can be resolved whatever theme the app uses. WinUI does the lookup, so its rules apply, including the Default fallback. For a key WinUI cannot resolve for that theme (one an app dictionary defines only for some themes), Reactor reads the app's Light, Dark and Default theme dictionaries, then does a plain lookup, which uses the app's theme: a key defined only for the app's theme therefore resolves to that brush for the other theme too, and a key defined only for the other theme resolves to null for the app's theme. Returns null when the key is not found or is not a Brush. Call it on the UI thread.

content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Controls.Validation. Learn more: Forms and Input Constructors ValidationContext Properties InvalidFields Returns the names of all fields that have at least one Error-severity message. RegisteredFields Returns all registered field names. SubmitAttempted Whether ValidationContext.MarkAllTouched has been called since the last reset — the context's record of a submit attempt, read by ShowWhen.AfterFirstSubmit. Version Monotonically increasing version number, bumped on every mutation. Useful for change detection in hooks/memos. Methods Add Add(ValidationMessage) Adds a validation message. Parameters Name Type Description message ValidationMessage Add(string, string, Severity) Adds a validation message for the specified field. Parameters Name Type Default Description field string text string severity Severity Severity.Error AddExternal AddExternal(ValidationMessage) Adds an externally-sourced validation message. Parameters Name Type Description message ValidationMessage AddExternal(string, string, Severity) Adds an externally-sourced validation message (e.g., server-side error). External messages persist until explicitly cleared or the field value changes. Parameters Name Type Default Description field string text string severity Severity Severity.Error Clear Clears all validation messages (both internal and external) for the specified field. Parameters Name Type Description field string ClearAll Clears all messages (internal and external) for all fields. ClearExternal Clears only external messages for the specified field. Parameters Name Type Description field string GetAllMessages Returns all messages (internal + external) across all fields. GetMessages Returns all messages (internal + external) for the specified field. Parameters Name Type Description field string HasError Returns true if the specified field has any Error-severity messages. Parameters Name Type Description field string HasMessages Returns true if the specified field has any messages of any severity. Parameters Name Type Description field string HighestSeverity Returns the highest severity among all messages for the specified field, or null if none. Parameters Name Type Description field string IsDirty IsDirty() Returns true if any registered field is dirty. IsDirty(string) Returns true if the field's current value differs from its initial value. Parameters Name Type Description field string IsTouched Returns true if the field has been focused and then blurred. Parameters Name Type Description field string IsValid Returns true when there are no Error-severity messages across all fields. MarkAllTouched Marks all registered fields as touched. Typically called on form submit. Also records that a submit was attempted, which is what ShowWhen.AfterFirstSubmit waits for. The framework has no other notion of "submit": this is the call the guide tells you to make on a submit attempt, so tying the two together is what makes that policy reachable on a FormField at all — before this it could never show an error, behaving identically to ShowWhen.Never (issue #1262). MarkTouched Marks a field as touched (e.g., after focus+blur). Parameters Name Type Description field string NotifyValueChanged Notifies the context of a field value change. Clears external messages for the field, because a server-side verdict about the old value says nothing about the new one. The clear is conditional on the value actually having moved. It used to be unconditional, which was survivable only while validation ran rarely: now that validators run on every render, an unconditional clear here would destroy any ValidationContext.AddExternal message on the very next repaint, before the user could read it. An async verdict is retired for the same reason, mirroring ValidationContext.ApplyValidation. A field validated only through .ValidateAsync(...) never reaches that method, so without this an error computed for a value the user has already replaced would stay on screen, and a pass opened against the old value could still install its result afterwards. Parameters Name Type Description field string value object? RegisterField Registers a field with the context. Called automatically by .Validate() or manually for fields that need dirty/touched tracking. Parameters Name Type Description field string Reset Resets a field to its initial value, clears touched state and all messages. Returns the initial value so the caller can update the UI. Parameters Name Type Description field string ResetAll Resets all fields to their initial values, clears all touched states and messages. Returns a dictionary of field → initial value. SetInitialValue Stores the initial value for a field. Called at field registration time. The current value is seeded only the first time the field is seen. Re-seeding it on every call would rewind whatever the user has since typed — harmless while nothing watched the context, but with change notification it becomes a permanent repaint loop for the common SetInitialValue(...) + NotifyValueChanged(...) pair that components run on each render: the rewind and the re-notify would take turns forever. Use ValidationContext.Reset to deliberately return a field to its baseline. Parameters Name Type Description field string value object? Events Changed Raised after any mutation that actually changed observable state — a message appearing or disappearing, a field becoming touched, a reset. UseValidationContext() subscribes to this so that mutating the context from an event handler (the canonical case being ValidationContext.MarkAllTouched on a submit attempt) repaints the form. Without it, an invalid submit changes nothing the user can see. Two rules keep this from driving a render loop. First, re-running the same validators over an unchanged value is silent: results are applied with a structural diff, so an idempotent re-validation raises nothing. Second, mutations made while a render is in flight are not announced inline — the rendering component reads the new state later in the same pass, and notifying there would re-enter the reconciler's re-render path from inside Render(). They are held and delivered once the pass finishes, so other subscribers — a parent rendering IsValid(), say — still hear about them; a pass that ends with the state it started with is dropped rather than delivered, since there is nothing to announce.

content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Controls.Validation. Learn more: Forms and Input Methods EvaluateRules EvaluateRules(ValidationContext, ValidationRuleElement[]) Evaluates ValidationRuleElements and pushes their results to the context. Each rule owns its own slot, identified by its field and the call site of its predicate, so re-running the same rules replaces each verdict rather than accumulating. Rules evaluated here are independent of each other and of any other caller using the same context. Callers are independent of one another as long as their predicates differ, which they do for the ordinary lambda case — each call site compiles to its own method. Two callers that pass the same *named method* as the predicate, for the same field and position, share a slot; give those a setId instead. This overload does not withdraw a rule that disappears from the list — nothing re-evaluates a rule that no longer exists. Use the ValidationReconciler.EvaluateRules overload when a set shrinks or empties, or mount the rules in the element tree, where unmount retracts them. Parameters Name Type Description ctx ValidationContext rules ValidationRuleElement[] EvaluateRules(ValidationContext, string, ValidationRuleElement[]) Evaluates a named rule set: the call owns that set for the context, so a producer from the previous call under the same setId that is absent this time has its contribution withdrawn. The identity is explicit because ownership is destructive. Two unrelated callers sharing one context must not silently retract each other's rules, which is what an implicit per-context set would do. Each rule is keyed by its position within the set, so two rules stay independent even if they carry the same message, and re-running the set replaces each verdict rather than accumulating. Parameters Name Type Description ctx ValidationContext setId string rules ValidationRuleElement[] EvaluateRulesAsync EvaluateRulesAsync(ValidationContext, ValidationRuleElement[]) The asynchronous counterpart to ValidationReconciler.EvaluateRules, for rules built by ValidationRuleAsync. Synchronous rules are evaluated normally. Rules run in order rather than concurrently, so the resulting message order for a field is the order the rules were given in — GetMessages exposes that order and callers read the first message. Each rule is ordered against itself by its own async generation, so two overlapping evaluations of the same rule cannot install out of order. Rules remain independent of each other. No lock is held across a caller's predicate. Parameters Name Type Description ctx ValidationContext rules ValidationRuleElement[] EvaluateRulesAsync(ValidationContext, string, ValidationRuleElement[]) The asynchronous counterpart to ValidationReconciler.EvaluateRules. Every verdict is computed before any is installed, and nothing is installed if the set has been re-evaluated in the meantime, or if a field's value changed while a predicate was running — each rule opens a per-producer async generation before its predicate runs, and those are verified at the moment of application. Parameters Name Type Description ctx ValidationContext setId string rules ValidationRuleElement[] EvaluateRulesAsync(ValidationContext, CancellationToken, ValidationRuleElement[]) As ValidationReconciler.EvaluateRulesAsync, with cancellation. A rule predicate takes no token of its own, so this is the only way to stop waiting on one that never completes — and with it, to release the evaluation's hold on the context. Parameters Name Type Description ctx ValidationContext cancellationToken CancellationToken rules ValidationRuleElement[] EvaluateRulesAsync(ValidationContext, string, CancellationToken, ValidationRuleElement[]) As ValidationReconciler.EvaluateRulesAsync, with cancellation. A cancelled call installs nothing: the verdicts are computed before any of them is committed, so there is no partial set to unwind. Parameters Name Type Description ctx ValidationContext setId string cancellationToken CancellationToken rules ValidationRuleElement[] ValidateAttached Runs validators from a ValidationAttached record and pushes results to the context. Parameters Name Type Description ctx ValidationContext attached ValidationAttached value object? ValidateField Runs all synchronous validators for a field and pushes results to the context. Call this from a component's Render() method after state is finalized. Results are applied as a single diffed replacement, so calling this repeatedly with an unchanged value is a no-op: no version bump, no change notification, no re-render. That is what lets .Validate() run on every render pass. Parameters Name Type Description ctx ValidationContext fieldName string value object? validators IValidator[] ValidateFieldAsync Runs all async validators for a field. Typically called from a UseEffect hook. Parameters Name Type Default Description ctx ValidationContext fieldName string value object? asyncValidators IAsyncValidator[] cancellationToken CancellationToken default

content: Namespace: Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Controls.Validation. Learn more: Forms and Input Methods Evaluate Evaluates the validation rule against a ValidationContext. Adds or clears messages based on the predicate result. The result is applied as one diffed replacement rather than clear-then-add. Mount/UpdateValidationRule calls this during reconcile — after the component's render scope has closed — so with clear-then-add a failing rule raised ValidationContext.Changed on every pass, each notification drove another render, and the reconciler tripped its re-render re-entrancy limit. Re-evaluating to the same verdict is now silent. Parameters Name Type Description ctx ValidationContext EvaluateAsync Evaluates the async validation rule against a ValidationContext. The previous verdict is kept while the check is in flight and replaced once, at the end. Clearing first would raise ValidationContext.Changed twice per evaluation for an already-failing rule, and would briefly report the field as valid in between. Overlapping evaluations are ordered by a generation token taken before the predicate is awaited. Without it, a slow failing check started first could resolve after a fast passing one and reinstate an error the newer run had already cleared. Parameters Name Type Default Description ctx ValidationContext cancellationToken CancellationToken default Factories ValidationRule ValidationRuleAsync
